title: The John Thorburn case

CONFIDENTIAL
DRAWER

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. & S. B. REGISTRY
S. B. D. 2404
5 3 32

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Friday, March 4, 1932

Thorburn Award Commission
Makes Known Its Findings

Payment of $5,000, the full amount of the reward offered by The Shanghai Evening Post and Mercury for information other than circumstantial as to the whereabouts of Mr. John H. Thorburn, 18-year-old British subject who disappeared last spring from his home in Shanghai, has been made to Mr. W. A. Betting, on decision of the Award Commission of three.
Mr. Betting, formerly proprietor of a private detective agency in Shanghai, spent more than three months in working on the case, and presented his findings to The Shanghai Evening Post and Mercury a short time before the Chinese National Government's second Commission of Inquiry made public its discovery that Mr. Thorburn had been shot and killed by Col. Huang, commander of the First Kiangsu Regiment of Gendarmerie, at Soochow.
The Chinese government cashiered the officer, placed him on trial, and he received a sentence of 11 years in jail which is now being served. The apologies of the Chinese National Government were tendered to and accepted by the British Government.
The award commission which reviewed all claims for participation in the reward offer was composed of Mr. H. Lipson Wert, prominent Shanghai attorney; Mr. C. Calder Marshall, of the British Chamber of Commerce, and Mr. G. H. French, of the American Chamber of Commerce.
Although these gentlemen served in an honorary capacity, they gave unstintingly of their time and care in sorting claims and hearing evidence, and The Shanghai Evening Post and Mercury wishes to take this opportunity to thank them for their assistance for rendering so valuable a public service.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1932年3月4日，星期五

索恩伯恩奖金委员会
公布其调查结果

根据由三人组成的奖金委员会的决定，已向W. A. Betting先生支付了5,000美元，此为《上海晚邮报与水星报》为征集关于去年春季从上海家中失踪的18岁英国籍男子约翰·H·索恩伯恩（John H. Thorburn）下落之非间接证据线索所设立的全额赏金。
Betting先生曾是上海一家私人侦探社的经营者，他在该案上花费了三个多月的时间，并在中国国民政府第二调查委员会公开披露其发现——即索恩伯恩先生在苏州被宪兵第一江苏团团长黄上校枪杀——前不久，将其调查结果提交给《上海晚邮报与水星报》。
中国政府将该军官革职，并对其提起诉讼，他被判处11年监禁，目前正在服刑。中国国民政府已向英国政府致歉，并为英方所接受。
负责审查所有奖金申领要求的奖金委员会由上海著名律师H. Lipson Wert先生、英国商会代表C. Calder Marshall先生以及美国商会代表G. H. French先生组成。
尽管这些先生是以荣誉身份任职，但他们在梳理申领材料和听取证据方面不吝惜时间与精力，《上海晚邮报与水星报》谨借此机会感谢他们提供了如此宝贵的公共服务。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, TUESDAY, DECEMBER 15, 1931
THE CASE OF MR. JOHN THORBURN
Full Story of Murder Told in Documents Submitted to the Commons

FROM OUR OWN CORRESPONDENT

London, Nov. 24.
The following questions and answers in the House of Commons during the week ended November 24 now appear in Hansard. It will be noticed that in reply to a question by Sir B. Falle the Government circulated the full text of the Chinese report on the death of Mr. John Thorburn, which throws a rather different light upon the matter than was given by the telegraphic summary which was issued early in November.

Sir Charles Cayzer asked the Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs whether any claim for compensation from Mr. John Thorburn's relatives has now been received and considered; and what steps he proposes to take to press this claim against the Chinese Government?

Mr. Eden: Mr. Thorburn's father has now requested that His Majesty's Minister should lodge a claim for compensation with the Chinese Government. My right hon. Friend is not yet in receipt of full details, but the request is being considered as urgently as possible.

Sir B. Falle asked the Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs if he will furnish this House with the text of the final reply of the Chinese Government to the representations of His Majesty's Government in the matter of the death of Mr. John Thorburn; and if he will press for an identification of the burial place of the remains of Mr. Thorburn?

Mr. Eden: The text of the reply of the Chinese Government and a summary of the report attached to it, which had been received by telegraph from His Majesty's Minister in China, were published in the Press on November 4. I will circulate in the Official Report the text of the note and the complete report which has now been received. I am in communication with His Majesty's Minister in regard to the matter referred to in the second part of the question.

Hansard then includes the Note from the Chinese Acting Minister for Foreign Affairs, which has already been published in full in these columns, and also the full report of the Chinese investigation, of which only a telegraphic summary was made available at the time of the publication of the Note. The full translation is as follows:—

The Joint Military Court held to inquire into the disappearance of Thorburn, having completed the investigation, its Findings and Judgment are respectfully set out as follows:

The Arrest
(1) At about ten o'clock in the night of June 1, 1931, Sub-Lieutenant P'eng Heng of the Gendarmerie stationed at Quinsan was ordered to lead his men out on patrol along the Shanghai-Nanking Railway line. He sent on ahead as patrols the three Gendarmes Li Kuo-ts'ai, Shen Li-sheng and Wu I-sen. When they had proceeded to the neighbourhood of Cheng I Railway Station, they saw a suspicious looking person walking hurriedly along the railway track. They challenged him and called on him to halt. He paid no attention.

They advanced to investigate and discovered him to be a foreigner. They then interrogated him. The foreigner however made no reply but fired his pistol and shot and wounded the two Gendarmes Li Kuo-ts'ai and Shen Li-sheng. They fell, but Wu I-sen whilst the soldiers behind were coming up courageously advanced and seized him. At this moment the express train from Shanghai to Nanking came by. The soldiers stepped aside and the foreigner wrenched himself loose and escaped.

He dropped a bag containing a pistol and a clip of cartridges, a knife and a cartridge-belt containing nineteen cartridges, a small bottle of chloroform and a gauze face mask, a long black kerchief, one white shirt and a bunch of keys. When this was reported to the Company Headquarters of the Gendarmerie reinforcements, were sent out who continued the search and pursuit until dawn of June 2, when Wu I-sen recognised and arrested the foreigner near the eastern end of the Cheng I Railway station buildings. Twenty dollars in Chinese notes were found on him. These, together with the articles found previously, were sent to the Company Headquarters of the Gendarmerie at Quinsan, where the prisoner was questioned. His photograph was taken and in the afternoon of the same day he was conveyed to the Regimental Headquarters at Soochow to be dealt with.

Held by Military
(2) After the said foreigner had been sent to the Regimental Headquarters at Soochow, Colonel Huang Chen-wu himself subjected him to further examination. The foreigner's behaviour was extremely insolent. When asked whether his name was "Sea-scout Troop" he replied, "Yes." Asked his nationality, he replied: "I live at Shanghai. Send me to Shanghai and you will then find out." Asked for his passport, he replied, "None." When shown the bag and its contents and asked whether they were his, he replied "Yes." When asked why he had shot the Gendarmes, he defiantly refused to reply. Because of the report from the Company Headquarters that a brigand had been arrested and because the foreigner had no passport, had carried two pistols, chloroform and a gauze face mask, etcetera, and because he had bought no railway ticket although he had twenty dollars in notes, and because he had been walking hurriedly on the railway track, the Colonel concluded that the man must be a foreign communist desperado. He consequently intended to send him to the Law Courts for trial. But as the wounded Gendarmes Li Kuo-ts'ai and Shen Li-sheng had already been sent to hospital at Shanghai for treatment, Colonel Huang decided to wait until they had somewhat recovered so that he could ascertain clearly the circumstances in which the foreigner had shot them before sending him on for trial. He therefore had the foreigner detained in the Barracks.

Shot by Colonel
Li Kuo-ts'ai died on June 7, and it was reported that there was no hope for Shen Li-sheng (who died later on June 12). Colonel Huang then decided to send the foreigner to trial. He accordingly summoned the foreigner in the morning of June 8 for a further interrogation. The foreigner, however, still refused to state directly who he was. All he would say was that he lived at Shanghai. After much cross-questioning he at last fully confessed that he had shot the Gendarmes. Asked where the revolver was with which he had shot and wounded the Gendarmes, he replied that he had thrown it into the water. After having questioned him thus far, the Colonel, unable to control his indignation, reviled the foreigner and cursed him as an outlaw. Hearing these words, the foreigner suddenly sprang at the Colonel, whom he took by surprise and struck him fiercely. The Colonel, in the face of the fierce aspect and savage strength of the foreigner, drew his pistol and shot him dead.

(3) After he had killed the foreigner Colonel Huang Chen-wu realised that he had exceeded what was justifiable in self-defence, and being afraid of incurring punishment, he caused to be destroyed all traces of the evidence, including the corpse, and gave strict orders to all his men not to divulge a word of what had passed, in the hope of covering up the matter. Thus it came about that the first investigation failed to reveal what had actually happened.

Identification Complete
(4) The facts above set out were subsequently elicited by inquiries pursued at the various Company and Regimental Headquarters of the Gendarmerie. Clues were obtained through strict examination of Sub-Lieutenant P'eng Heng and others. Repeated cross-questioning of Sergeant Liu Chang-wen and others at last resulted in eliciting the facts of the case and in the identification beyond doubt of the foreigner in question as the man Thorburn who had disappeared. Colonel Huang Chen-wu was thereupon cashiered and sent to trial. This Ministry constituted a Joint Military Court before which the accused Huang Chen-wu at first denied his guilt, relying on the destruction of the evidence. But when he was later confronted by the evidence collected he made a full confession of the above facts. As regards the point concerning the identification of the foreigner in question as Thorburn, Colonel Huang was shown the photograph of Thorburn communicated by the British authorities when they were pressing for an investigation, and said it was indeed the man whom he had shot and killed. The facts of the case having been clearly ascertained, judgment was passed.

(5) The findings of the Joint Military Court were to the effect that the said Colonel Huang Chen-wu was according to law to be punished for his crime by being sentenced to a term of fourteen years' imprisonment. It is on record that he has already commenced to serve the sentence of imprisonment.

Seal of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

（印：MUNICIPAL POLICE REGISTRY S. B. D. 2464/N. 16. 12. 31.）

Commissioner of Police,
Sir,

《字林西报》，1931年12月15日，星期二
约翰·索恩伯恩先生案
提交下议院的文件详述谋杀案全貌

本报特约记者

伦敦，11月24日。
截至11月24日的一周内，下议院出现的以下问答现刊登于《汉萨德议会辩论记录》。值得注意的是，在答复B·法尔爵士（Sir B. Falle）的提问时，政府 circulated 了关于约翰·索恩伯恩先生死亡事件的中方报告全文，该报告所揭示的情况与11月初发布的电报摘要大相径庭。

查尔斯·凯泽爵士（Sir Charles Cayzer）询问外交大臣，目前是否已收到并审议了约翰·索恩伯恩先生亲属提出的任何赔偿要求；以及他打算采取何种步骤向中国政府施压以落实这一索赔？

艾登先生（Mr. Eden）：索恩伯恩先生的父亲现已请求英王陛下驻华公使向中国政府提出赔偿要求。我的尊贵同僚尚未收到全部细节，但正在尽可能紧急地审议此项请求。

B·法尔爵士询问外交大臣，他能否向本议院提供中国政府就英王陛下政府关于约翰·索恩伯恩先生死亡一事所作交涉的最终复文文本；以及他是否会敦促确认索恩伯恩先生遗体的埋葬地点？

艾登先生：中国政府的复文文本及其附带报告的摘要已于11月4日见报，这些文件是经由英王陛下驻华公使通过电报收到的。我将把现已收到的照会文本和完整报告在《官方记录》中分发。关于问题第二部分所提及的事项，我正与英王陛下驻华公使进行沟通。

《汉萨德议会辩论记录》随后收录了中国代理外交部长的照会，该照会此前已在本报专栏全文刊登，同时也收录了中国方面调查的完整报告，而在照会发布时仅提供了该报告的电报摘要。完整译文如下：—

为调查索恩伯恩失踪案而设立的军事法庭，已完成调查，谨将其裁决与判决陈述如下：

逮捕经过
(1) 1931年6月1日晚十时许，驻昆山的宪兵排长彭恒奉命率领部下沿沪宁铁路线巡逻。他派遣李国才、沈立生和吴一森三名宪兵作为前哨先行巡逻。当他们行进至真义火车站附近时，发现一名形迹可疑之人正沿着铁轨匆忙行走。他们对其喝问并命令其站住。此人未予理睬。

他们上前盘查，发现是一名外国人。随即对其进行讯问。然而该外国人不予回答，反而拔出手枪射击，击伤了两名宪兵李国才和沈立生。二人倒地，此时后方士兵赶到，吴一森勇敢上前将其抓获。恰在此时，由上海开往南京的特快列车驶过。士兵们避让到一旁，该外国人趁机挣脱逃脱。

他遗落了一个包，内有一支手枪和一夹子弹、一把刀、一条装有十九发子弹的子弹带、一小瓶氯仿和一块纱布面罩、一条黑色长头巾、一件白衬衫以及一串钥匙。此事上报至宪兵连部后，派出增援部队继续搜索追捕，直至6月2日黎明，吴一森在真义火车站站房东端附近认出并逮捕了该外国人。身上搜出中国纸币二十元。这些物品连同此前发现的物证一并送往昆山宪兵连部，并对囚犯进行了讯问。拍摄了其照片，并于当日下午将其押送至苏州团部处理。

由军方羁押
(2) 该外国人被送往苏州团部后，黄震吾上校亲自对其进行了进一步审讯。该外国人的态度极为傲慢无礼。当被问及名字是否为“Sea-scout Troop”时，他回答：“是。”问其国籍，他回答：“我住在上海。把我送到上海，你们就会知道。”索要护照，他回答：“没有。”向他出示那个包及其内容物并询问是否属于他时，他回答：“是。”当被问及为何开枪射击宪兵时，他挑衅地拒绝回答。鉴于连部报告称已逮捕一名匪徒，且该外国人没有护照，携带两支手枪、氯仿和纱布面罩等物品，虽身携二十元纸币却未购买火车票，且在铁轨上匆忙行走，黄上校断定此人必是一名外国共产党亡命之徒。因此他打算将其送交法院审判。但由于受伤的宪兵李国才和沈立生已被送往上海医院治疗，黄上校决定待他们稍加康复，以便在将其送审前清楚查明该外国人开枪射击他们的具体情况。因此，他将该外国人拘禁在营房内。

被上校击毙
李国才于6月7日死亡，据报沈立生已无生还希望（沈于6月12日稍后死亡）。黄上校遂决定将该外国人送审。于是他在6月8日上午传唤该外国人进行进一步讯问。然而，该外国人仍拒绝直接说明自己的身份。他只说住在上海。经过反复盘问，他最终完全承认开枪射击了宪兵。当被问及用于射击并击伤宪兵的左轮手枪何在时，他回答已扔入水中。审讯至此，黄上校无法抑制愤怒，斥责该外国人并咒骂其为不法之徒。听到这些话，该外国人突然扑向黄上校，出其不意地猛烈击打他。面对该外国人凶狠的面目和野蛮的力量，黄上校拔出手枪将其当场击毙。

(3) 击毙该外国人后，黄震吾上校意识到其行为超出了正当防卫的范畴，因害怕受到惩处，他下令销毁包括尸体在内的所有证据痕迹，并严令所有部下不得泄露只言片语，企图掩盖此事。因此，初次调查未能揭示实际发生的情况。

身份确认无误
(4) 上述事实在随后对宪兵各连部和团部的调查中得以查明。通过对排长彭恒等人的严格审查获得了线索。对刘长文军士等人进行反复盘问，最终查明了案件事实，并毫无疑问地确认该外国人即为失踪的索恩伯恩。黄震吾上校随即被革职并送交审判。本部组建了军事法庭，被告黄震吾起初倚仗证据已被销毁而否认罪行。但当后来向其出示收集到的证据时，他对上述事实供认不讳。关于将该外国人确认为索恩伯恩这一点，向黄上校展示了英国当局在敦促调查时提供的索恩伯恩照片，他说这确实是他开枪击毙的那个人。案件事实既已查清，遂作出判决。

(5) 军事法庭的裁决结果是，被告黄震吾上校依法被判有期徒刑十四年。记录显示，他已开始服刑。

外交部印。

（印：工部局警务处档案 S. B. D. 2464/N. 16. 12. 31.）

警务处处长，
先生，
情报

The Thorburn Case

The editor of the China Times published the
following comment on November 1:-

After thorough investigations made by the
Chinese Government into the disappearance of Thorburn,
it has been found that he left Shanghai for Chenju by
train on June 1 and using his pistol, injured two
soldiers who succumbed to their injuries. This
caused resentment by soldiers on duty there. They
caught and sent him to Soochow where he was assaulted
and fatally injured. Upon discovery, the Chinese
Government arrested and placed the Regimental
Commander Wang in custody.

In view of the fact that relations between
China and Great Britain are closer, we regret the
occurrence of this unfortunate case. Although Thorburn
was wrong in killing two soldiers, the Chinese soldiers
failed to refer Thorburn to their Commander but
instead they assaulted and fatally injured him; such
acts being a violation of the law. The Chinese
Government will certainly inflict severe punishment
on these soldiers. However we hope that both Governments
will treat this affair as a usual military and criminal
case and will not enlarge it which would simply afford
irresponsible persons the chance to provoke instigations.

索伯恩案

《字林西报》（China Times）编辑于11月1日发表如下评论：

经中国政府对索伯恩失踪案进行彻底调查后，查明其于6月1日乘火车离开上海前往陈居（Chenju，音译），期间使用手枪致伤两名士兵，该两名士兵因伤身亡。此举引起当地执勤士兵的愤慨。他们将其抓获并送往苏州，在那里他遭到殴打并受致命伤。事发后，中国政府逮捕并拘留了团长王某。

鉴于中英两国关系日益密切，我们对这一不幸案件的发生深感遗憾。虽然索伯恩杀害两名士兵有错在先，但中国士兵未将索伯恩移交其指挥官，反而对其进行殴打并致其重伤身亡，此类行为违反法律。中国政府必将严惩这些士兵。然而，我们希望两国政府将此事件作为一般的军事和刑事案件处理，不要扩大事态，以免给不负责任之人提供煽动挑唆的机会。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, WEDNESDAY, NOVEMBER 2, 1932
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL C. & S. D. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. 2464/2
Date 5.11.32

THORBURN CASE CLEARED
UP BY CHINESE NOTE

Shanghai Youth Shot Dead by Officer
During Interrogation

ALL EVIDENCE DESTROYED

14 Years' Imprisonment For Colonel
Huang Who Killed Him

THE mystery of the disappearance of Mr. John Hay Thorburn, the Shanghai youth who left Shanghai at the end of May for Nanking, was involved in a shooting affair with Chinese gendarmes at Quinsan, and after his arrest was never seen again, is cleared up in a Note from the Nanking Government to Sir Miles Lampson, the British Minister.

The Note, to which is attached a summary of a translation of the report, reveals that Mr. Thorburn shot and fatally wounded two gendarmes and was arrested near Quinsan on June 2. He was subsequently interrogated by the Regimental Commander, Colonel Huang Chen-wu, who "lost his temper and provoked by the behaviour of the prisoner, drew his pistol and shot Thorburn dead." Col. Huang then destroyed all evidence, including disposing of the corpse and ordered his men to keep silent.

Tried by court martial, Col. Huang was sentenced to 14 years' imprisonment. Nanking has been orally informed that this settlement of the incident is acceptable to H. M. Government.

NANKING EXPRESSES REGRETS

The first document consists of a Note from Mr. Chingiuin W. Frank Lee, Acting Minister of Foreign Affairs, to Sir Miles Lampson, H. M. Minister to China, dated October 20, in which Mr. Lee states:

Sir:—With reference to the case of the disappearance of Mr. John Hay Thorburn, I have the honour to recall that in June last, based on certain reported facts concerning the case, an investigation was made at Quinsan and Soochow by the British Consular authorities, and that the result of this investigation was communicated to this Ministry together with certain papers tending to show that Mr. Thorburn was involved in the shooting affair which occurred near Quinsan on the night of June 1, and was arrested by the gendarmes on the morning of June 2 and taken to Soochow on the same day.

When it was known that the inquiry conducted early in July by the representatives of the Ministry of War and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs failed to reveal the same facts as found by the British Consular officials, Your Excellency communicated on July 29 to my predecessor, by instruction, a special message from the British Government to the Head of my Government who, as Your Excellency was notified on August 6, immediately ordered General Chen Yi, Vice-Minister of War, to make a thorough investigation of the matter.

Gen. Chen's Investigation

On account of the loss of all direct evidence which caused much difficulty at the initial stage of the investigation, General Chen proceeded with his work with especial care and circumspection, which accounts for the fact that his labours could not have been concluded as early as the Government desired.

On September 25, however, when General Chen's investigation had reached a satisfactory stage, my predecessor was able to inform Your Excellency that the arrest of Mr. Thorburn had been established and that the person involved in the affair had been placed under detention.

I have now received a full report from General Chen Yi, a copy of which is attached to the present note. From this report it is evident that the fears of the British Government as to the fate of Mr. Thorburn have been justified. It is with the utmost regret that the Chinese Government has to inform Your Excellency that Mr. Thorburn, after he had shot and wounded two gendarmes who subsequently died, was arrested near Quinsan on June 2 and met his death at Soochow at the hands of Colonel Huang Chen-wu on June 3. The Chinese Government further regrets that it is now clear from the report that Colonel Huang Chen-wu sought to suppress the truth as to what had occurred even from the Government itself.

Mr. J. H. Thorburn.

Jile
Silligal

中方照会澄清
索伯恩案

上海青年在审讯期间
被军官枪杀

所有证据被销毁

杀人凶手黄上校
被判监禁14年

上海青年约翰·海·索伯恩（John Hay Thorburn）先生于5月底离开上海前往南京，在昆山与中国宪兵发生枪战，被捕后便杳无音信，其失踪之谜随着南京政府致英国公使蓝普森爵士（Sir Miles Lampson）的一份照会而得以澄清。

该照会附有一份报告译文的摘要，显示索伯恩先生开枪击伤两名宪兵并致其死亡，随后于6月2日在昆山附近被捕。此后，他受到团长黄振武（Huang Chen-wu，音译）上校的审讯，黄上校“因囚犯的行为而激怒，失去理智，拔出手枪将索伯恩当场击毙”。随后，黄上校销毁了所有证据，包括处理尸体，并命令其部下保持沉默。

经军法审判，黄上校被判处14年监禁。南京方面已获口头通知，英王陛下政府接受对此事件的这一处理结果。

南京表示遗憾

第一份文件是代理外交部长李景基（Chingiuin W. Frank Lee，音译）先生于10月20日致英国驻华公使蓝普森爵士的照会，李先生在照会中称：

阁下：——关于约翰·海·索伯恩先生失踪一案，谨提请阁下注意，去年六月，基于该案某些 Reported facts（报道的事实），英国领事当局在昆山和苏州进行了调查，调查结果连同某些表明索伯恩先生卷入6月1日晚发生在昆山附近的枪击事件、并于6月2日上午被宪兵逮捕且同日被带往苏州的文件一并送交本部。

当得知陆军部和外交部代表于7月初进行的调查未能揭示出与英国领事官员所发现相同的事实时，阁下于7月29日奉命向我的前任转达了英国政府致我国政府首脑的特别信息，正如阁下于8月6日获知的那样，我国政府首脑随即命令陆军次长陈仪将军对此事进行彻底调查。

陈将军的调查

由于所有直接证据丢失，导致调查初期困难重重，陈将军以格外谨慎小心的态度开展工作，这也解释了为何其工作未能如政府所愿尽早完成。

然而，到了9月25日，当陈将军的调查取得令人满意的进展时，我的前任能够告知阁下，索伯恩先生被捕一事已得到证实，涉案人员已被拘留。

我现在收到了陈仪将军的完整报告，副本附于本照会之后。从该报告可以明显看出，英国政府对索伯恩先生命运的担忧是有根据的。中国政府极为遗憾地通知阁下，索伯恩先生在开枪击伤两名宪兵（后者随后死亡）后，于6月2日在昆山附近被捕，并于6月3日在苏州死于黄振武上校之手。中国政府进一步遗憾地指出，从报告中可以清楚看到，黄振武上校甚至试图向政府本身隐瞒事实真相。

J. H. 索伯恩先生。

吉乐（Jile，音译）
西利加尔（Silligal，音译）

page_data.en:
Why He was Not Handed Over
It may be recalled that the shooting affair near Quinsan occurred just at the time when the general menace of subversive activities in this country was at its height and when orders had been given to the gendarmerie to keep vigilance on all suspects in the regions traversed by the Nanking-Shanghai Railway. It was in these circumstances that Mr. Thorburn was arrested after the shooting incident and taken to Soochow. His own violent conduct, the strange articles found among his belongings, and his refusal to reveal his name and nationality, inevitably produced the suspicion that he was bent on some activity dangerous to the safety of the State. It was therefore owing to this state of apprehension and to the initial absence of any means of establishing Mr. Thorburn's identity that he was not handed over to the British authorities after his arrest.
As the report shows, a sentence of imprisonment for fourteen years has been imposed upon Colonel Huang Chen-wu as a result of a trial by court-martial, and I wish to add that the Chinese Government has caused the verdict to be communicated to all the military commanders.
The Chinese Government feels thankful for the help afforded by the British officials in supplying all the evidence at their disposal thereby contributing in no small degree to the eventual elucidation of what had occurred.
In conclusion, I wish to reaffirm the determination of the Chinese Government to uphold the modern conception of justice and see it administered within the Chinese territory and hope that the action taken by the Chinese Government in this case will convince the British Government of the sincerity of China's professions in the matter.
I avail myself of this opportunity to renew to Your Excellency the assurance of my highest consideration.

Summary of Report
Accompanying the Note is a summary of the report, which reads:
"On the night of June 1 three gendarmes patrolling the line met and challenged a suspicious character hurrying along the railway track. As the foreigner disregarded their challenge, they approached to investigate, whereupon the foreigner shot down two of the gendarmes. At this moment the express passed and the foreigner escaped. He dropped a bag containing a pistol and cartridges, a knife, a small bottle of chloroform and gauze face cover, and other articles. He was arrested next day and taken to Soochow where he was examined by the Regimental Commander Colonel Huang. He refused to say who he was except that he came from Shanghai, had no passport, admitted the bag was his, and refused to give any reasons for shooting the gendarmes. Colonel Huang in view of suspicious circumstances believed prisoner to be a foreign communist and intended sending him to the law courts. He desired, however, to await the recovery and evidence of the wounded gendarmes first. On June 7, Colonel Huang learned that one of the wounded men had died and that the other could not recover. He accordingly interrogated Thorburn again on June 8. In the course of this further interrogation Colonel Huang lost his temper and provoked by the behaviour of the prisoner, drew his pistol and shot Thorburn dead. Colonel Huang then realising what he had done, destroyed all evidence, including the corpse, and ordered his men not to divulge anything. In this way the first investigation failed. Subsequently the true facts were elicited from subordinate officers. Colonel Huang was arrested, brought to trial by court-martial and sentenced to 14 years' imprisonment."
The Nanking Government has been orally informed that this settlement of the incident is acceptable to H. M. Government."
page_data.zh:
为何未将其移交
值得一提的是，昆山附近的枪击事件发生时，正值国内颠覆活动威胁最为严重之际，且当局已下令宪兵对京沪铁路沿线地区的所有嫌疑人保持警惕。正是在这种背景下，索伯恩先生在枪击事件发生后被捕并被带往苏州。他本人的暴力行为、在其随身物品中发现的奇怪物件，以及他拒绝透露姓名和国籍，不可避免地使人怀疑他企图从事危害国家安全的活动。因此，正是由于这种担忧状态，加之起初无法确定索伯恩先生的身份，导致他在被捕后未被移交给英国当局。
正如报告所示，黄振武上校经军法审判后被判处14年监禁，我愿补充说明，中国政府已将该判决结果通报给所有军事指挥官。
中国政府感谢英国官员提供其所掌握的所有证据，这对最终阐明事件真相起到了不小的作用。
最后，我愿重申中国政府决心维护现代司法理念，并在中国领土内施行司法，希望中国政府在此案中的行动能使英国政府相信中国在此事上声明的诚意。
借此机会，我再次向阁下致以最崇高的敬意。

报告摘要
随照会附有一份报告摘要，内容如下：
“6月1日晚，三名沿铁路线巡逻的宪兵遇到并盘查一名沿铁轨匆忙行走的可疑人物。由于该外国人无视盘查，宪兵上前调查，该外国人随即开枪击倒两名宪兵。此时快车经过，该外国人逃脱。他掉落了一个包，内含手枪及子弹、一把刀、一小瓶氯仿和纱布面罩及其他物品。次日他被捕并被带往苏州，由团长黄上校进行审问。他拒绝说明身份，仅称来自上海，没有护照，承认包是他的，但拒绝说明向宪兵开枪的理由。鉴于情况可疑，黄上校认为囚犯是一名外国共产主义者，打算将其送交法庭。但他希望先等待受伤宪兵康复并提供证词。6月7日，黄上校得知一名伤者死亡，另一名无法康复。因此，他于6月8日再次审讯索伯恩。在这次进一步审讯过程中，黄上校因囚犯的行为而被激怒，失去理智，拔出手枪将索伯恩当场击毙。黄上校随后意识到自己所作所为，销毁了包括尸体在内的所有证据，并命令部下不得泄露任何消息。至此，第一次调查失败。随后，从下级军官处查明了真实情况。黄上校被捕，经军法审判，被判处14年监禁。”
南京政府已获口头通知，英王陛下政府接受对此事件的这一处理结果。”

THE SHANGHAI MERCURY, TUESDAY, NOVEMBER 3, 1931.

Stricter London Comment
On Thorburn Case And
"Extraterritoriality" Surrender

Lord Lloyd Says That Protection Of Consular
Jurisdiction Should Not Be Abolished
Until Parliament Has Approved

"NEWS CHRONICLE" POINTS OUT HOW
CHINA ENDANGERS HER CAUSE

LONDON, Oct. 31.—The newspapers to-day again give prominence to the Thorburn case and there is very pungent criticism of what is regarded as the inability of the Chinese Government to maintain law and order. In a letter to the "Times," Lord Lloyd, the former High Commissioner of Egypt and the Sudan, referring to the agreement which it is understood Sir Miles Lampson negotiated with Dr. C. T. Wang, the former Chinese Foreign Minister, cites the Thorburn case as a reason why extraterritoriality rights should not be abolished, at any rate until Parliament has been given an opportunity to review the whole question.

The comments of the papers on the Thorburn case are based upon the Chinese report of the official investigation into Thorburn's disappearance. It is understood that this report states that Thorburn, when halted by troops in Soochow, drew his revolver and shot two soldiers. He was then overpowered and after being paraded through the streets of Soochow was killed. The disposition of the body, it is stated, still remains a mystery.

"Possible Murder"

The "News Chronicle" states that the alarming feature of the Thorburn murder is not merely that such an outrage should be possible, but that it is so difficult to suggest any really adequate measures for the protection of the lives of British nationals against such outrages.

"What can be hoped for," says the paper, "is that Chinese authorities, with the example from Soochow before their eyes, will realize that the peril in which they place themselves and their house when they allow such things to happen is greater than any advantage they may hope to gain."

Lord Lloyd cites the general understanding that Sir Miles Lampson, the British Minister to China, has recently negotiated a treaty with the Chinese Foreign Minister under which Britons will be finally deprived of the protection of Consular Jurisdiction.

He declares it to be the unanimous opinion and the urgent plea of British communities in China that no such treaty should be concluded until its conditions have been submitted to, and approved by, Parliament.

A Remote Prospect

Lord Lloyd, in support of his contention, quotes the Thorburn case and says the prospect of any stable and effective Central Government being established in China is extremely remote.

He also emphasizes the difficulties with Japan in the absence of a Government in China which is able to maintain order and protect the interests of foreigners and, finally, points to the fact that the Foreign Minister, with whom Sir Miles Lampson has been negotiating in Nanking, has now resigned from the Central Government.

《上海泰晤士报》，1931年11月3日，星期二。

伦敦就索恩伯恩案及放弃“治外法权”发表更严厉评论

劳埃德勋爵称，在议会批准之前，不应废除领事裁判权的保护

《新闻纪事报》指出中国如何危及其自身事业

伦敦，10月31日电。——今日各报再次显著报道索恩伯恩案，并对被视为中国政府无法维持法律和秩序的情况进行了非常尖锐的批评。前埃及和苏丹高级专员劳埃德勋爵在给《泰晤士报》的一封信中，提及据悉英使蓝普森爵士与前中国外交部长王正廷博士谈判达成的协议，引用索恩伯恩案作为理由，说明治外法权权利不应被废除，至少应等到议会有机会审查整个问题之后。

报纸对索恩伯恩案的评论是基于中方关于调查索恩伯恩失踪事件的官方报告。据悉，该报告称，索恩伯恩在苏州被军队拦下时，拔出手枪射伤两名士兵。随后他被制服，在被押解游街示众于苏州街道后遭杀害。据报道，尸体的处置至今仍是个谜。

“可能系谋杀”

《新闻纪事报》称，索恩伯恩谋杀案令人震惊之处不仅在于此类暴行可能发生，而且在于很难提出任何真正充分的措施来保护英国国民的生命免受此类暴行侵害。

该报称：“人们所希望的是，中国当局以苏州事件为鉴，认识到允许此类事情发生使他们自身及其国家置于的危险，大于他们可能希望获得的任何利益。”

劳埃德勋爵引用普遍看法，即英国驻华公使蓝普森爵士最近与中国外交部长谈判了一项条约，根据该条约，英国人将最终失去领事裁判权的保护。

他宣称，在华英国社群的一致意见和迫切呼吁是，在该条约的条件提交议会并获得批准之前，不应缔结此类条约。

前景渺茫

劳埃德勋爵为支持其主张，引用了索恩伯恩案，并称在中国建立任何稳定有效的中央政府的前景极其渺茫。

他还强调，由于中国缺乏一个能够维持秩序并保护外国人利益的政府，导致与日本的关系存在困难，最后他指出，蓝普森爵士一直在南京与之谈判的外交部长现已从中央政府辞职。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, OCTOBER 31, 1931

John Thorburn's Death
Confirmed In Nanking
Note To Great Britain

Chinese Authorities Admit Correctness Of Original
Report That British Youth Was Done To
Death And Body Destroyed

BRITISH AUTHORITIES HERE DECLINE
TO ISSUE ANY STATEMENT

According to messages from Nanking and London received here yesterday, the National Government, in a Note to the British Government, confirms the killing of John Thorburn by Chinese soldiers in the vicinity of Soochow on June 2 and the disposal of the body. The report of the findings of the commission which investigated the mysterious disappearance of the 18-year-old British youth have been awaited for many weeks, but it was known shortly after his disappearance that Thorburn was dead. Confirmation of the stack of evidence adduced to prove his murder was not forthcoming until the National Government presented its Note to the British Minister to China. Local British authorities declined to make any statement.

根据昨日在此收到的来自南京和伦敦的消息，国民政府在一项致英国政府的照会中，确认了约翰·索恩伯恩于6月2日在苏州附近被中国士兵杀害以及尸体被处置一事。人们已等待多周，盼望着调查这位18岁英国青年神秘失踪事件的委员会调查结果报告，但在其失踪后不久便已知晓索恩伯恩已死。直到国民政府向英国驻华公使提交照会，证实用于证明其被谋杀的大量证据才随之而来。当地英国当局拒绝发表任何声明。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, TUESDAY, OCTOBER 27, 1931

THE THORBURN
CASE

Chinese Reply Received
in London

OFFICIAL RETICENCE

“A Considerable Advance”
but—

FROM OUR OWN CORRESPONDENT

London, Oct. 26.

I am informed that the tenor of
the reply of the Chinese Govern-
ment to the British Government's
demands for a further Report on
the disappearance of Mr. John
Thorburn, as the result of the se-
cond investigation ordered by Gen-
eral Chiang Kai-shek, has been
communicated to the Foreign Office
here. The nature of the proposals
has not been disclosed and officials
are very reticent on the subject.
Although the reply, in certain ma-
terial respects, represents a con-
siderable advance on the Chinese
Government's original attitude,
there appear to be questions of vital
importance to be settled before it
can be considered that a satisfac-
tory outcome has been reached.
This seems to account for the
guarded view taken in Whitehall.

History of the Case

The following is a chronological
record of the history of the case:—
June 1. Mr. John Thorburn left
Shanghai in search of adventure.
June 2. Believed to have been ar-
rested by Chinese gendarmes.
June 3. Reported in the Chinese
press that a foreigner challenged on
the railway line near Weiting, on the
night of June 1, fired and wounded two
soldiers, making good his escape. He
was arrested on the following morning
and sent to Soochow under escort.
June 9. Mr. A. L. Scott, of the
British Consulate, visited Soochow to
make enquiries regarding Mr. Thor-
burn's disappearance.

June 10. Last credible evidence of
Mr. Thorburn's having been seen alive.
July 16. Official report by the Chin-
ese Ministry of Foreign Affairs to
British Government disclaiming all
knowledge of Mr. Thorburn or the
arrest of any foreigner.
July 21. Meeting of the China As-
sociation passes a resolution urging
the British Government to adopt
measures to secure exhaustive investiga-
tion.
Telegram with 2,800 signatures of
Shanghai residents despatched to Lon-
don demanding suitable action in the
case.
July 28. Mr. Sheng, the original
investigator appointed by the Chinese
Government into the case died as the
result of a ricksha accident.
July 25. Mr. Henderson instructs
Sir Miles Lampson to take the case to
General Chiang Kai-shek.
July 31. Sir Miles Lampson arrives
in Nanking by aeroplane.
August 10. The "North-China Daily
News" announces that General Chiang
Kai-shek, as the result of Sir Miles
Lampson's representations, has, in the
most emphatic language, ordered a new
enquiry.
August 12. General Ch i Yih ar-
rives at Soochow to conduct a new
enquiry, which is expected to be com-
pleted in less than a fortnight.
August 14. Reported by Reuter
from Nanking that General Chen Yih's
enquiry will throw no further light
on the case.
August 18. "North-China Daily
News" receives semi-official reports
from Nanking to the effect that the
enquiry is not completed.
August 19. "North-China Daily
News" receives news that General Chen
Yih has returned to Soochow to follow
up a new clue.
August 19. "North-China Daily
News" announces the receipt of reports
from Nanking to the effect that General
Chen Yih had returned from Soochow
and was preparing his report.
September 7. "North-China Daily
News" records a statement from
Chinese sources to the effect that the
enquiry would be speeded up and that
General Chiang Kai-shek was alive to
the importance of an early announce-
ment.
October 14. Sir Miles Lampson ar-
rives in Nanking by Air.
October 20. "North-China Daily
News" points out the necessity to
remove resentment caused by delay in
the Chinese Government's handling of
the Thorburn case.

《字林西报》，1931年10月27日，星期二

索恩伯恩案

伦敦收到中国回复

官方保持缄默

“重大进展”
但是——

本报特约记者

伦敦，10月26日。

我获悉，中国政府就约翰·索恩伯恩先生失踪一案向英国政府要求进一步报告的回复要点，已传达至此处外交部，该回复是蒋介石将军下令进行第二次调查的结果。提案的性质尚未披露，官员们对此事非常缄默。虽然该回复在某些重要方面代表了中国政府最初态度的重大进步，但在被认为达成满意结果之前，似乎仍有至关重要的问题需要解决。这似乎解释了怀特霍尔（Whitehall，指英国政府）所持的谨慎观点。

案件历史

以下是该案历史的 chronological 记录：—
6月1日。约翰·索恩伯恩先生离开上海去寻找冒险经历。
6月2日。据信被中国宪兵逮捕。
6月3日。中文报纸报道称，一名外国人在6月1日晚于唯亭附近的铁路线上受到盘查时开枪打伤两名士兵，成功逃脱。他于次日早晨被捕，并在押送下送往苏州。
6月9日。英国领事馆的A. L. Scott先生访问苏州，查询索恩伯恩先生失踪事宜。

6月10日。有关索恩伯恩先生生前被看到的最后可信证据。
7月16日。中国外交部向英国政府提交正式报告，否认知晓索恩伯恩先生或任何外国人被捕之事。
7月21日。上海英商公会会议通过决议，敦促英国政府采取措施确保进行彻底调查。
带有2800名上海居民签名的电报发往伦敦，要求在此案中采取适当行动。
7月28日。中国政府任命的最初调查此案的盛先生因人力车事故去世。
7月25日。亨德森先生指示蓝普森爵士将此案提交给蒋介石将军。
7月31日。蓝普森爵士乘飞机抵达南京。
8月10日。《字林西报》宣布，鉴于蓝普森爵士的交涉，蒋介石将军以最强烈的措辞下令重新调查。
8月12日。陈仪将军抵达苏州主持新的调查，预计将在不到两周内完成。
8月14日。路透社从南京报道，陈仪将军的调查不会为此案提供更多线索。
8月18日。《字林西报》收到来自南京的半官方报告，称调查尚未完成。
8月19日。《字林西报》收到消息，陈仪将军已返回苏州跟进新线索。
8月19日。《字林西报》宣布收到来自南京的报告，称陈仪将军已从苏州返回，正在准备报告。
9月7日。《字林西报》记录了中国方面的声明，称调查将加速进行，蒋介石将军意识到尽早公布的重要性。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Monday, October 19, 1931
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S. C. REGISTRY No S. D. D. 2464/31 Date 21.10.31.）

THE THORBURN CASE
AFTER 141 DAYS
By R. G. W. WOODMAN, C.M.G.

THE British Minister is once more in Nanking. And though it seems probable that the immediate object of his visit is to keep in touch with the Chinese Government during the Sino-Japanese crisis, it is to be hoped that he will also have instructions to press for a report upon the Thorburn case.

It is now 141 days since the young Briton, John Hay Thorburn, disappeared. He was last seen in the hands of the Chinese military at Quinsan and Soochow, and the evidence that has since been obtained from various sources leaves little doubt that he was done to death by his captors.

A demand for an investigation was made by the British Authorities, as soon as what in their opinion, was conclusive evidence that he had been arrested by the Chinese military had been obtained. And on July 16, the Ministry for Foreign Affairs transmitted to the British Minister a Report compiled by representatives of the Ministry of War and the Waichiaopu, which denied that the young Briton had ever been in the hands of the military, and quoted several of the witnesses who had been questioned by a British Consular Officer as saying exactly the opposite to what they told him.

Local Indignation
NOT unnaturally this brazen attempt to evade the issue aroused intense indignation among the British communities in China. The China Association, British Patriotic Societies and individual Britons took up the matter, and cabled strong protests to London, with the result that Mr. Miles Lampson was instructed to proceed to Nanking as soon as possible, and to take up the matter in person with General Chiang Kai-shek.

索恩伯恩案
141天后
作者：R. G. W. WOODMAN, C.M.G.

英国公使再次来到南京。虽然看来他此次访问的直接目的可能是在中日危机期间与中国政府保持联系，但希望他也接到指令，催促提交关于索恩伯恩案的报告。

这位年轻的英国人约翰·海·索恩伯恩失踪至今已141天。他最后一次被人看见是在昆山和苏州的中国军方手中，此后从各种来源获得的证据几乎毫无疑问地表明，他被捕获者杀害。

一旦英国当局获得了他们认为确凿的证据，证明他已被中国军方逮捕，便立即要求进行调查。7月16日，外交部向英国公使提交了一份由军政部代表和外务部（Waichiaopu）编制的报告，否认这位年轻的英国人曾落入军方手中，并引用了几位曾被英国领事官员询问过的证人的话，这些证人对领事官员所说的话与他们之前所说的完全相反。

地方愤慨
这种厚颜无耻地试图回避问题的做法自然引起了在华英国社群的强烈愤慨。上海英商公会、英国爱国团体和个人英国人介入此事，并向伦敦发出强烈抗议电报，结果是米尔斯·蓝普森先生受命尽快前往南京，亲自向蒋介石将军提出此事。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, TUESDAY, OCTOBER 6, 1931

CHINA QUESTIONS
IN COMMONS

Thorburn Case Produces
Another Query

NO CHANGE REPORT-
ED ON EXTRALITY

FROM OUR OWN CORRESPONDENT
London, Sept 15.
The following questions were
asked in the House this week:
6. Mr. Wardlaw-Milne asked the
Under-Secretary of State for For-
eign Affairs whether any further
action has been taken by His Ma-
jesty's Minister in China in connec-
tion with the disappearance of Mr.
John Thorburn; and, if so, with
what result?
The Under-Secretary of State for
Foreign Affairs (Captain Eden):
His Majesty's Minister has not
reported any action subsequent to
that described in my reply to the
hon. Member for Chester (Sir C.
Cayzer) on Thursday last.

Extraterritoriality

7. Mr. Wardlaw-Milne asked the
Under-Secretary of State for For-
eign Affairs what is the present
position of the extraterritoriality
negotiations being carried on with
the Chinese Government?
Captain Eden: As stated in the
answer returned in this House on
June 17 last, the negotiations have
reached a stage which enables them
to be reported to their respective
Governments. Owing to the political
conditions in China, there has been
no change in the position since that
date.
Mr. Wardlaw-Milne: Are we to
understand that negotiations have,
in fact, been interrupted and no
date has been fixed for their resump-
tion? If not, is not that desirable
in view of the Thorburn case and
other cases of a similar kind, which
appear to make it undesirable to go
on with these negotiations?
Captain Eden: The position is
that neither Government has yet
completed its examination of the
position reached in the negotiations.

下议院中的
中国问题

索恩伯恩案引发
又一质询

据报道治外法权
谈判无变化

本报驻伦敦记者专电
伦敦，9月15日。
本周在下议院提出了以下问题：
6. 沃德劳-米尔恩先生（Mr. Wardlaw-Milne）询问外交部次长，陛下驻华公使是否就约翰·索恩伯恩先生（Mr. John Thorburn）失踪一事采取了进一步行动；如有，结果如何？
外交部次长（伊登上尉 Captain Eden）：陛下驻华公使未报告在上周四回复切斯特选区议员（卡泽爵士 Sir C. Cayzer）时所述行动之后的任何新行动。

治外法权

7. 沃德劳-米尔恩先生询问外交部次长，目前与中国政府进行的治外法权谈判处于何种阶段？
伊登上尉：正如去年6月17日在本下议院所作答复中所述，谈判已达到可向各自政府汇报的阶段。由于中国的政治局势，自该日期以来局势没有变化。
沃德劳-米尔恩先生：我们是否可以理解为谈判实际上已经中断，且尚未确定恢复谈判的日期？如果不是，鉴于索恩伯恩案及其他类似案件，继续这些谈判似乎并不适宜，难道此时中断不是更可取吗？
伊登上尉：情况是，双方政府均未完成对谈判所达阶段的审查。

归档

REPORT EXPECTED AT

LONDON, Sept. 14.—Replying
to a question in connection with
the Thorburn case in the House
of Commons to-day, Captain E. A.
Eden, the Under Secretary of
State for Foreign Affairs, stated
that neither the British nor the
Chinese Government had complet-
ed their examination of the posi-

tion subsequent to that described
in the statement he made last
Thursday, when he informed the
House that the inquiry had not
been completed, adding, the Chin-
ese Government had reported it

that its report could be expected
before the end of the current
month.
Sir Miles Lampson, he continu-
ed, had pressed the Chinese Minis-

moment and made known his dis-
appointment at the delay of the

it.

resident of Shanghai, disappear-

been heard of.—Reuter.

September 8, 1931. Morning Translation

MISCELLANEOUS

TRUTH ABOUT THE THORBURN CASE

The Shanghai Nippo publishes
the following report:-
Soochow, August 31.
According to a reliable source, the following truthful
statement regarding the Thorburn case has been received.
At midnight on June 1, two Chinese gendarmes, who were
on sentry duty in the vicinity of Tsing Nyi Railway
station guarding the line, observed a suspicious looking
European whom they questioned. Thorburn shot both
these gendarmes and made good his escape under cover of
the darkness. A thorough search for the culprit was
instituted by the Chinese authorities. Mr. Thorburn
was arrested and taken to the gendarmerie headquarters
of the First Corps at Soochow. The gendarmerie authorities
suspected Thorburn to be a communist attempting to
damage the railway line as he had left near the track
certain instruments such as monkey wrench, screw drivers
etc. Judging from the prisoners clothing and
language it was apparent that he was an Englishman, but
they tried to force Mr. Thorburn to admit that he was
a communist, finally torturing him by stringing him up
because he refused to admit the allegation. Mr.
Thorburn fainted due to loss of blood from injuries.
The following day the Chief of the Gendarmerie Corps
who was absent returned to headquarters and was informed
regarding Thorburn case. He scolded the officers who
conducted the case, but Mr. Thorburn was afterward
shot and incinerated in order to destroy all proof
because the gendarmerie authorities feared serious trouble
would arise should Thorburn be set free. The gendarmerie
authorities also ordered all the Chinese newspaper men
not to publish a word about the matter and forced some
of them who had already published certain parts of the
incident to contradict their statements. However
there was a certain newspaper reporter who witnessed
Thorburn being tortured. He can not divulge the
particulars because of the existing relations between
Britain and China. It is expected however that the
persons responsible for Thorburn's death will be punished
in accordance with law. It is also reported that Mr.
Chen Nyi, who was commissioned to investigate the matter,
submitted his report to General Chiang giving the true
fact of the case and has asked instruction how to deal
with the matter in a proper manner.

KOREAN SENTENCED

The Shanghai Nichi-Nichi
publishes the following report:-
A Korean named Kim Do
Man, aged 27, residing at No. 25 East Tuhong Road, Chapel,
was arrested by the Japanese Consular authorities on
September 1, for violating the deportation order of
the Japanese Consular Police and conducting a brothel.
He was sentenced to 14 days' imprisonment at the Japanese
Police Court.

JAPANESE SKETCHED

1931年9月8日。晨间译文

杂项

索恩伯恩案真相

《上海日报》（Shanghai Nippo）刊登如下报道：-
苏州，8月31日。
据可靠消息来源，收到有关索恩伯恩案的如下真实陈述。
6月1日午夜，两名在津浦铁路（Tsing Nyi Railway）车站附近守卫线路的中国宪兵哨兵，观察到一名形迹可疑的欧洲人并对其进行了盘问。索恩伯恩开枪射击这两名宪兵，并在夜色掩护下成功逃脱。中国当局随即对凶手展开了全面搜捕。索恩伯恩先生被捕后被带往苏州第一军团宪兵司令部。宪兵当局怀疑索恩伯恩是一名试图破坏铁路线的共产党人，因为他在轨道附近留下了扳手、螺丝刀等某些工具。从囚犯的衣着和语言判断，他显然是一名英国人，但他们试图强迫索恩伯恩先生承认自己是共产党人，最终因他拒绝承认这一指控而将其吊起施以酷刑。索恩伯恩先生因受伤失血过多而昏迷。
次日，外出不在的宪兵团团长返回司令部，获悉了索恩伯恩案的情况。他斥责了办理此案的官员，但随后索恩伯恩先生被枪决并焚尸，以销毁所有证据，因为宪兵当局担心如果释放索恩伯恩将会引起严重麻烦。宪兵当局还命令所有中国新闻记者不得刊登有关此事的任何文字，并迫使一些已经刊登了部分事件内容的记者撤回其陈述。然而，有一位目睹索恩伯恩受刑的报社记者。由于英中之间的现有关系，他不能透露细节。不过，预计对索恩伯恩之死负责的人员将依法受到惩处。另据报道，奉命调查此事的陈仪（Chen Nyi）先生已向蒋介石将军提交了报告，陈述了案件的真实情况，并请示如何妥善处理此事。

朝鲜人被判刑

《上海日日新闻》（Shanghai Nichi-Nichi）刊登如下报道：-
一名名叫金道万（Kim Do Man）的27岁朝鲜人，居住在闸北（Chapel）东土洪路25号，因违反日本领事警察的驱逐令并经营妓院，于9月1日被日本领事当局逮捕。他被日本警察法庭判处监禁14天。

日本人素描

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SATURDAY, SEPTEMBER 12, 1931

NOTES & COMMENTS

The Thorburn Case

The statement that the Chinese Government expect to be able to issue a "satisfactory" report on the disappearance of Mr. John Thorburn and to submit it to Sir Miles Lampson before the end of the current month, is elicited from the new Under-Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs in the House of Commons. It shows that the process of speeding up the report of General Chen Yih has not been as effective as was recently suggested from Nanking. It means, presumably that, in the course of the next fortnight the document will be available for the British Government. Of its character it is impossible to say anything in advance at this stage. There was, it will be remembered, an apparently authoritative suggestion that it left matters where they were. This was, however, promptly denied by other equally authoritative statements, which went so far as to hint that material evidence of value had been obtained, leading to General Chen Yih's second visit to Soochow. It seems to be essential that, after this long delay, some substantial result should accrue in response to the British Government's urgent inquiries. The matter may be left there for the moment.

笔记与评论

索恩伯恩案

外交部新任次长在下议院透露，中国政府期望能够就约翰·索恩伯恩先生失踪一案发布一份“令人满意”的报告，并在本月月底前提交给迈尔斯·兰普森爵士。这表明，加速陈仪将军报告进程的努力并未如近期南京方面所暗示的那样有效。这可能意味着，在未来两周内，英国政府将能看到这份文件。在此阶段，不可能对其性质做任何预先判断。人们记得，曾有一种看似权威的说法暗示报告维持原状，未带来新进展。然而，其他同样权威的声明迅速否认了这一点，甚至暗示已获得有价值的重要证据，导致陈仪将军第二次前往苏州。看来至关重要的是，在经过如此漫长的拖延后，针对英国政府的紧急质询应产生一些实质性的结果。此事暂且搁置于此。

----------------------------------------

TRUTH ABOUT THE THORBURN CASE

The Shanghai Nippo publishes
the following report :-
Soochow, August 31.

According to a reliable source, the following truthful
statement regarding the Thorburn case has been received.
At midnight on June 1, two Chinese gendarmes, who were
on sentry duty in the vicinity of Tsing Nyi Railway
station guarding the line, observed a suspicious looking
European whom they questioned. Thorburn shot both
these gendarmes and made good his escape under cover of
the darkness. A thorough search for the culprit was
instituted by the Chinese authorities. Mr. Thorburn
was arrested and taken to the gendarmerie headquarters
of the First Corps at Soochow. The gendarmerie authorities
suspected Thorburn to be a communist attempting to
damage the railway line as he had left near the track
certain instruments such as monkey wrench, screw drivers
etc. Judging from the prisoners clothing and
language it was apparent that he was an Englishman, but
they tried to force Mr. Thorburn to admit that he was
a communist, finally torturing him by stringing him up
because he refused to admit the allegation. Mr.
Thorburn fainted due to loss of blood from injuries.
The following day the Chief of the Gendarmerie Corps
who was absent returned to headquarters and was informed
regarding Thorburn case. He scolded the officers who
conducted the case. Thorburn was afterward
shot and incinerated in order to destroy all proof
because the gendarmerie authorities feared serious trouble
would arise should Thorburn be set free. The gendarmerie
authorities also ordered all the Chinese newspaper men
not to publish a word about the matter and forced some
of them who had already published certain parts of the
incident to contradict their statements. However
there was a certain newspaper reporter who witnessed
Thorburn being tortured. He can not divulge the
particulars because of the existing relations between
Britain and China. It is expected however that the
persons responsible for Thorburn's death will be punished
in accordance with law. It is also reported that Mr.
Chen Nyi, who was commissioned to investigate the matter,
submitted his report to General Chiang giving the true
facts of the case and has asked instruction how to deal
with the matter in a proper manner.

索伯恩案真相

《上海日文报纸》（Shanghai Nippo）刊登如下报道：——
苏州，8月31日。

据可靠消息来源，收到关于索伯恩（Thorburn）案的如下真实陈述。6月1日午夜，两名中国宪兵在青泥（Tsing Nyi，音译）火车站附近执行守卫铁路线的哨兵任务时，发现一名形迹可疑的欧洲人并对其进行盘问。索伯恩枪击了这两名宪兵，并在夜色掩护下成功逃脱。中国当局随即对凶手展开了全面搜捕。索伯恩先生被捕后被带至苏州第一军团宪兵司令部。宪兵当局怀疑索伯恩是一名企图破坏铁路线的共产党人，因为他在铁轨附近留下了扳手、螺丝刀等工具。从囚犯的衣着和语言判断，他显然是一名英国人，但当局试图强迫索伯恩先生承认他是共产党人，最终因他拒绝承认这一指控而将其吊起施以酷刑。索伯恩先生因受伤失血过多而昏厥。次日，外出不在的宪兵团长返回司令部，获悉索伯恩案情况。他斥责了负责此案的警官。随后，索伯恩被枪决并焚尸，以销毁所有证据，因为宪兵当局担心若释放索伯恩将引发严重事端。宪兵当局还命令所有中国报人不得刊登有关此事的任何文字，并迫使一些已刊登部分案情的人否认其先前的报道。然而，有一位报社记者目睹了索伯恩受刑的过程。由于英中之间现存的关系，他无法透露细节。不过，预计对索伯恩之死负责的人员将依法受到惩处。另据报道，奉命调查此事的陈尼（Chen Nyi，音译）先生已向蒋介石将军提交报告，陈述案件真实情况，并请示如何妥善处理此事。

THE CHINESE DAILY

The Shen Pao publishes the following
telegram from Nanking:-
In connection with Thortman's disappearance,
the British Authorities have sent a note to the Ministry
of Foreign Affairs on the result of their findings:-
(1) A member of the Chinese Military Police, named
Sada , states that on June 2 he saw a foreigner
arrested after a shooting affray with a foreign
youth near Tsinan.
(2) A certain woman of Tsinan described the arrest
of a foreign youth whose features resemble those
of Thortman whose photo was shown to her by the
British investigator.
(3) A railway policeman at Tsinan Station declared
that in the afternoon of June 2 he saw a foreigner
travelling to Soochow by train. Another policeman
stated that the said foreigner declared himself to
be a British subject.
In addition to the foregoing, there are other
proofs such as fracture of his nose, ears, etc., having
been cut off.
On the day in question at Tsinan, 20 miles
distant from Shanghai, the Chinese Military Police were
engaged in a gun fight with a foreigner, resulting in
the death and wounding of both Chinese soldiers and the
subsequent arrest of the foreigner.

August 9, 1928.
Nanking Transmission

THE CHINA TIMES EDITORIAL.

RE THORNTON CASE—DENIAL OF DISCOVERY.

The China Times reports:—
In connection with the disappearance of a British subject named Thornton and the publication of yesterday's Nanking telegram to the effect that Thornton's dead body had been found in Soochow, a reporter of the Far Eastern News agency yesterday called on Dr. Tang Wen Tsao, Chief of the Shanghai Office of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, enquiring the truth of the report. In reply Dr. Tang solemnly declared that the news was entirely groundless. He has also requested Dr. C. T. Wang, Minister for Foreign Affairs, to send a wire to the Nanking Ministry directing it to disclaim the source of this telegram.
----------
The China Times publishes the following letter from the Shanghai Office of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs:—
We were greatly surprised to read a telegram from Nanking published in your paper of August 8 that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs was in receipt of a report from its Shanghai Office to the effect that the dead body of a missing British subject named Thornton had been found in Soochow. In this connection, we have to state that this office has received no news regarding this case nor has it forwarded any report to the Ministry. We therefore request you to publish a correction in order to avoid misunderstanding.

《字林西报》报道：——
关于一名名为桑顿（Thornton）的英国臣民失踪一事，以及昨日南京电讯所称桑顿尸体已在苏州被发现的说法，《远东新闻社》（Far Eastern News agency）的一名记者昨日拜访了外交部上海办事处主任唐文藻（Tang Wen Tsao）博士，询问该报道的真实性。唐博士郑重声明，该消息完全毫无根据。他还请求外交部长王正廷（C. T. Wang）博士致电南京外交部，指令其否认该电讯的来源。
----------
《字林西报》刊登如下来自外交部上海办事处的信函：——
阅及贵报8月8日刊登的来自南京的电讯，称外交部收到其上海办事处报告，指出一名失踪的英国臣民桑顿的尸体已在苏州被发现，我们深感惊讶。就此，我们必须声明，本办事处未收到关于此案的任何消息，也未向部里转发任何报告。因此，我们请求贵报刊登更正，以避免误解。

The China Press published the following report on July 29th:
The circumstances of Hartman, an English youth, as first, have not been located since he was missing on the night of May 6th.
Information from foreign sources states that he was arrested by police and removed to Nanking in connection with the shooting of Military Police at the Wei-Hsing Railway Station.
Upon receipt of a letter from Mr. Miles Lampson, the British Minister in China, and the British Consul in Nanking, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of the Interior directed efforts to conduct careful investigations regarding the case of seizure and detention and have now sent a reply to the effect that after enquiries to the military authorities stating that no Hartman was ever arrested. These Ministries have also instructed the civil and military authorities of the Shanghai, Chekiang and Anhwei Provincial Governments to locate the whereabouts of the missing Hartman.

（批：Extract for file）
（批：m.c.）

The China Press published the following comment on July 30th:
For the past week reports on Hartman were have been published in local Chinese and foreign newspapers.
Hartman, an English boy of 19 years old, mysteriously left home and did not return. Simultaneously a case of shooting of Military Police took place and, according to press reports, the culprit was a Russian who, it was also reported, had been arrested.
Corresponding, foreign newspapers contained that the prisoner was Hartman. Hartman's family then approached the British Minister in China for assistance. The latter detailed officials to contact investigators and also requested the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to ask the Ministry of War to get information.
According to Peking's "Jenmin" the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in its reply stated that as a result of investigations made jointly by the officers of the Ministries of Foreign Affairs and War, no development in the case of Hartman has been secured by members of the Chinese Army.
It is still a matter of doubt whether on the day in question Hartman was ever at the scene of the shooting of the Military Police — of course, the fact that Hartman has vanished cannot be definitely proved. The matter is very puzzling. Recently, the Shanghai Evening Post and Mercury of to-day's date publishes a statement to the effect that Hartman was really arrested by Chinese soldiers and that the reply of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs is unsatisfactory. In closing the brief, briefly, the story was correct; but this cannot any affect the validity of the justification of international relationship.

I (the writer) do not know whether Mr. Hartman consulted with the Judge or (in point of the matter) simply purpose to writing his account to the Shanghai Times because the facts in question also touched the guilt of the Japanese public although it was very clear by then the offence had been committed.

《字林西报》于7月29日刊登了以下报道：
英国青年哈特曼（Hartman）自5月6日晚失踪以来，其下落起初一直未被查明。
据外籍人士方面的消息指出，他因涉及在卫兴火车站枪击宪兵一案，被警方逮捕并押往南京。
在收到英国驻华公使迈尔斯·兰普森（Miles Lampson）先生和英国驻南京领事的来信后，外交部与内政部指示对该扣押和拘留案件进行仔细调查，并已复函称，经向军方查询，答复是从未逮捕过名为哈特曼的人。上述两部亦已指令上海、浙江及安徽省政府的文武当局查找失踪者哈特曼的下落。

（批注：摘录归档）
（批注：m.c.）

《字林西报》于7月30日刊登了以下评论：
过去一周，当地中英文报纸均刊登了有关哈特曼的报道。
哈特曼是一名19岁的英国少年，神秘离家后未归。与此同时，发生了一起枪击宪兵的案件，据报刊报道，凶手是一名俄国人，亦有报道称该人已被捕。
相应地，外文报纸刊载称被捕者即为哈特曼。哈特曼的家属随后向英国驻华公使求助。后者指派官员联系调查人员，并请求外交部向陆军部询问以获取信息。
据北京《人民报》称，外交部在回复中表示，经外交部和陆军部官员联合调查，中国军队成员并未在哈特曼一案中取得任何进展。
事发当日哈特曼是否曾出现在枪击宪兵的现场，仍属疑点——当然，哈特曼失踪这一事实也无法得到确证。此事令人十分困惑。近日，《上海晚邮报与信使报》在今日的版面中发表声明，称哈特曼确实被中国士兵逮捕，且外交部的回复不能令人满意。简而言之，该报道是正确的；但这并不影响国际关系正当性的效力。

我（作者）不知哈特曼先生是否咨询过法官，或（就此事而言）仅仅是为了向《泰晤士报》撰写他的陈述，因为所涉事实也触及日本公众的罪责，尽管当时罪行已经非常清楚。

THE SHOCKING CASE OF THORNTON VTE THE BRITISH MERCHANT-

The China Press publishes the following
articles:-

At the present time when the Japanese are
aggressing Manchuria and when Japan is making aggressive policy
against China, naturally arousing unfavourable attitude towards
namely the disappearance of Thornton. Thornton is a
British resident of Shanghai aged 50. He is missing and
so far has not been located. Many Britishers suspect
he was assaulted and put to death by Chinese soldiers and
consequently are demanding that their Minister in China
lodge a protest with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of
the Chinese Government requesting a thorough investigation
into the affair.

This incident has been seldom mentioned in the
Chinese press and so our readers know little of the
indignation displayed by the Britishers over it, and
perhaps many have not yet heard of the case. We can
imagine that, while no proof of Thornton's death is yet
to hand, the Britishers have unanimously stood together
in this case in such a manner that they intend to satisfy
themselves that China is to be blamed. Their indignation
is really caused more greater than in any attitude
towards the massacre of hundreds of Chinese residents
who were butchered by Koreans in Korea.

I do not know where Thornton is at present,
whether he is alive or dead, but according to reports
published by the local foreign newspapers during the last
few days it is evident that he is dead and that he died
at the hands of Chinese. A certain foreign paper
published a large advertisement offering a reward of
$5,000 for information leading to his whereabouts. Other
foreign papers are daily publishing correspondence from
readers unanimously urging their government to open strong
negotiations with the National Government. Yesterday the
British community formed a committee which is prepared to
support the action of their government, and at the same
time a letter appeared in a certain paper stating that
the British Government should immediately serve an
ultimatum on the Chinese Government demanding the latter
to hand over Thornton within 48 hours, otherwise troops
would be dispatched to the Chinese Islands and these latter
seized.

桑顿案震惊人心——一位英国商人遇害

《字林西报》刊登了以下文章：

当前，日本正侵略满洲，并对中国采取侵略政策，自然引起了不利的态度，即桑顿（Thornton）失踪一事。桑顿是居住在上海的英国人，现年50岁。他已失踪，至今下落不明。许多英国人怀疑他遭到中国士兵袭击并被杀害，因此要求他们在中国的公使向中国政府外交部提出抗议，要求对此事进行彻底调查。

中文报纸很少提及此事，因此我们的读者对英国人由此表现出的愤慨知之甚少，或许许多人尚未听闻此案。我们可以想象，虽然目前尚无桑顿死亡的证据，但英国人在此案中团结一致，意图以此认定中国应受指责。他们的愤慨程度，实际上远超过对在朝鲜被韩国人屠杀的数百名中国居民所持的任何态度。

我不知道桑顿目前身在何处，是生是死，但根据过去几天当地外文报纸发布的报道，显然他已经死亡，且死于中国人之手。某家外文报纸刊登了一则大幅广告，悬赏5,000美元以获取能指引找到其下落的线索。其他外文报纸每日刊登读者来信，一致敦促其政府与国民政府展开强硬谈判。昨日，英侨社区成立了一个委员会，准备支持其政府的行动，同时某家报纸刊登了一封信，称英国政府应立即向中国政府发出最后通牒，要求后者在48小时内交出桑顿，否则将派遣军队前往中国岛屿并将其占领。

July 24, 1885.
Afternoon Translation

EDITORIAL

The foregoing comparisons show how the life
of a foreigner is valued as compared with that of Chinese.
When a foreigner disappears in China, there are certain
people who already say before it has even been ascertained
whether he is still alive or dead. On the other hand,
when Chinese are actually killed and shot by foreigners
and definite proofs are abundant, the foreigners treat
such an event as a matter of no consequence.
Where is justice and where is international
morality? Only one difference exists in this world,
namely the strong and the weak, the rich and the poor.
There is no such thing as courtesy, faith, shame, honour,
etc., etc. When there is talk of rights, one must
first of all possess sufficient power to support the
talk.

At the present moment, when the Sino-Japanese
negotiations are becoming serious, the case of Thortsen's
disappearance serves us with a good example with which to
judge others. It is still a matter of doubt whether
Thortsen is dead or alive. Supposing him to be dead,
then his life cannot be considered of more value than
that of the several hundreds of Chinese massacred in Korea
regarding which there is abundant proof. Notwithstanding
this, the independence of Chinese is not to be compared
with that displayed by the Britishers over Thortsen's
disappearance. Why is it that the life of Chinese
is held so lightly?

as above

社论

前述比较显示了外国人的生命与中国人的生命相比是如何被估价的。当一名外国人在中国失踪时，甚至在查明其生死之前，就已有人断言。另一方面，当中国人确实被外国人杀害和枪击，且证据确凿充分时，外国人却将此事件视为无足轻重。
正义何在？国际道德何在？这世上只存在一种区别，即强与弱、富与贫。不存在所谓礼让、信义、羞耻、荣誉等等。当谈论权利时，首先必须拥有足够的力量来支撑这种言论。

当前，中日谈判日益严峻，托尔森（Thortsen）失踪案为我们提供了一个评判他人的良好范例。托尔森是死是活仍属疑点。假设他已死亡，那么他的生命也不能被认为比在朝鲜被屠杀的数百名中国人的生命更有价值，而对于后者我们有充分的证据。尽管如此，中国人的独立精神却无法与英国人在托尔森失踪案中表现出的态度相提并论。为何中国人的生命如此被轻视？

同上

英国公众对其自身事务或其东方殖民地属地的行为是否感兴趣，或者是否漠不关心到足以允许所有国籍的人民真正安全，这仍是一个疑问。

THE THORNE INCIDENT - A COMMENTARY

The China Times publishes the following article:-

In connection with Thorne's disappearance, a letter written by a Chinese Mr. Gao appeared in a certain foreign evening newspaper on July 24 citing an incident which affected two Chinese in Australia some years ago. The following is the gist of the letter:-

"Two Chinese, brothers, named Ah Vong and Ah San respectively, returned to Australia from China where they had been attending school. Although they were born in Australia, they were refused entry by the Australian authorities who were not anxious at that time to have any more Chinese in Australia. In spite of their being in possession of birth certificates and passports, both brothers were forcibly detained and thrown in a deep prison at Port Darwin.

They were subsequently released pending the decision of the High Court of Australia, but immediately they regained their freedom, they were again arrested by British troops and removed to another place. While passing a bush, they unwittingly aroused the anger of the British soldiers and were driven into the bush where Ah Vong died from the intense heat. Ah San survived. Fortunately some days later he managed to effect his escape. He then reported the affair to the various Chinese overseas organizations who raised a hue and cry which continued for several months, but the Australian Government made no reply on the plea of lack of evidence. Finally the Australian authorities formally tendered an apology to the Chinese Government with advice to 'forget it'. This unfortunate affair was ultimately dropped.

"Death is terrible to both Chinese and foreigners. Supposing Thorne were actually killed by the Chinese, it is not a similar case to that of Ah Vong? If so, why is it doing therefore the Britishmen had better 'forget it'.

If the Australians would but calmly think the matter over after reading Mr. Gao's letter, the Thorne case would soon collapse. I wish, however, to inform Mr. Gao that the life of a foreigner is considered to be of more value than that of Chinese. Several decades ago, in the year Kang Si of the Tsing Dynasty, the murder of a Japanese Legation Secretary resulted in war started by 8 allied powers. There are always old examples to quote for foreigners when Chinese are affected, but Chinese dispose of matters generally.

At the present time when China is still sound asleep, Mr. Gao's letter will have no effect.

索恩事件——评论

《时事新报》刊登了以下文章：

关于索恩（Thorne）失踪一事，一位姓高的中国先生于7月24日在某家外文晚报上发表了一封信，引用了几年前发生在澳大利亚的两名中国人的事件。以下是信件大意：

“两名中国人兄弟，分别名为阿旺（Ah Vong）和阿三（Ah San），从中国求学后返回澳大利亚。尽管他们出生在澳大利亚，但澳大利亚当局拒绝他们入境，因为当时当局不希望再有更多中国人进入澳大利亚。尽管两兄弟持有出生证明和护照，但仍被强行拘留并关进达尔文港的一所深牢中。

他们随后在等待澳大利亚高等法院裁决期间获释，但刚一重获自由，便再次被英军逮捕并转移到另一地点。在经过一片灌木丛时，他们无意中激怒了英国士兵，被驱赶进灌木丛中，阿旺因酷热而死。阿三幸存下来。幸运的是，几天后他设法逃脱。随后他将此事报告给各个海外华人组织，引发了持续数月的强烈抗议，但澳大利亚政府以缺乏证据为由未作答复。最终，澳大利亚当局正式向中国政府道歉，并建议‘忘掉此事’。这起不幸的事件最终不了了之。

“死亡对中国人和外国人来说都是可怕的。假设索恩确实是被中国人杀害的，这与阿旺的案例不是相似吗？如果是这样，那么英国人最好也‘忘掉此事’。

如果澳大利亚人在读完高先生的信后能冷静思考此事，索恩案很快就会瓦解。然而，我想告知高先生，外国人的生命被认为比中国人的生命更有价值。几十年前，在清朝康熙年间，一名日本公使馆秘书被谋杀，导致了八国联军发动的战争。当涉及中国人时，外国人总有旧例可引，但中国人通常自行处理事务。

当前，中国仍处于沉睡之中，高先生的信不会产生任何影响。

（批注：摘录归档）

MISCELLANEOUS

MR. THORBURN MURDERED BY CHINESE OFFICIALS

The Shanghai Night-Bulletin publishes the following report:-

On August 13, the Shanghai Night-Bulletin received an anonymous letter from a certain Chinese person outside of the administration of the Shanghai Municipal Council, for having handed over Mr. and Mrs. Thorburn on August 12 to the Chinese authorities and being under certain of their authority. The original communication implied that extraterritorial rights enjoyed by the British should not be withdrawn on the grounds that the Chinese authorities are corrupt and China's laws are unreliable. The letter also accuses the Chinese authorities of brutality by pointing out, as an example, the Thorburn case, as follows:-

(Extract for Thorburn bill)
(M.P.)

"Thorburn was arrested at Quinsan on June 30 and immediately handed over to Sheng Chen Yu (this man is phonetically spelled), Chief of the First Gendarmerie Corps at Suchow. Mr. Sheng immediately communicated with Mr. Ho Feng Lung, the Defence Commissioner of Nanking requesting instructions how to deal with Thorburn. About two weeks later the Defence Commissioner of Nanking issued the order to shoot Thorburn. Subsequently Thorburn was executed at the Nanking Gendarmerie Headquarters. His relatives the funeral the flying crowd at the execution can be easily identified. Thorburn's body was burnt together with his clothing thus leaving absolutely no trace of him. The information reported the other day by a Chinese newspaper to the effect that Thorburn's head was discovered in Suchow is sheer nonsense. Thorburn will never be found. I (the writer of the letter) have further details regarding Thorburn's murder. The public may doubt my information because I sent my letter without signing my name but I thought it wiser to publish my news at present however I am not afraid to lose my life for disclosing a great mystery of the Chinese Government. However I will stand before the public and give evidence when it is required. I also declare that the surrender of Mr. and Mrs. Thorburn to the Chinese authorities by the Shanghai Municipal Council is not compatible with the sense of humanity and justice."

At present, it is impossible to identify the writer of this letter, however, it appears that all his information is based at least on some degree of truth.

It is presumed that the day is fast approaching when all the truth regarding the Thorburn case will be brought into the lime light exposing the barbarous action of the Chinese authorities.

索恩伯恩先生被中国官员谋杀

《上海夜报》刊登了如下报道：-

8月13日，《上海夜报》收到一封来自上海工部局管辖范围之外某位中国人的匿名信，信中提及于8月12日将索恩伯恩夫妇移交给中国当局并受其管辖一事。原信函暗示，鉴于中国当局腐败且中国法律不可靠，不应以此为由撤销英国人享有的治外法权。该信还以索恩伯恩案为例，指责中国当局的暴行，内容如下：-

（索恩伯恩账单摘录）
(国会议员)

“索恩伯恩于6月30日在昆山被捕，并立即被移交给苏州第一宪兵团团长盛臣玉（音译）。盛先生随即与南京卫戍司令何丰林先生联系，请示如何处理索恩伯恩。约两周后，南京卫戍司令下达了枪决索恩伯恩的命令。随后，索恩伯恩在南京宪兵司令部被执行死刑。他的亲属、葬礼以及行刑时围观的人群都很容易辨认。索恩伯恩的尸体连同衣物一起被焚烧，因此没有留下任何痕迹。日前一家中文报纸报道说在苏州发现了索恩伯恩的头颅，这纯属无稽之谈。索恩伯恩永远也找不到了。我（写信人）掌握有关索恩伯恩被谋杀的更多细节。公众可能会怀疑我的信息，因为我寄信时未署名，但我认为目前公开我的消息更为明智，不过我并不害怕因揭露中国政府的一个巨大谜团而丧命。然而，当需要时，我将站在公众面前作证。我还声明，上海工部局将索恩伯恩夫妇移交给中国当局的做法不符合人道和正义感。”

目前，无法确认这封信的作者，但看来他的所有信息至少在一定程度上基于事实。

据推测，关于索恩伯恩案的全部真相即将大白于天下，从而揭露中国当局的野蛮行径。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, AUGUST 20, 1931

Note sent to Ministry
Of Foreign Affairs,
Nanking

1. — A British subject named Thorburn was arrested at Quinsan on June 2nd by Chinese military police and subsequently died from injuries received during the arrest. The circumstances of the arrest are still under investigation by the British Consular authorities.

2. — A certain woman of Quinsan described the arrest of a foreign youth whose features resemble those of Thorburn whose photo was shown to her by the British investigator (Mr. A. L. Sockett)

3. — A railway policeman at Quinsan station declared that in the afternoon of June 2 he saw a foreigner travelling to Soochow by train, while another policeman stated that the said foreigner declared himself to be a British subject.

On the day in question at Quinsan, 36 miles from Shanghai, two Chinese military police were engaged in a gun-fight with a foreigner, resulting in the death and wounding of both Chinese soldiers and the subsequent arrest of the foreigner.

Locally, no information of any sort is obtainable from the British consular authorities upon the Thorburn case, instructions having been issued by the Consul-General that no statement of any sort is to be made to the Press.

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, WEDNESDAY, AUGUST 19, 1931.
BRITISH DEMANDS ON
THORBURN
Promises Given To
Thorburn Case
In London
LONDON, July 28.—Sir Miles
Lampson, the British Minister in
China, has been instructed to tell
Marshal Chiang Kai-shek, the head
of the Chinese Government, that
the British Government consider
that Mr. Thorburn, a British subject,
who was disappeared at Tientsin,
and of whose fate no information
has been received, must be found
if he is still alive.
An announcement to this effect
was made in Parliament yesterday
by Dr. Dalton, the Under-Secretary
of State for Foreign Affairs, in reply
to a question by Mr. A. E. Pritt, M.P.,
in the "Daily Express."
Dr. Dalton said: "The report of
the Chinese commission of inquiry
states that all evidence shows that
the local Chinese authorities had
knowledge of any foreigners having
been arrested.
"Sir Miles Lampson has there-
fore been instructed to make re-
presentations to the Chinese Gov-
ernment in the following terms:—
Government's Duty
"Independent inquiries have
established beyond all reasonable
doubt that Mr. Thorburn, who is
under suspicion in some quarters
of having shot at and fatally
wounded two Chinese gendarmes,
was arrested and handed over to
the custody of military authorities,
who have found means to silence
the witnesses possessing knowledge
of the facts.
"It is the duty of the Chinese
Government in the first place to
discover Mr. Thorburn's where-
abouts and hand him over to the
British authorities in China if he
is still alive; and in the second
place to inflict suitable punishment
on any military authority who may
have been responsible for maltreat-
ing him or causing his death.
"His Majesty's Government
therefore most earnestly and
strongly urge the Chinese Govern-
ment with all expedition to find
means of persuading the military
authorities concerned in the pre-
sent case of the urgent necessity
of enabling the Chinese Govern-
ment to carry out the ordinary
obligations of a civilized State.'
"Sir Miles Lampson has been in-
structed to convey the foregoing
as a special message from His
Majesty's Government to Marshal
Chiang Kai-shek, the President of
the National Government, stating
that he has instructions to raise
the question with the highest
authority, since his Majesty's
Government must insist on pro-
per protection being afforded to
British subjects."

索恩伯恩案提出要求
伦敦就
索恩伯恩案作出承诺
伦敦，7月28日。— 英国驻华公使蓝普森爵士已奉命告知中国政府首脑蒋介石元帅，英国政府认为，在天津失踪且至今下落不明的英国臣民索恩伯恩先生，如果尚在人世，必须被找到。
外交部次长道尔顿博士（Dr. Dalton）昨日在议会回答议员 A. E. Pritt 先生在《每日快报》上提出的问题时，发表了上述声明。
道尔顿博士说：“中国调查委员会的报告指出，所有证据均显示，当地中国当局知晓有任何外国人被捕。
“因此，蓝普森爵士已奉命按以下措辞向中国政府提出交涉：—
政府的责任
“独立调查已毫无疑问地证实，索恩伯恩先生因涉嫌枪击并致命伤害两名中国宪兵而被捕，并被移交给军事当局看管，后者已设法让知情证人保持沉默。
“中国政府的首要责任是查明索恩伯恩先生的下落，如果他还活着，将其移交给在华英国当局；其次，对任何可能对其施虐或导致其死亡的军事当局人员给予适当惩罚。
“因此，英王陛下政府最诚挚且强烈地敦促中国政府尽快设法说服本案涉及的军事当局，使其认识到让中国政府履行文明国家通常义务的紧迫必要性。”
“蓝普森爵士已奉命将上述内容作为英王陛下政府给国民政府主席蒋介石元帅的特别口信传达给他，并说明他已奉命向最高当局提出此问题，因为英王陛下政府必须坚持为英国臣民提供适当的保护。”

THORBURN INQUIRY
NOT COMPLETE
Further Information Compels
More Investigations

FROM OUR OWN CORRESPONDENT
London, Aug. 17.
Inquiry at the Foreign Office here reveals the fact that the official report of the second inquiry into the disappearance of Mr. John Hay Thorburn has not yet been received. The result of the investigation made by the Vice-Minister of War, General Chen Yih, has not been forwarded by Sir Miles Lampson, H.M. Minister. Whitehall thus has no official knowledge of the substance of General Chen Yih's findings, which were reported in the Press to correspond with the findings of the first commission of inquiry, denying that any foreigner at all was involved in the shooting incident which, it is alleged, was the reason advanced for the arrest of the young Briton.
Semi-official reports from Chinese Government sources state that the inquiry of General Chen Yih into the disappearance of Mr. John Thorburn is not complete. It is believed that further information has been received necessitating inquiries which are now being made. The report is therefore not yet fully drafted for submission to the Foreign Ministry.
It will be recalled that, on Saturday, a Reuter message from Nanking stated that the report which was "nearly completed" threw no further light on the case and reiterated the statement that no foreigner had been arrested. On this message the "North-China Daily News" pointed out the serious implications of the adoption by the Chinese Government of so fantastic a report.

索恩伯恩调查
尚未完成
进一步信息迫使
进行更多调查

本报特约记者
伦敦，8月17日。
在此处的外交部进行的调查揭示了一个事实，即关于约翰·海·索恩伯恩（John Hay Thorburn）先生失踪案的第二次调查的正式报告尚未收到。由陆军次长陈仪将军进行的调查结果尚未由英国驻华公使蓝普森爵士转交。因此，白厅（英国政府）对陈仪将军调查结果的实质内容一无所知，此前新闻界报道称这些结果与第一次调查委员会的结果一致，否认有任何外国人卷入据称是导致这位年轻英国人被捕原因的枪击事件。
来自中国政府渠道的半官方报告称，陈仪将军对约翰·索恩伯恩先生失踪案的调查尚未完成。据信，已收到需要进一步调查的新信息，目前正在进行相关调查。因此，该报告尚未完全起草完毕以提交外交部。
回想起来，上周六，路透社从南京发出的消息称，这份“接近完成”的报告并未为该案提供更多线索，并重申没有外国人被捕的说法。针对这一消息，《字林西报》指出，中国政府采纳如此荒诞的报告具有严重的含义。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Monday, August 17, 1931

THE THORNBURN INQUIRY.
ANOTHER FARCE.
By H. G. W. WOODHEAD, C.M.G.

FOR some days past it has been repeatedly stated in the Chinese Press that General Chen Yi, Vice-Minister of War, who had been entrusted by General Chiang Kai-shek with the conduct of the new inquiry into the disappearance of John Thornburn, had returned to Nanking, after spending two or three days in Soochow and Quinsan, and had reported that he had been unable to discover any evidence in regard to the arrest and subsequent fate of the missing Briton.

This report was confirmed on Friday, by a Reuter message from Nanking, which stated that General Chen Yi's investigation had been nearly completed, and that his report to the Waichiaopu would throw no further light upon the case.

An Impossible Task
Until this report is officially confirmed I should hesitate to believe that the Chinese Government would be guilty of the crass stupidity of appointing the British Government to form a finding. General Chiang Kai-shek, it may be assumed, intended a thorough investigation, and entrusted the task to the most responsible military officer available for the task. But there has not been even a pretence of an investigation up to the present. And if a report is issued based upon what General Chen Yi has done up to the present grave doubts will be thrown upon the sincerity of the Chinese Government from the President downward.

No British Participation
It is no secret that exhaustive inquiries into Thornburn's disappearance have been made by a British Consular official, Mr. A. L. Scott, and that he obtained a mass of evidence that "established beyond reasonable doubt that Mr. Thornburn...was arrested and handed over to a Chinese Military Authority, who found reasons to silence witnesses with a knowledge of the facts." This quotation is from the statement made on behalf of the British Foreign Office in the House of Commons.

If, therefore, the Chinese Government really desired to elucidate the mystery of Mr. Thornburn's disappearance its first step should have been to invite Mr. Scott to attend the inquiry, and to place at his disposal all the information which he has collected. Instead of doing this, the Chinese authorities have ignored him completely, and have conducted their investigation in such a way as to make it impossible for any foreigner to obtain access to the facts. The result is that the inquiry has been a farce from beginning to end, and that the Chinese Government has failed to convince anyone of its sincerity.

investigation, was the last man who ought to have been intrusted, without adequate safeguards, to conduct the search.

Not unless Nanking feels that it can safely affront the British Government, will any findings which do not disclose the facts regarding Mr. Thornburn's disappearance be transmitted to H.M.'s Minister at Nanking. If, however, the Chinese Government is determined to identify itself with a policy of blindness and evasion, and to let the matter drop their own way, it is probable that action is being taken which will encourage the continuation of affronting a great white Power.

What Should Be Done
I trust that in the event of a reply on the lines here predicted being sent to the British Legation, he will immediately return it to the Waichiaopu as unacceptable, and that he will be instructed by the British Foreign Office to withdraw from China until the Chinese Government is ready to give proof of its goodwill and good-faith.

In the meantime, in my opinion, no time should be lost in publishing, in the form of a White Paper, all the evidence relating to Mr. Thornburn's disappearance which can properly be disclosed by the British Authorities. The case has attracted worldwide attention. And if the Chinese Government is unable to "carry out the ordinary obligations of a civilized State" the truth should be given the widest possible publicity in such a form as to leave no doubt regarding the position.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1931年8月17日，星期一

索恩伯恩调查案。
又一出闹剧。
H. G. W. 伍德黑德（H. G. W. Woodhead），C.M.G. 著

过去几天，中文报纸反复报道称，受蒋介石将军委托负责对新近失踪的约翰·索恩伯恩（John Thornburn）一案进行新调查的陆军次长陈仪将军，在苏州和昆山逗留两三天后已返回南京，并报告称未能发现有关这名失踪英国人被捕及其随后遭遇的任何证据。

周五来自南京的一则路透社消息证实了这一报道，该消息称陈仪将军的调查已接近尾声，其向外交部的报告将不会为该案提供更多线索。

一项不可能完成的任务
在该报告得到官方确认之前，我不愿相信中国政府会犯下如此严重的愚蠢错误，即任命[原文如此，意指让英国政府接受其调查结果]。可以推测，蒋介石将军意在进行一次彻底调查，并将此任务委托给所能找到的最负责任的军事官员。但迄今为止，甚至连假装调查的样子都没有。如果基于陈仪将军迄今所做之事发布一份报告，那么从总统往下，中国政府的诚意将受到严重质疑。

无英国方面参与
英国领事馆官员 A. L. 斯科特先生对索恩伯恩失踪案进行了详尽调查，这已不是秘密；他获得了大量证据，“毫无疑问地证实索恩伯恩先生……被捕并被移交给中国军事当局，后者出于某种原因让知晓事实的证人保持沉默。”这段引文出自英国外交部在下议院所作的声明。

因此，如果中国政府真的希望阐明索恩伯恩先生失踪之谜，其第一步本应是邀请斯科特先生出席调查，并向他提供其所收集的所有信息。然而，中国当局完全无视了他，并以一种使任何外国人都无法接触事实真相的方式进行了调查。结果是，这次调查从头到尾都是一场闹剧，中国政府未能让任何人相信其诚意。

[此处原文似乎有缺漏或排版错误，接下文] ……调查，是最不应该在没有充分保障措施的情况下被委以搜寻重任的人。

除非南京方面认为可以安全地冒犯英国政府，否则任何未披露索恩伯恩先生失踪相关事实的调查结论都不会递交给英国驻南京公使。然而，如果中国政府决心奉行盲目和逃避的政策，并以自己的方式让此事不了了之，那么很可能正在采取的行动将助长继续冒犯一个白色大国的风气。

应当怎么做
我深信，如果英国公使馆收到符合上述预测的回复，他应立即将其退回外交部，表示不可接受；并且他将接到英国外交部的指示，撤离中国，直到中国政府准备好证明其善意和诚信为止。

与此同时，我认为应不失时机地以白皮书的形式，公布英国当局可以适当披露的、与索恩伯恩先生失踪有关的所有证据。此案已引起全世界的关注。如果中国政府无法“履行文明国家的普通义务”，那么就应以一种不留疑问的方式，尽可能广泛地公开真相。

（批注：Reg / Manfile / 4/8）

While he was at Soochow, General Chao Kin attended a tea party in his honour, and he was present at a review of the local garrison.
It is understood that the report to the Foreign Office will throw no further light on the case, nor indeed add anything material to the previous Chinese official report. out Result
The second Chinese official in-
vestigation of the Thorburn
mystery has been completed,
according to a Chinese report re-
ceived in Shanghai from Nanking
yesterday, which states that Gen-
eral Cheng Yih, Vice-Minister of
War, has completed his inquiries
at Quinsan and Soochow and re-
turned to the capital to render his
report to the Ministry of Foreign
Affairs.
General Cheng is alleged to have
told press representatives at Nan-
king that he commenced his inves-
tigation by questioning numerous
railway guards along the line from
Nanking to Quinsan, all of whom
denied knowledge of the missing
British youth.
Some of them admitted know-
ledge of the skirmish between
railway guards and a gang of
bandits wherein two guards were
killed. But they denied any know-
ledge of a Russian or foreigner
being involved in that affair.
While in Soochow, General Cheng
interrogated military and civil
officials, but without discovering
any information which might
throw light on the mystery.
In Soochow he learned from the
military authorities that on the
morning of June 2 a gang of rail-
way bandits was active in the
vicinity of Quinsan and that in-
structions were issued to the rail-
way guards to exercise extra
precautions.
The guards eventually came into
conflict with a gang and sustained
casualties after being ambushed.
A report of this incident appear-
ing in the Chinese press at Shang-
hai implicated a Russian in the
shooting, but investigation of it
failed to connect Thorburn with the
affair in any way.

索恩伯恩案
第二次调查
陆军次长
无功而返
据昨日从南京发往上海的一份中文报道，针对索恩伯恩谜案的第二次中国官方调查已经结束。该报道称，陆军次长成义将军已完成在昆山和苏州的调查，并返回首都向外交部提交报告。
据称，成将军在南京告诉新闻界代表，他通过讯问南京至昆山沿线的大量铁路警卫开始了调查，这些警卫均否认认识这名失踪的英国青年。
其中一些人承认知道铁路警卫与一伙匪徒之间发生的 skirmish（小规模冲突），其中两名警卫丧生。但他们否认有任何俄罗斯人或外国人卷入该事件。
在苏州期间，成将军讯问了军方和文职官员，但未发现任何有助于解开谜团的信息。
在苏州，他从军方获悉，6月2日上午，一伙铁路匪徒在昆山附近活动，当局已向铁路警卫发出指令，要求格外警惕。
警卫最终与一伙匪徒发生冲突，并在遭到伏击后出现伤亡。
上海中文报纸上关于此事件的报道牵连到一名俄罗斯人参与了枪击，但对此事的调查未能将索恩伯恩与该事件以任何方式联系起来。
