THE SHANGHAI SUNDAY TIMES, AUGUST 9, 1931.

THORBURN MURDER
WAS DENIED

Chinese Press Report Of
Finding Missing Man
Is Denied

RETROSPECTIVE INTEREST
OF CHINESE PRESS

Interest in the Thorburn case
was revived in the Chinese press
yesterday with the publication of
a report in one of the local
papers, which stated that Mr.
Thorburn's body had been found
at a place near Mukden. The
report further stated that the
body had been identified by
certain persons who had seen it.
The report caused considerable
excitement in Chinese circles,
and inquiries were made at various
official sources as to its truth.
It was, however, officially denied
by the authorities.

Officially Denied

"Absolutely groundless," is how
Mr. T. C. Chao, Chief Secretary
of the local office, described the
report. How and where the
Chinese newspapers got hold of
such a report, Mr. Chao was at
a loss to understand. "Even if
the Foreign Ministry had received
such information," declared Mr.
Chao, "it could not release such
information piecemeal until the
matter had thoroughly been
investigated, in view of the gravity
of the affair."

Dr. B. T. Wang, Nationalist
Minister for Foreign Affairs, at
present in Shanghai, who has had
several conferences with Sir Miles
Lampson, British Minister to
China, with regard to the Thor-
burn mystery and its ramifications,
also heard nothing of the
discovery reported by the Chinese
press, the Consul-General also
stated.

A letter has been addressed to
the editor of the paper in question
by the British Consulate-General
in Nanking, requesting him to
forward to Nanking the information alleg-
ed by the paper in question. The
editor of the paper is advised to
publish a retraction of the report.

Nanking Inquiries

NANKING, Aug. 8.—Inquiries
made here this morning at both
the Foreign Office and at the
British Consulate fail to get
confirmation of reports in the
Shanghai Chinese newspapers
that the body of Mr. John Thor-
burn had been found at Moukden.
—Reuter.

索恩伯恩谋杀案
系属谣传

中文报刊关于
发现失踪者尸体的报道
被否认

中文报刊的
回顾性关注

昨日，当地一家报纸刊登了一则报道，称索恩伯恩（Thorburn）先生的尸体已在沈阳附近某地被发现，这使得中文报刊对索恩伯恩案的兴趣重新燃起。该报道还称，尸体已由某些目击者辨认。此报道在华界引起了相当大的轰动，各方人士向各官方渠道查询其真实性。然而，当局已正式予以否认。

官方否认

本地办事处首席秘书赵先生（Mr. T. C. Chao）形容该报道“毫无根据”。赵先生表示，他不明白中文报纸是从何处获得此类报道的。赵先生宣称：“即使外交部收到了此类信息，鉴于事态严重，在彻底调查之前，也不能零星发布此类信息。”

目前在上海的国民政府外交部长王正廷博士（Dr. B. T. Wang）曾就索恩伯恩谜案及其牵连问题与英国驻华公使蓝普森爵士（Sir Miles Lampson）举行多次会谈，他也未听闻中文报刊所报道的发现之事，总领事亦如是陈述。

英国驻南京总领事馆已致函涉事报纸编辑，要求他将该报所称的信息转寄至南京。建议该报编辑刊登更正声明，撤回该报道。

南京方面的查询

南京，8月8日电。——今晨在此间向外务部及英国领事馆进行的查询，均未能证实上海中文报纸关于约翰·索恩伯恩（John Thorburn）先生尸体在奉天（Moukden）被发现的报道。——路透社。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SATURDAY, AUGUST 8, 1931

NEW DEVELOPMENT IN THE
THORBURN CASE

Gen. Chiang Kai-shek Orders Another
and Thorough Investigation

INSTRUCTIONS FROM NANCHANG

Searching Inquiry Ordered Into Mystery
of Missing British Youth

THE "North-China Daily News" is reliably informed, on advices received late last night from Nanking, that President Chiang Kai-shek has issued orders from Nanchang for another and thorough investigation into the circumstances of the disappearance of Mr. Jeff Thorburn, in the light of the further representations made to the Chinese Government by Sir Miles Lampson at Nanking.

It is understood that the President's orders are of the most definite kind and call firmly for a most searching investigation. This is the outcome of the personal efforts which Sir Miles Lampson has been making since his arrival at Nanking by air from Peitaiho on July 28.

There have been conversations between Sir Miles and Dr. C. T. Wang who have discussed the matter at great length. Some difficulty was created by the absence of General Chiang Kai-shek in Kiangsi, where he has been engaged in personally directing the campaign against the rebel Communist armies. General Chiang Kai-shek was, however, apprised at Nanchang of the British Government's views on the reply sent by the Chinese Government on July 16 to the representations made in June by the British Minister on the subject of Mr. Thorburn's whereabouts.

It will be recalled that Mr. Henderson on July 27 instructed Sir Miles Lampson to point out that an independent inquiry had established beyond reasonable doubt that Mr. Thorburn, who was under suspicion in some quarters of having shot and fatally wounded two Chinese gendarmes, had been arrested and handed over to the Chinese military authority, who had found means to silence witnesses with a knowledge of the facts. It was therefore the first duty of the Chinese Government firstly to discover Mr. Thorburn's whereabouts and to hand him over to the British authorities if he was still alive, and secondly suitably to punish any military authorities responsible for maltreating him or causing his death.

The instructions ended with a strong request to the Chinese Government "with all expedition to find means of persuading the military authorities concerned of the urgent necessity of enabling the Chinese Government to carry out the ordinary obligations of a civilised state."

These instructions have been in discussion between Sir Miles and Dr. C. T. Wang since July 28. Communication was established with General Chiang Kai-shek. The result is now seen in the order for the new and more thorough inquiry.

《字林西报》，1931年8月8日，星期六

索恩伯恩案的
新进展

蒋介石将军命令进行
另一次彻底调查

来自南昌的指示

下令对失踪英国青年之谜
进行深入调查

据《字林西报》从南京于昨晚深夜收到的消息可靠获悉，鉴于蓝普森爵士（Sir Miles Lampson）在南京向中国政府提出的进一步交涉，蒋介石主席已从南昌发出命令，要求对杰夫·索恩伯恩（Jeff Thorburn）先生失踪的情况进行另一次彻底调查。

据悉，主席的命令性质极为明确，坚决要求进行最深入的调查。这是蓝普森爵士自7月28日从北戴河乘飞机抵达南京以来一直亲自努力的结果。

蓝普森爵士与王正廷博士（Dr. C. T. Wang）之间进行了会谈，双方对此事进行了 lengthy 讨论。由于蒋介石将军身在江西，亲自指挥围剿叛乱共产党军队的战役，造成了一些困难。然而，蒋介石将军在南昌获悉了英国政府对中方政府7月16日就英国公使6月关于索恩伯恩先生下落问题所作交涉而发出的回复所持的看法。

需指出的是，亨德森先生（Mr. Henderson）于7月27日指示蓝普森爵士指出，一项独立调查已毫无疑问地证实，索恩伯恩先生因涉嫌枪击并致命伤害两名中国宪兵而被捕，并被移交给中国军事当局，后者已设法让知晓事实的证人保持沉默。因此，中国政府的首要责任是：第一，查明索恩伯恩先生的下落，如果他还活着，将其移交给英国当局；第二，适当惩罚任何对其施虐或导致其死亡的军事当局责任人。

这些指示最后强烈请求中国政府“迅速设法说服有关军事当局，使其认识到让中国政府履行文明国家通常义务的紧迫必要性”。

自7月28日以来，蓝普森爵士与王正廷博士一直在讨论这些指示。已与蒋介石将军建立联系。现在下达新的更彻底调查的命令即是这一过程的结果。

（批注：请归档 M.S. 8:8:'31）

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SATURDAY, AUGUST 8, 1931

Another Thorburn Inquiry
The news that the President of the National Government has ordered another and most searching investigation into the circumstances surrounding the disappearance of Mr. John Thorburn, shows that Sir Miles Lampson's presentation of the British Government's firm but friendly request to General Chiang Kai-shek has borne fruit. The Chinese Government have acted with prudent recognition of the justice of the contentions, put forward on the basis of the consular investigations, thus deciding to call for a further examination of the case. It is to be hoped that conditions will favour a prompt inquiry, for there seems, on the face of it, little reason for delay as the accumulation of material evidence has been steadily proceeding. No doubt, the British Government and the public behind them will recognise the correctness of the Chinese Government's response to Sir Miles Lampson's latest revelations. There will be every readiness to give the new investigators a fair field and to await their report accordingly.

另一次索恩伯恩调查

国民政府主席下令对约翰·索恩伯恩先生失踪周围的情况进行另一次最深入调查的消息表明，蓝普森爵士向蒋介石将军提出英国政府坚定但友好的请求已取得成果。中国政府审慎地承认了基于领事调查所提出的主张的公正性，从而决定要求对此案进行进一步审查。希望局势有利于迅速进行调查，因为表面上看，几乎没有理由拖延，物质证据的积累一直在稳步进行。毫无疑问，英国政府及其背后的公众将认可中国政府对蓝普森爵士最新披露内容作出的回应是正确的。各方将完全愿意给予新调查人员公平的调查空间，并据此等待他们的报告。

《时事新报》刊登了以下来自南京的电报：-

外交部收到其上海办事处的一份报告，称名为索恩伯恩的失踪英国公民的尸体已在苏州被发现，但其死因不明。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SATURDAY, AUGUST 8, 1931

PRESIDENT'S INTEREST IN THE
THORBURN CASE

Chiang Kai-shek Orders Another
and Thorough Investigation

INSTRUCTIONS FROM NANCHANG

Searching Inquiry Ordered Into Mystery
of Missing British Youth

The "North-China Daily News" is reliably informed, on
advices received late last night from Nanking, that
President Chiang Kai-shek has issued orders from Nanchang
for another and thorough investigation into the circumstances
of the disappearance of Mr. John Thorburn, in the light of the
representations made to the Chinese Government by Sir
Miles Lampson at Nanking.

It is understood that the President's orders are of the most
emphatic kind and call loudly for a most searching investigation.
In view of the evidence of the personal interest which Sir Miles
Lampson has been taking since his arrival at Nanking by air
from Shanghai on July 29.

There have been conversations
between Sir Miles and Dr. C. T.
Wang who have discussed the
matter in great detail. Some
difficulty was created by the
absence of General Chiang Kai-
shek in Kiangsi, where he has
been engaged in personally direct-
ing the campaign against the Red
Communist armies. General Chiang
Kai-shek was, however, apprised at
Nanchang of the British Govern-
ment's views in the early part of
July by the representations made in
this regard by the British Minister on
the occasion of Mr. Thorburn's
disappearance.

It will be recalled that Mr.
Henderson on July 27 instructed
Sir Miles Lampson to point out
that an independent inquiry had
established beyond reasonable
doubt that Mr. Thorburn, who was
under suspicion in some quarters
of having shot and fatally wound-
ed two Chinese gendarmes, had
been arrested and handed over to a
Chinese military authority, who
had found means to silence wit-
nesses with a knowledge of the
facts. It was therefore the first
duty of the Chinese Government
firstly to discover Mr. Thorburn's
whereabouts and to hand him over
to the British authorities if he was
still alive, and secondly suitably to
punish any military authorities
responsible for maltreating him or
causing his death.

The discussions ended with a
strong request to the Chinese Gov-
ernment with all expedition to
find means of tracing the
military authority concerned of
the arrest, detention, of enabling the
Chinese Government to carry out
the ordinary obligations of a
civilised state.

These instructions have been in
discussion between Sir Miles and
Dr. C. T. Wang since July 28.
Communication was established
with General Chiang Kai-shek.
The result is now seen in the or-
der for the new and more thorough
inquiry.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》，1931年8月8日，星期六

总统对
索恩伯恩案的关注

蒋介石命令进行
另一次彻底调查

来自南昌的指示

下令对失踪英国青年之谜
进行深入调查

据《字林西报》从南京于昨晚深夜收到的消息可靠获悉，鉴于蓝普森爵士（Sir Miles Lampson）在南京向中国政府提出的交涉，蒋介石主席已从南昌发出命令，要求对约翰·索恩伯恩（John Thorburn）先生失踪的情况进行另一次彻底调查。

据悉，主席的命令性质极为强调，强烈要求进行最深入的调查。鉴于蓝普森爵士自7月29日从上海乘飞机抵达南京以来一直表现出个人关注的证据。

蓝普森爵士与王正廷博士（Dr. C. T. Wang）之间进行了会谈，双方对此事进行了详细讨论。由于蒋介石将军身在江西，亲自指挥围剿红色共产党军队的战役，造成了一些困难。然而，蒋介石将军在南昌于7月上旬获悉了英国政府的看法，这是由英国公使就索恩伯恩先生失踪一事在此方面提出的交涉所致。

需指出的是，亨德森先生（Mr. Henderson）于7月27日指示蓝普森爵士指出，一项独立调查已毫无疑问地证实，索恩伯恩先生因涉嫌枪击并致命伤害两名中国宪兵而被捕，并被移交给中国军事当局，后者已设法让知晓事实的证人保持沉默。因此，中国政府的首要责任是：第一，查明索恩伯恩先生的下落，如果他还活着，将其移交给英国当局；第二，适当惩罚任何对其施虐或导致其死亡的军事当局责任人。

讨论结束时，强烈请求中国政府迅速设法追踪负责逮捕、拘留的有关军事当局，以使中国政府能够履行文明国家的通常义务。

自7月28日以来，蓝普森爵士与王正廷博士一直在讨论这些指示。已与蒋介石将军建立联系。现在下达新的更彻底调查的命令即是这一过程的结果。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, AUGUST 1, 1931
F. 8. 31.

Unjust To Blame China For
Thorburn, Says Dr. Wang

Mr. Sheng, Foreign Office Man Who Went To Soochow
To Investigate, Reported Killed By Truck;
Last Piece Of Evidence Obliterated

NANKING, July 31.—Sir Miles
Lampson, British Minister to
China, called on Dr. C. T. Wang,
Minister for Foreign Affairs, on
Wednesday afternoon in regard to
the case of John Thorburn.

Sir Miles conveyed the British
Government's strong protest, together with a request that the
Chinese Government discover the
whereabouts of young Thorburn
and hand him over to the British
authorities, if he is still alive, or,
if he is dead, that suitable punishment should be meted out to the
military authorities responsible.

Dr. Wang's Attitude

It is understood that the attitude adopted by Dr. C. T. Wang
is, briefly, as follows:

"Mr. Thorburn is a British subject living in a Foreign Concession—Shanghai. As far as the
Chinese authorities are concerned
his existence was unknown. When
he left Shanghai for an unknown
destination, he obtained no passport from the Chinese Government. It is, therefore, unjust to lay
the entire blame of anything that
may have happened to him on the
Chinese Government."

It is announced that Mr. Sheng,
the representative of the Foreign
Office, who, together with a representative of the War Office, went
to Soochow to investigate the case
some weeks ago, died on July 27
as the result of injuries received
by being run down by a truck.
He died of concussion of the brain.
The only piece of evidence that
might have been obtained from
the only Chinese civil official who
investigated the Thorburn case is
no longer available.—Reuter.

（批：1/8/31）

《上海泰晤士报》，1931年8月1日，星期六
F. 8. 31.

王博士称因索恩伯恩案
指责中国是不公正的

前往苏州调查的外交部官员盛先生
据报道被卡车撞死；
最后一件证据被抹去

南京，7月31日电。——英国驻华公使蓝普森爵士（Sir Miles Lampson）于周三下午拜访了外交部长王正廷博士（Dr. C. T. Wang），商谈约翰·索恩伯恩（John Thorburn）一案。

蓝普森爵士传达了英国政府的强烈抗议，并请求中国政府查明年轻索恩伯恩的下落，如果他还活着，将其移交给英国当局；或者，如果他已死亡，则对负责的军事当局给予适当的惩罚。

王博士的态度

据悉，王正廷博士采取的态度简要如下：

“索恩伯恩先生是居住在上海外国租界内的英国臣民。就中国当局而言，他的存在不为人知。当他离开上海前往一个未知的目的地时，他并未从中国政府获得护照。因此，将可能发生在他身上的任何事情的全部责任归咎于中国政府是不公正的。”

据宣布，数周前与军政部代表一同前往苏州调查此案的外交部代表盛先生，于7月27日因被卡车撞伤致死。他死于脑震荡。唯一可能从调查索恩伯恩案的唯一中国文职官员那里获得的证据已不再可得。——路透社。

（批注：1/8/31）
（手写签名：J de M）

NO FURTHER LIGHT ON
THORBURN CASE
H. M.'s Minister's Move-
ments At Nanking
Undisclosed
No fresh light was thrown upon
the Thorburn case yesterday,
either by official or other sources.
The British Consul-General, Mr.
J. F. Brennan, questioned with re-
gard to a report allegedly em-
anating from Nanking wherein
Dr. C. T. Wang, Nationalist Mini-

provide himself with this docu-
ment which, according to the
Nationalist Minister, would have
advised the Chinese authorities of
his intention to pass through
Chinese territory and gained for
him a measure of protection.
The report concludes by saying
that "the responsible authorities,
not having been acquainted with
Thorburn's intentions, could not
possibly hold themselves respons-

《上海泰晤士报》，1931年8月1日，星期六

索恩伯恩案
再无新线索

英王陛下公使
在南京的行踪
未予披露

昨日，无论是官方还是其他来源，均未就索恩伯恩案提供新的线索。英国总领事布伦南先生（Mr. J. F. Brennan）就被问及一则据称发自南京的报道时声明，他无可奉告。该报道声称，国民政府外交部长王正廷博士指责索恩伯恩在没有“护照”（huchao，即内地通行证）的情况下进入中国领土。

根据这则报道，中国当局认为，索恩伯恩未能提供这份文件，从而承担了不必要的风险；据这位国民政府部长称，这份文件本可以告知中国当局他穿越中国领土的意图，并为他提供一定程度的保护。

报道最后称，“负责当局因不了解索恩伯恩的意图，不可能对他的行动承担责任。”
（批注：8/1/31）

THE CHINA PRESS FRIDAY, JULY 31, 1931

Thorburn Without
Huchao, Declares
Foreign Ministry

Waichiaopu Defends By
Saying Journey
Illegal

(Special To The China Press)
NANKING, July 30.—Sir Miles Lampson, the British minister to China, had a lengthy conversation with Dr. C. T. Wang, minister of foreign affairs, yesterday immediately upon his arrival by airplane from Peiping. Sir Miles, in the course of the conversation, is understood to have handed to Dr. Wang a memorandum on the Thorburn case.
Replying to the British minister's note today, the Foreign Ministry in a communication is said to have pointed out that according to the regular procedure, foreigners intending to travel in the interior of China must first obtain the necessary "huchao" so that the responsible authorities can notify beforehand the various local authorities through whose territory the traveler is expected to go in order that proper protection can be provided.
Mr. Thorburn, the ministry's reply is reported to have pointed out, failed to observe the required procedure. Moreover, the responsible authorities had not been acquainted with his intentions and therefore could not possibly hold themselves responsible for his movements.

No Lampson Report
(Reuter's Service)
LONDON, July 29.—Questioned in House of Commons today the Under-Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs, Dr. Hugh Dalton, said that in view of the interest, very rightly and naturally, taken in the Thorburn case, he was sure Foreign Secretary Arthur Henderson, would give publicity to any communication received from Sir Miles Lampson, the British minister to China, during the Parliamentary recess.
Dr. Dalton added that no further reports had been expected from Sir Miles Lampson for some days in view of the fact that General Chiang Kai-shek was at present conducting military operations in Kiangsi.

外交部宣称：
索本无护照

外交部辩护称
其行程非法

（《字林西报》专讯）
南京，7月30日电。——英国驻华公使蓝普森爵士（Sir Miles Lampson）昨日乘飞机从北平抵达后，立即与外交部长王正廷博士进行了 lengthy 谈话。据悉，蓝普森爵士在谈话过程中向王博士递交了一份关于索本案的备忘录。
据称，外交部今日在回复英国公使的照会中指出，按照常规程序，拟在中国内地旅行的外国人必须首先取得必要的“护照”（huchao），以便主管当局预先通知旅行者预计途经各地的地方当局，从而提供适当的保护。
据称，外交部的回复指出，索本先生未能遵守规定的程序。此外，主管当局并不知晓其意图，因此不可能对其行动负责。

暂无蓝普森报告
（路透社服务）
伦敦，7月29日电。——今日在下议院被问及此事时，外交部次官休·道尔顿博士（Dr. Hugh Dalton）表示，鉴于人们对索本案表现出非常正当且自然的兴趣，他确信外交大臣阿瑟·亨德森（Arthur Henderson）将在议会休会期间公布从英国驻华公使蓝普森爵士处收到的任何信函。
道尔顿博士补充说，鉴于蒋介石将军目前正在江西进行军事行动，预计未来几天内不会收到蓝普森爵士的进一步报告。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, FRIDAY, JULY 31, 1931

Thorburn Publicity Is
Promised By Dr. Dalton
During Commons Recess

Under-Secretary Says He Feels Sure That Mr. Arthur
Henderson Will Disclose Any Communication
Received From Sir Miles Lampson

SIX BRITISH SUBJECTS DIE WHILE IN
CAPTIVITY DURING PAST 3 YEARS

LONDON, July 29.—Questioned in the House of Com-
mons to-day, Dr. Hugh Dalton, Under-Secretary of State for
Foreign Affairs, said that in view of the interest, very
rightly and naturally, taken in the Thorburn case, he was
sure Mr. Arthur Henderson, Foreign Secretary, would give
publicity to any communication received from Sir Miles
Lampson, British Minister to China, during the Parliament-
ary recess.
Dr. Dalton added that no fur-
ther news had been expected
from Sir Miles Lampson for some
days in view of the fact that
General Chiang Kai-shek was at
present conducting military oper-
ations in Kiangsi.—Reuter.

BRITISH MINISTER
SEES DR. WANG

Nature Of Conversation
Unrevealed By Local
Authorities

Although no official statement
was made by local British consular
authorities yesterday regarding
movements of the British Minister
to China, now in Nanking in con-
nection with the Thorburn inquiry,
it was learned that Sir Miles
Lampson had already conferred
with Dr. C. T. Wang, Nationalist
Minister of Foreign Affairs.
Sir Miles arrived at the capital
by air from Peitaiho in the early
part of this week for the special
purpose of pressing the Nanking
Government for a further inves-
tigation of the Thorburn mystery
which the press and public of
Shanghai and Great Britain have
demanded in emphatic terms.
Just what form of further in-
vestigation the British Minister is
demanding of the Nanking Gov-
ernment, cannot be ascertained at
present as no information of any
sort is being given out by local
British officials. Mr. J. F. Brenan,
British Consul-General, when ques-
tioned by a representative of this
paper stated that he had nothing
to say about Sir Miles' movements.

Two Months Ago

It is exactly two months since
John Thorburn (19), British youth,
disappeared from his home in the
French Concession, supposedly
after setting out on foot in the
direction of Nanking. The evi-
dence...

Britain's Message

LONDON, July 29.—Dr. Hugh
Dalton, Under-Secretary for For-
eign Affairs, in the House of
Commons to-day, said, "Sir Miles
Lampson, British Minister, left
Peiping yesterday morning by
aeroplane for Nanking with the
object of delivering the message
of the British Government per-
sonally to Marshal Chiang Kai-
shek."
In the message which Sir Miles
has been instructed to convey to
the Chinese Government, the
Government is urged with all de-
spatch to find means of persuad-
ing the military authorities in
whose hands Thorburn is believed
to be, of the urgent necessity of
enabling the Chinese Government
to carry out the ordinary obliga-
tions of a civilized state.
In reply to another question,
Dr. Dalton stated that six British
subjects had died in captivity in
China in the past three years.
—Reuters through Reuter.

道尔顿博士承诺
在议会休会期间
公布索本案件宣传材料

次官表示确信阿瑟·亨德森先生将披露

过去三年中
六名英国臣民
在被囚禁期间死亡

伦敦，7月29日电。——今日在下议院被问及此事时，外交部次官休·道尔顿博士表示，鉴于人们对索本案表现出非常正当且自然的兴趣，他确信外交大臣阿瑟·亨德森先生将在议会休会期间公布从英国驻华公使蓝普森爵士处收到的任何信函。
道尔顿博士补充说，鉴于蒋介石将军目前正在江西进行军事行动，预计未来几天内不会收到蓝普森爵士的进一步消息。——路透社。

英国公使
会见王博士

当地当局
未透露谈话性质

尽管当地英国领事当局昨日未就与中国索本案调查有关的英国驻华公使的行踪发表官方声明，但获悉蓝普森爵士已与国民政府外交部长王正廷博士进行了会谈。
蓝普森爵士本周初乘飞机从北戴河抵达首都，其特别目的是敦促南京政府对索本谜案进行进一步调查，上海和英国的媒体及公众已强烈要求对此进行调查。
目前尚无法确定英国公使正要求南京政府采取何种形式的进一步调查，因为当地英国官员未发布任何此类信息。英国总领事布伦南先生（Mr. J. F. Brenan）在接受本报记者询问时表示，他对蓝普森爵士的行踪无可奉告。

两月前

英国青年约翰·索本（19岁）从其法租界家中失踪，据称是步行前往南京方向，至今恰好两个月。证据……

英国的信息

伦敦，7月29日电。——外交部次官休·道尔顿博士今日在下议院表示：“英国公使蓝普森爵士昨晨乘飞机离开北平前往南京，目的是亲自向蒋介石元帅传达英国政府的信息。”
在受命传达给中国政府的信息中，敦促中国政府尽快设法说服被认为控制着索本的军事当局，使其认识到让中国政府履行文明国家通常义务的紧迫必要性。
在回答另一个问题时，道尔顿博士表示，过去三年中有六名英国臣民在中国被囚禁期间死亡。
——路透社通过路透社转发。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Thursday, July 30, 1931

Wang At Nanking
Seen By Lampson
In Thorburn Case

British Minister Pays
Visit To Foreign
Affairs Chief

CONSULATE HERE
AWAITS MESSAGE

Future Extrality Plans
May Rest On Outcome
Of Negotiations

Sir Miles Lampson, British
Minister to China, made a formal
call yesterday afternoon at the
offices of Dr. C. T. Wang, Minister
of Foreign Affairs for the National-
ist Government, and the disappear-
ance of young John Thorburn was
discussed, according to a message
received this morning from Nan-
king.

The exact nature of the discus-
sion was not revealed. The con-
versation lasted for two full hours,
it was stated, before Sir Miles and
his Chinese secretary, Mr. Eric
Teichman, departed.

Consulate Not Informed

Up to noon today no word was
received at the local British Con-
sulate-General regarding the nature
of Sir Miles' conversation with Dr.
Wang. Whether Sir Miles has made
formal demands upon the Chinese
government for punishment of
Chinese soldiers alleged to have
arrested and detained young John
Thorburn is still unknown.

Sir Miles has been instructed by
his government in London to
demand another investigation by
the Chinese in the Thorburn case.
The instructions from London
followed almost two full months
of spirited agitation on the part of
the local press for justice in young
Thorburn's disappearance.

Youth Missing 50 Days

With future extraterritoriality
negotiations possibly hanging in
the balance, interest in the Thor-
burn case has intensified this week.
This morning Mr. J. P. Brenan,
British Consul General here, paid
wearily to and fro in his office
as to the latest developments in Sir
Miles' visit.

Young John Thorburn will be
missing from Shanghai two months
tomorrow. He departed on June
1 to seek adventure, was seen at
various times near Soochow until
about June 10, after which time he
vanished. Soochow is less than 60
miles from Shanghai.

List Grows

It was announced by Mr. H. J
Andrews, a friend of the missing
youth that the international list
started last week in protest against
the inaction in the Thorburn case now
bears more than 400 signatures, re-
presenting 30 different nationalities.
Those who have not yet signed
and wish to do so will find a
circular list at the R.Y.C. Club in
the Administration Building, Pei-
how Road.

The $5,000 reward offered by The
Shanghai Evening Post and Mercury
for information leading to the
whereabouts, dead or alive, of Mr.
John Thorburn still was unclaimed
this morning.

31.7.31.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1931年7月30日，星期四

王正廷在南京
就索本案
会见蓝普森

英国公使拜访
外交部长

本地领事馆
等待消息

未来治外法权计划
可能取决于
谈判结果

据今晨从南京收到的消息，英国驻华公使蓝普森爵士昨日下午正式拜访了国民政府外交部长王正廷博士的办公室，并讨论了青年约翰·索本失踪一事。

讨论的具体性质未予透露。据悉，在蓝普森爵士及其中文秘书埃里克·泰奇曼先生（Mr. Eric Teichman）离开之前，谈话持续了整整两个小时。

领事馆未获通知

截至今日中午，本地英国总领事馆尚未收到有关蓝普森爵士与王博士谈话性质的任何消息。蓝普森爵士是否已就据称逮捕并拘留青年约翰·索本的中国士兵的惩罚问题向中国政府提出正式要求，目前仍不得而知。

伦敦政府已指示蓝普森爵士要求中方对索本案进行另一次调查。伦敦方面的指示是在本地媒体为索本青年失踪案伸张正义而进行了近两个月的激烈呼吁之后发出的。

青年失踪50天

随着未来治外法权谈判可能处于成败关键之际，本周对索本案的关注加剧。今晨，英国驻沪总领事布伦南先生（Mr. J. P. Brenan）在办公室内疲惫地来回踱步，关注蓝普森爵士访问的最新进展。

明日，青年约翰·索本离开上海将满两个月。他于6月1日出发寻求冒险，直到6月10日左右在苏州附近多次被人看见，此后便消失无踪。苏州距离上海不到60英里。

名单增加

失踪青年的朋友 H. J. 安德鲁斯先生（Mr. H. J Andrews）宣布，上周发起的抗议索本案处理不力的国际签名名单，现在已有来自30个不同国籍的400多人签名。尚未签名但希望签名者，可在北河南路行政大楼的皇家游艇俱乐部（R.Y.C. Club）找到循环签名表。

《上海晚邮报与水星报》为提供约翰·索本先生下落（无论生死）线索而提供的5,000美元赏金，今晨仍无人认领。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL
C. & S. D. REGIS. 1971
No. S. B. D. 2464
Date 31-7-31.

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, JULY 30, 1931

Thorburn Affair A Test
Case For Both China And
Britain, Declares 'Times'

LONDON CANNOT SUFFER ITS SUBJECTS
TO BE ARRESTED BY MILITARY AND
THEN DONE TO DEATH

NOTHING DOUBTFUL ABOUT FATE OF
EXTRALITY TALK, SAYS 'TELEGRAPH'

Any Abdication Of Its Duty Would Deeply Discredit
British Government In Public Opinion; Lord
Palmerston Would Not Have Temporized

LONDON, July 28.—A very indignant leading article on
the Thorburn case is published by the "Daily Telegraph"
this morning. Remarking ironically that it has taken two
months to decide that Sir Miles Lampson, British Minister,
should personally take up the case with the Chinese Govern-
ment, the paper declares that whatever reply to the British
demands may be forthcoming from General Chiang Kai-
shek, there ought to be nothing doubtful about the fate of
the preposterous diplomatic extrality proceedings which
assume Nanking's ability to carry out "the ordinary
obligations of a civilized government."

"The Times" states that before the British Government
irretrievably commits itself, it says, the least that public opinion
is entitled to expect is that it should most carefully ponder the
lessons of the Thorburn case and give consideration to the recom-
mendations of Mr. Justice Feetham.

The present system, concludes
the "Times," contains admitted
defects and anomalies which should
be abolished, but in the Treaty
Ports, and particularly in Shang-
hai, there is a nucleus of stability
which is far too important a factor
in the orderly progress of China
to be jeopardised by a Government
unable, or unwilling, to compel its
own servants to respect the law
or even to call them to account
when they have flagrantly broken
it.

The "Daily Express" remarks
that Lord Palmerston, who knew
the value of prestige in the Orient
would not have waited half as long
as Sir Miles Lampson has done.
It adds that Sir Miles Lampson
must compensate for Mr. Arthur
Henderson's tardiness by acting
with double vigour and insistence.
—Reuter.

（批：8/2 30/7/31）

日期 31-7-31.

《上海泰晤士报》，1931年7月30日，星期四

《泰晤士报》宣称：
索本案是对中国和英国
双方的考验

伦敦不能容忍其臣民
被军方逮捕并随后致死

《每日电讯报》称：
治外法权谈判的命运
毫无疑问

任何放弃职责的行为都将严重损害
英国政府在公众舆论中的信誉；帕默斯顿勋爵
绝不会拖延

伦敦，7月28日电。——《每日电讯报》今早刊登了一篇关于索本案的极为愤慨的社论。该报讽刺地评论说，花了两个月时间才决定由英国公使蓝普森爵士亲自向中国政府提出此案，并宣称，无论蒋介石将军对英国要求作出何种答复，那些荒谬的外交治外法权程序的命运不应有任何疑义，这些程序假定南京有能力履行“文明政府的通常义务”。

《泰晤士报》指出，在英国政府不可挽回地做出承诺之前，公众舆论至少有权期待政府最仔细地思考索本案的教训，并考虑费瑟姆法官（Mr. Justice Feetham）的建议。

《泰晤士报》总结道，现行制度存在公认的缺陷和异常，应予废除，但在通商口岸，特别是上海，有一个稳定的核心，这对于中国的有序进步是一个至关重要的因素，不能被一个无法或不愿强迫其下属尊重法律，甚至在其公然违法时也不追究其责任的政府所危及。

《每日快报》评论说，深知东方声望价值的帕默斯顿勋爵（Lord Palmerston）等待的时间绝不会像蓝普森爵士那样长的一半。该报补充说，蓝普森爵士必须以加倍的力度和坚持来弥补阿瑟·亨德森先生的迟缓。
——路透社。

（批注：8/2 30/7/31）

pected almost immediately.
The British Minister reached
the capital on Tuesday night by
aeroplane from Peiping where he
was on summer vacation. The
urgency of the Thorburn case
caused this to be cut short, how-
ever, on instructions received from

No statement could be made

that he had reached Nanking. The
Minister, it is understood, intends
making direct representations to
General Chiang Kai-shek in a
further effort to solve the mystery
of the disappearance of John
Thorburn, 19-year-old British youth
missing from his home in Shang-
hai for two months.

Agitation locally for official
action in the matter has tem-
porarily subsided since news of the
Minister's movements has reached
the city, although interest in the
case is believed to have been
heightened rather than to have
diminished, in spite of lack of out-
ward evidence of same.

几乎立即受到期待。
英国公使于周二晚间乘飞机从北平抵达首都，他此前正在那里度暑假。然而，据信由于收到本国政府的指示，索本案的紧迫性导致假期缩短。

Le Journal de Shanghai.
dated July 30, 1931.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / C. & S. B. REGISTRY / No. S. B. D. 2464 / date 31/7/31）

The case of Thorburn and its reflections.

Our contemporary The North Chin a Daily News
published yesterday once again details in connection
with the case of Thorburn. The young Englishman was seen
in Soochow on June 10 by a witness at about dusk. He was
in a pitiful state, wounded, covered with blood, and his
hands tied at the back, pushed by soldiers who appeared
to be conducting him to a place from which there is no return.
(Here follows an extract on the subject from the "North China
Daily News" ).
Despite the negative result of an enquiry conducted
by the Nanking Government nobody doubts any longer that
the young Thorburn had been arrested by the soldiers of
Soochow garrison, was tortured by them and very possibly
executed under circumstances which we are ignorant of
but which it would be interesting to know.
We think that the officials of Waichiaopu are persons
of too much intelligence to believe that the report of
the enquiry commission appointed by the Ministry of Foreign
Affairs and the War Ministry, is correct. It is probable
that upon learning of the execution of Thorburn by the
soldiers, the enquiry commission decided to throw a thick
veil on the whole of this affair in order to hide from the
world the real situation in China, which official representatives
of Nanking Government abroad describe as a country where
law is respected, where good order prevails, and where
extraterritoriality is to all appearances an anomaly..
Leaders of the Anglo-Saxon nations have since many
months now been conducting negotiations on the subject of
extraterritoriality. In obedience to certain reasons
of opportunism which we shall refrain from discussing, or
in support of certain influences, which we shall not comment
upon or pass judgment on, they were showing a spirit of
accommodating conciliation to a great extent, Never before
were there so many missionaries and foreigners arrested,
carried away or massacred in China as within the past
two three years, nevertheless the renunciation to special
foreign rights in interior provinces, that is to say,
logically, where the situation is practically the same
to-day as when these rights were granted, continued to
be discussed. It would seem as if one was fascinated
by Nanking, where the Government had assembled numerous
intelligent and educated officials and established a
modern administration. What does it matter that a few
hours away from Nanking the situation was quite different,
the capital alone mattered together with the distinguished
men who were preparing a future there. The discussions
were inclined to treat the future as reality.
When news was received that in Hounan, Kiangsi, Hupeh
and Nganhoei, bandits and communists had been arresting
or killing missionaries, it was sufficient to deplore these
sad incidents.
The case of Thorburn, by its reflections abroad, has
brought about the effect of a thunderbolt. The veil which
concealed the truth has been torn apart. It is only 40
kilometres from Shanghai that the military authorities

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处 / 刑事与特别 bureau 登记处 / 编号 S. B. D. 2464 / 日期 31/7/31）

索伯恩案及其反响。

本报同行《字林西报》昨日再次刊登了有关索伯恩案的详细报道。6月10日黄昏时分，一名目击者在苏州看到了这位年轻的英国人。他处境凄惨，身负重伤，浑身是血，双手被反绑在背后，由几名士兵推搡着，这些士兵似乎正将他带往一个有去无回的地方。
（以下是《字林西报》关于此事的摘录）。
尽管南京政府的调查得出了否定的结果，但如今已无人怀疑，年轻的索伯恩已被苏州驻军士兵逮捕，遭受他们的酷刑，并极有可能在某种我们尚不知情、但若知晓将颇具意义的情形下被处决。
我们认为，外交部官员的智慧足以让他们不相信由外交部和陆军部委派的调查委员会的报告是正确的。很可能，当调查委员会得知索伯恩被士兵处决后，决定对整个事件严加遮掩，以便向世人隐瞒中国的真实状况，而南京政府在海外的官方代表却将中国描述为一个尊重法律、秩序井然、且治外法权表面上看来是一种异常现象的国家。
盎格鲁-撒克逊国家的领导人数月来一直在就治外法权问题进行谈判。出于某些我们将不予讨论的权宜之计原因，或为了支持某些我们将不予评论或评判的影响因素，他们表现出极大的通融与和解精神。过去两三年间，在中国被捕、被带走或被屠杀的传教士和外国人之多，前所未有，然而，放弃内地省份的特殊外国权利——也就是说，逻辑上讲，在这些权利授予时与今日局势几乎相同的地方——的讨论仍在继续。人们似乎被南京迷住了，那里政府聚集了许多聪明且受过教育的官员，并建立了现代化的行政体系。距离南京仅几小时路程的地方局势截然不同，这又有什么关系呢？重要的是首都本身，以及在那里筹备未来的杰出人物。讨论倾向于将未来当作现实来对待。
当收到湖南、江西、湖北和安徽的匪徒和共产党人逮捕或杀害传教士的消息时，人们仅仅对这些悲惨事件表示惋惜。
索伯恩案因其在国外引起的反响，产生了如晴天霹雳般的效果。掩盖真相的面纱已被撕开。就在距离上海仅40公里的地方，军事当局

page_data.en:

subjected directly to the Central Government have
violated international conventions and ignored the
authority of the Nanking Government. Furthermore,
this same Government, which, we are certain, is the
first to deplore the excesses of the Soochow garrison
soldiers, did not, however dare to deal vigorously
with the guilty military and attempted to pass the affair
by in silence, thinking that the foreign opinion would
get tired and would end up by finding other interests.
Bad reckoning; the truth has emerged in spite of everything.
The result of all this is that the Anglo-Saxon
countries are now talking of showing themselves less
inclined to be conciliatory in the matter of extraterritoriality.
And really speaking, when one considers that the military
are in a position to oppose the Government, and to prevent
the functioning of a judicial body by intimidating witnesses,
the question naturally arises what will be the fate of
foreigners when the abolition of extraterritoriality
will have delivered them to the mercy of uncultured,
brutal and unscrupulous soldiers.
G.M.

这一切的结果是，盎格鲁-撒克逊国家现在表示，在治外法权问题上不太愿意采取和解态度。确实，考虑到军队有能力对抗政府，并通过恐吓证人阻碍司法机构的运作，人们自然会产生疑问：一旦废除治外法权，将外国人交由未开化、残暴且肆无忌惮的士兵摆布，他们的命运将会如何。

Thorburn case
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. & S. B. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. 2434
Date 30 7 31
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Wednesday, July 29, 1931

Lampson To Ask
Troops Punished
Demand Will Be Filed
With Fresh Protest,
Officials State

Responding quickly to the orders
of the British Foreign Office in
London demanding a further in-
vestigation on the part of the Na-
tionalist Government in the Thor-
burn case, Sir Miles Lampson,
British Minister to China, landed
in Nanking by plane last night.

Sir Miles' holiday at Peitaiho was
ended abruptly yesterday when he
was instructed to file further pro-
test over the mysterious disap-
pearance of young John Thorburn,
19, British subject, missing from his
home in Shanghai 39 days.

Plans Uncertain

It was stated at the local British
Consulate-General this morning
that Sir Miles' plans are indefinite,
but it was considered certain that
demands would be made upon Chi-
nese authorities for punishment of
soldiers responsible for the deten-
tion or possible slaying of young
Thorburn.

Sir Miles may make a flying trip
to Nanchang to deliver his message
personally to General Chiang Kai-
shek, or else he may make his de-
mands to Dr. C. T. Wang, Minister
of Foreign Affairs.

New Evidence

Meanwhile further evidence was
uncovered in an attempt to corro-
borate the opinion expressed by pre-
vious investigators that young
Thorburn was arrested by Chinese
soldiers at Soochow.

A man now in this city, whose
identity is being kept secret has
described how he saw the youth
badly injured, in the company of
Chinese gendarmes in Soochow on
June 10. Young Thorburn was
bleeding and bound, it was charged,
being driven by Chinese soldiers to
a boat in the creek for transporta-
tion, evidently to Taihu Lake, which
is 10 miles away from Soochow.

Great Secrecy

His head and body were cut and
bleeding, it was stated. Passersby
were threatened when they attempt-
ed to approach the youth, it was
charged, and the Chinese soldiers
were taking great care to insure
secrecy in their operations.

The reward of $5,000 offered by
The Shanghai Evening Post and
Mercury for information leading to
the whereabouts of Mr. John Thor-
burn, dead or alive, still is unclaim-
ed. A board of awards will decide
the virtue of all claims and informa-
tion received will be held in strict
confidence.

索伯恩案
上海公共租界工部局警务处
刑事与特别 bureau 登记处
编号 S. B. D. 2434
日期 31年7月30日
《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1931年7月29日，星期三

兰普森将要求
惩办士兵
将与新的抗议书
一并提交诉求，
官员称

为迅速响应伦敦英国外交部要求在索伯恩案中由国民政府进行进一步调查的命令，英国驻华公使迈尔斯·兰普森爵士昨晚乘飞机抵达南京。

兰普森爵士在北戴河的假期于昨日突然结束，当时他接到指令，就19岁的英国臣民约翰·索伯恩神秘失踪一事提出进一步抗议，该青年已从其在上海的家中失踪39天。

计划未定

今晨当地英国总领事馆表示，兰普森爵士的计划尚未确定，但据信肯定会向中国当局提出要求，惩办对拘留或可能杀害年轻索伯恩负责的士兵。

兰普森爵士可能会快速飞往南昌，亲自向蒋介石将军传达信息，或者也可能向外交部长王正廷博士提出诉求。

新证据

与此同时，发现了更多证据，试图证实先前调查人员表达的观点，即年轻索伯恩在苏州被中国士兵逮捕。

目前在本市的一名身份保密的男子描述了他在6月10日于苏州看到这名青年与中国宪兵在一起时身受重伤的情景。据称，年轻的索伯恩流血不止且被捆绑，由中国士兵驱赶至小河中的一艘船上，显然是要运往距离苏州10英里的太湖。

高度保密

据称，他的头部和身体多处割伤并流血。据称，当路人试图接近该青年时受到威胁，中国士兵在行动中极力确保秘密性。

《上海晚邮报与水星报》为提供导致找到约翰·索伯恩先生下落（无论生死）的信息所提供的5,000美元赏金，仍无人认领。奖励委员会将裁定所有索赔的有效性，收到的信息将严格保密。

THE CHINA PRESS, WEDNESDAY, JULY 29, 1931

Lampson Flying
To Nanking For
Thorburn Probe

Minister To Press For
Fuller Information On
British Youth

(Reuter's Pacific Service)
PEKING, July 28.—It is understood here that Sir Miles Lampson left yesterday to air this morning for Nanking to take up the Thorburn case. He will proceed thence to see Gen. Chiang Kai-shek.

Demand Before Chiang.
(Reuter's Pacific Service)
PEKING, July 28.—The French aviator, Count de Sibour, accompanied by his wife, flew from Peiping to Paitsafio this morning with the intention of picking up Sir Miles Lampson and conveying him to Nanking. However, owing to the floods in the capital, the authorities here are doubtful whether they will be able to land in Nanking.

Decision of the British government to ask the Chinese government "with all expedition to find means of persuading the military authorities concerned of the urgent necessity of enabling the Chinese Government to carry out the ordinary obligations of a civilized state" has led Dr. Hugh Dalton, the Under-Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs to instruct Sir Miles Lampson, British Minister to China to place the demand before president Chiang Kai-shek himself.

Sir Miles will arrive with his staff at Nanking next Friday, it was announced by the local British Consulate yesterday. This has necessitated his cutting short his holiday at Peitaiho, where he has been for sometime.

The protection of the rights of British subjects in China has been renewed in the minds of members of the House of Commons as a result of the persistent publicity that has been given the case of John Thorburn, who has been missing from his home in Shanghai for 50 days. Press notices, editorials, petitions of loyal British subjects all have contributed to arousing the government of Great Britain to request their representative in China to demand action.

The special demands of the British government are that the Chinese Government find Mr. Thorburn and deliver him to British authori-

ties, punish those responsible, and then to make adequate reparation. The British Minister is also instructed to ask for an explanation of the delay in finding Mr. Thorburn and to inquire into the "lack of authority" in the areas concerned, and to appeal to him for action in the matter.

(Reuter's Telegram)
(From Our Own Correspondent)
LONDON, July 28.—In the House of Commons today, the Under Secretary for Foreign Affairs, Dr. H. Dalton, replied on behalf of the Foreign Secretary to questions concerning the disappearance of John Thorburn.

He said that Sir Miles Lampson had been instructed to make representations to the Chinese Government in the following sense: "In view of the facts which have established beyond all reasonable doubt that Thorburn, who is under suspicion by some quarters of having shot and fatally wounded two Chinese soldiers, was arrested and handed over to the custody of the military authorities, who have found him guilty after a summary trial, and that these authorities possess full knowledge of the facts.

"It is the duty of the Chinese Government in the first place to ascertain the whereabouts of Thorburn, and if he is alive, to hand him over to the civil authorities, and in any event to inflict suitable punishment on those military authorities who have been responsible for detaining him or inflicting upon him any ill-treatment. His Majesty's Government earnestly and urgently requests the Chinese Government to use its best endeavours to find means of persuading the military authorities concerned of the present urgent necessity of enabling the Chinese Government to carry out the ordinary obligations of a civilized state."

He added that Sir Miles Lampson had been instructed to convey the foregoing communication personally from the British Government and to ask for an early reply. He proposed to raise the matter again if no satisfactory answer was received within a reasonable time.

《大美晚报》，1931年7月29日，星期三

兰普森飞赴
南京调查
索伯恩案

公使将敦促获取
关于英国青年的
更完整信息

（路透社太平洋分社）
北平，7月28日电。——据悉，迈尔斯·兰普森爵士已于昨日离开，今晨乘飞机前往南京处理索伯恩案。他将随后前往会见蒋介石将军。

向蒋介石提出诉求。
（路透社太平洋分社）
北平，7月28日电。——法国飞行员西布尔伯爵（Count de Sibour）在其夫人陪同下，今晨从北平飞往北戴河，意图接上迈尔斯·兰普森爵士并将其送往南京。然而，由于首都洪水泛滥，当地当局怀疑他们是否能在南京降落。

英国政府决定要求中国政府“尽快设法说服相关军事当局，使其认识到让中国政府履行文明国家通常义务的紧迫必要性”，这一决定导致外交部次长休·道尔顿博士指示英国驻华公使迈尔斯·兰普森爵士亲自向蒋介石主席提出该诉求。

当地英国领事馆昨日宣布，兰普森爵士及其随员将于下周五抵达南京。这迫使他缩短了在北戴河已停留一段时间的假期。

由于约翰·索伯恩案持续受到宣传，他从上海家中失踪已达50天，保护在华英国臣民权利的问题再次引起下议院成员的关注。新闻报导、社论、忠诚英国臣民的请愿书，都促使英国政府要求其驻华代表采取行动。

英国政府的特别要求是：中国政府找到索伯恩先生并将其移交给英国当局，惩办责任人，然后给予充分赔偿。英国公使还受命要求解释寻找索伯恩先生的延误原因，并调查相关地区的“缺乏权威”状况，并呼吁他在此事上采取行动。

（路透社电报）
（本报特约记者）
伦敦，7月28日电。——今日在下议院，外交部次长 H. 道尔顿博士代表外交大臣回答了有关约翰·索伯恩失踪的问题。

他表示，迈尔斯·兰普森爵士已受命向中国政府提出如下交涉：“鉴于事实已毫无疑问地确立，索伯恩被某些方面怀疑枪击并致命伤害了两名中国士兵，他被逮捕并移交给军事当局保管，后者经简易审判判定其有罪，且这些当局完全掌握事实真相。

中国政府的首要职责是查明索伯恩的下落，如果他还活着，将其移交给民事当局，并在任何情况下对负责拘留他或对他施加任何虐待的军事当局施以适当的惩罚。英王陛下政府恳切且紧急地请求中国政府尽最大努力设法说服相关军事当局，使其认识到当前让中国政府履行文明国家通常义务的紧迫必要性。”

他补充说，迈尔斯·兰普森爵士已受命亲自传达英国政府的上述照会，并要求尽早回复。如果在合理时间内未收到满意答复，他提议再次提出此事。

THE NORTH-CHINA SUNDAY NEWS, JULY 24, 1931

THE THORBURN
CASE

Demand for Surrender of
Missing Briton

HELD BY MILITARY

Further Representations
Authorised

From Our Own Correspondent

London, July 22.
I am officially informed that the Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs, Mr. Arthur Henderson, this morning authorised further representations to the Nanking Government over the disappearance of Mr. J. H. Thorburn. A demand is to be made that Mr. Thorburn be produced for immediate trial under British law, in accordance with the extraterritoriality provisions of the treaty between Great Britain and China.

From an independent source the British Government has been informed that Mr. Thorburn, alive or dead, is in the hands of the Chinese military.

Local Protests

That the disappearance of Mr. John Thorburn, and the apparent official indifference to his whereabouts, is actively engaging the attention of Britons everywhere in China is indicated by a telegram received yesterday from Weihaiwei.

This reported that 52 signatures to the protest recently circulated among local British residents had been mailed from visitors to that summer resort.

The list of signatures to the protest is otherwise steadily growing and indignation has obviously transcended the bounds of nationality. A non-British protest, now in circulation, yesterday afternoon had 24 nationalities represented by its more than 200 endorsers.

Government Approached

The telegram sent to London by the China Association after its meeting on July 21 has also had gratifying results, according to word received yesterday from Home. The London executive of the Association has now undertaken to bring the circumstances of the Thorburn case vividly before the people of Great Britain and as an initial effort in this connection has already broadcast the text of the telegram throughout the country.

The Parent Body has also arranged for a number of further questions to be asked in the House of Commons in regard to Thorburn's whereabouts and has approached the Government on the subject. Although no definite action has yet been notified by the Government nor a reply received to the letter containing particulars of the protest and the reasons, it is confidently expected that satisfactory information will be available for transmission to Shanghai at an early date.

《华北星期新闻》，1931年7月24日

索恩伯恩案

要求引渡失踪英人

由军方羁押

获准进一步交涉

本报特约记者

伦敦，7月22日。
本人从官方获悉，外交大臣阿瑟·亨德森先生（Mr. Arthur Henderson）于今晨授权就 J. H. 索恩伯恩先生（Mr. J. H. Thorburn）失踪一事向南京政府作进一步交涉。将提出要求，根据中英条约中的治外法权条款，依据英国法律立即对索恩伯恩先生进行审判。

据一独立消息源告知英国政府，索恩伯恩先生无论生死，均在中国军方手中。

地方抗议

来自威海卫的一份电报显示，约翰·索恩伯恩先生（Mr. John Thorburn）的失踪以及当局对其下落明显的漠不关心，正积极引起在华所有英国人的关注。

该电报称，近期在当地英国居民中 circulated 的抗议书上的52个签名，是由前往该避暑胜地的游客寄出的。

抗议书上的签名名单仍在稳步增加，愤慨之情显然已超越了国籍界限。一份非英国人的抗议书目前正在流传，截至昨日下午，其200多名签署者代表了24个国籍。

向政府提出诉求

据昨日从国内收到的消息，英华协会（China Association）在7月21日会议后发给伦敦的电报也取得了令人满意的结果。该协会伦敦执行委员会现已着手向英国公众生动地介绍索恩伯恩案的情况，并作为此项工作的初步努力，已在全国广播了该电报的全文。

总会还安排在下议院就索恩伯恩的下落提出更多质询，并已就此问题与政府接洽。虽然政府尚未通知采取任何具体行动，也未回复载有抗议详情及理由的信件，但人们有信心预计，不久将有令人满意的信息可供转达至上海。

FURTHER QUESTIONS
ON THORBURN
Interpellations To Be Put
To Henderson Next
Monday
DANGERS OF GIVING UP
EXTRALITY RIGHTS
LONDON, July 23.—The interest taken by the House of Commons in the case of Mr. Thorburn is indicated by the fact that further questions will be put to Mr. Arthur Henderson, Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs, on Monday.
The line taken by the Conservatives is that the case illustrates the dangers of relinquishing extraterritoriality or of any measure which would place Europeans under Chinese authority.
The firm line indicated in the reply given by the Government in the House of Commons yesterday is welcomed, and it is stated that every possible step will be taken to keep the question in active being until it is settled satisfactorily.

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, JULY 18th, 1931. 45.7.31.

Additional Evidence Is
Found Thorburn Was
Arrested By Gendarmerie

PRIEST TELLS OF VIEW FROM BRITISH
YOUTH DURING NIGHT OF JUNE 7 AND
SUBSEQUENT ARREST BY SOLDIERS

STRUGGLES WITH CAPTORS AND RECEIVES
BAYONET WOUND IN NECK

Appeal Of Local British Residents Received In
London; Reply Comes Back Stating Action
Will Be Taken; Chinese Comment

"The Shanghai Times" is able to-day to give additional
indisputable evidence of the fact that John Thorburn, 19-
year-old British resident of Shanghai, who has been missing
for over seven weeks, was actually arrested in the vicinity
of Quinsan by Chinese military police. The evidence has
been furnished by a Catholic priest who actually saw
Thorburn on the night of June 7 and later saw him seized
by Chinese police and taken off to Quinsan. The evidence
also shows that Thorburn broke away from his captors and
dashed down the railway line where he was intercepted and
again arrested after a struggle, during which he was wound-
ed in the neck by a bayonet carried by one of the soldiers.
What happened to Thorburn after his second arrest is a
mystery which the entire foreign community of Shanghai is
anxious to solve, with or without the aid of the Chinese
authorities.

This further proof of Thor-
burn's arrest has come from a
reliable source. The report gives
details of the incident as actually
witnessed by the priest.

It was reported that Thor-
burn was seen, presumably by
Chinese soldiers and Hsienli
on the morning of June 7. He
was seen in Hsuti and later in
Quinsan.

发现补充证据表明
索恩伯恩曾被宪兵逮捕

神父讲述6月7日晚所见英国青年情况及
随后被士兵逮捕经过

与抓捕者搏斗并颈部受刺刀伤

伦敦收到当地英国居民的上诉；回电称将采取行动；中方评论

《上海泰晤士报》今日能够提供无可辩驳的补充证据，证明失踪已逾七周的19岁上海英籍居民约翰·索恩伯恩（John Thorburn）确实在昆山附近被中国军警逮捕。该证据由一位天主教神父提供，他曾在6月7日晚亲眼见到索恩伯恩，随后目睹他被中国警察抓获并带往昆山。证据还显示，索恩伯恩曾挣脱抓捕者，沿铁路线奔跑，但在拦截后再次被捕，期间在与一名持有刺刀的士兵搏斗中颈部受伤。索恩伯恩第二次被捕后的遭遇成了一个谜，整个上海外侨社群都急于解开这个谜团，无论是否有中国当局的协助。

这一关于索恩伯恩被捕的进一步证据来自可靠来源。报告详细描述了神父亲眼目睹的事件经过。

据报道，6月7日上午，有人看见索恩伯恩，推测是被中国士兵和乡绅（Hsienli）看见。他先是在徐家汇（Hsuti）被看见，后来在昆山被看见。

Next morning Thorburn took
his leave of the priest and was
only seen by some villagers who
said he was going to Soochow, while
this was not so.

Next morning soldiers took
him away from the house and was
only seen by some villagers who
said he was going to Soochow, while
this was not so. They immediately
seized him and led him off in the
direction of Quinsan. He was
locked up temporarily in a small
house, but somehow managed to
break out, and fled once again in
the direction of the priest's house.
Pursued by soldiers, Thorburn
dashed along the railway line
where he was intercepted by
another group of soldiers, who
seized him. Thorburn struggled
violently, but was finally over-
come, receiving a bayonet wound
in the neck during the struggle.
Just how serious the wound was
the priest was unable to say, as
Thorburn was hurried off in the
direction of the Quinsan railway
station. This was the last seen
of Thorburn by the priest.

Other Testimony
Other witnesses examined by
Mr. A. L. Gavit, British Vice-
Consul, have stated that Thorburn

次日早晨，索恩伯恩向神父告别，只有几位村民看见他，他们说他要前往苏州，但事实并非如此。

次日早晨，士兵将他从屋内带走，只有几位村民看见他，他们说他要前往苏州，但事实并非如此。他们立即抓住他，将他朝昆山方向押解。他被暂时关押在一间小屋里，但不知何故设法逃脱，再次朝神父住所方向逃跑。在士兵的追捕下，索恩伯恩沿铁路线狂奔，在那里被另一群士兵拦截并抓获。索恩伯恩激烈反抗，但最终被制服，在搏斗中颈部被刺刀刺伤。神父无法说明伤势究竟有多严重，因为索恩伯恩被匆忙押往昆山火车站方向。这是神父最后一次见到索恩伯恩。

其他证词
英国副领事 A. L. 加维特先生（Mr. A. L. Gavit）讯问的其他证人表示，索恩伯恩的双臂被绑在背后，乘火车从昆山被带往苏州。证人还表示，有人在苏州见过受伤的索恩伯恩，且据未经证实的消息称，他遭受了残害。

鉴于这些新证据，索恩伯恩在昆山被中国士兵逮捕并被非法带至昆山火车站，随后被装上开往苏州的火车，这似乎已毫无疑问。

另一起抗议
与此同时，上海的愤慨情绪日益高涨。由2800多名英国居民签署的电报抗议书已抵达伦敦，前上海居民 F. H. 克罗斯利先生（Mr. F. H. Crossley）已发电报确认收到该抗议书，他将确保其送达相关主管部门。

又一个全国性社团对索恩伯恩的失踪表示了关注。昨日，由当地澳大利亚人和新西兰人组成的上海澳新军团协会（Anzac Society）分会向英国首相发出了以下电报抗议：

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL
C. & S. B. REG.S
No. S. B. D. 2464
ate 24. 7. 31.

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Thursday, July 23, 1931

Lampson Warns
Wang To Probe
Thorburn Case

Minister Has Condemned
Action By Nanking,
Parliament Told

FEELING AROUSED
IN GREAT BRITAIN

Dalton Tells Commons
Sir Miles Demands
Investigation

(United Press)
LONDON, July 22.—Any further delay on the part of the Chinese Government in solving the mysterious disappearance of Mr. John Thorburn, a 22-year-old British subject who has been missing for almost two months from his home in Shanghai, will confirm the suspicion that the Chinese Government is deliberately procrastinating, Mr. Hugh Dalton, the Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs declared in the House of Commons tonight.
Replying to blunt questions from Sir Charles Cayzer, the Conservative member of Parliament for the City of Chester, Under-Secretary Dalton said that already Sir Miles Lampson, His Britannic Majesty's Minister in China, has made strong representations to the Chinese National Government at Nanking.

Lampson Warns Nanking
In his representations to Dr. C. T. Wang, the Foreign Minister of the Nanking Government, Sir Miles Lampson has expressed regret that there has been no further clarification of the disappearance of Mr. Thorburn since the statement of the Chinese authorities that their investigation showed that the young British subject never was arrested nor imprisoned by the Chinese police or military.
Mr. Dalton said that Sir Miles Lampson has warned the Foreign Minister at Nanking that "any further delay will confirm the suspicion that the Chinese authorities are deliberately procrastinating, believing that the Thorburn case can be hushed up and eventually forgotten."

Indignation In England Growing
Through the efforts of British subjects in China, especially in Shanghai, and because of the interest which has been aroused in official circles in England the Thorburn case is receiving widespread publicity in England.

Indignation has mounted since the receipt of cabled reports of the only official statement given out by the Nanking Government last week. Belief here prevails that it would have been impossible for Mr. Thorburn to disappear completely from the earth within only a few miles of Shanghai without the knowledge of the Chinese authorities, who enjoy diplomatic recognition by the British Government.

Press Linked With Extrality
The British press is carrying full and detailed accounts of the Thorburn case, the feeling it has aroused throughout China and criticism of British as well as of Chinese officials.
A very definite connection between the Thorburn case and China's demands for the abolition of extraterritoriality is seen by many British editors.

Anzac Send Message
The Anzac Society of Shanghai, the newest British organization here, yesterday added its protest to those already sent to London by various other organizations, including St. George's Society, St. Andrew's Society, St. Patrick's Society and St. David's Society. The protest of the Anzac Society was in the form of a telegram to the British Prime Minister. The message follows:
"Shanghai Anzac Society, consisting of Anzacs who fought in Great War, and Australians, New Zealanders resident in China, record strongest indignation on disappearance of John Thorburn. Despite conclusive evidence of arrest obtained by British authorities, Chinese Government denies all knowledge of his whereabouts. Anzac Society prays that immediate action be taken to safeguard British prestige as the future safety of all Britishers in China is dependent on this."

New Evidence Found
New evidence concerning the arrest of young Thorburn has been uncovered, according to one report made public this morning. The report states that a Catholic priest living near Quinsan has come forward with the story of the arrest of the youth.
"The young man, according to the priest, called at his house about 10 p.m. on June 1. He knocked at the door and was admitted. His clothes seemed to have been thoroughly wet. He remarked that he had fallen into the water. The following morning, the report says, the youth left the house but had gone only a short distance when he was accosted by soldiers. He broke away after a struggle, ran, but again was seized, being wounded in the neck by a bayonet in the hands of a soldier. The last the priest saw of him he was being hurried off in the direction of the Quinsan railway station."

British Women Protest
It is announced that all British women interested in the Thorburn case will find a list for signatures prepared at the British Women's Association headquarters, 13 The Bund during morning office hours 9 a.m. to 12 noon.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1931年7月23日，星期四

兰普森警告
王正廷调查
索恩伯恩案

大臣谴责南京方面
之行动，告知议会

英国国内情绪激愤

道尔顿告知下议院
迈尔斯爵士要求调查

（合众社）
伦敦，7月22日电。——英国外交部政务次官休·道尔顿先生今晚在下议院宣称，如果中国政府在解决现年22岁的英国臣民约翰·索恩伯恩先生失踪案上再有任何拖延——该员自其上海寓所失踪已近两个月——这将证实人们对中国政府故意拖延的怀疑。
在回答切斯特市选区保守党议员查尔斯·凯泽爵士直率的提问时，道尔顿次官表示，英国驻华公使迈尔斯·兰普森爵士已向南京的中国国民政府提出强烈交涉。

兰普森警告南京方面
迈尔斯·兰普森爵士在向南京政府外交部长王正廷博士提出的交涉中，对中方当局声明其调查显示该名年轻英国臣民从未被中国警察或军方逮捕或监禁之后，索恩伯恩失踪一事仍未得到进一步澄清表示遗憾。
道尔顿先生称，迈尔斯·兰普森爵士已警告南京方面的外交部长，“任何进一步的拖延都将证实这种怀疑，即中国当局正在故意拖延，认为索恩伯恩案可以被掩盖并最终被遗忘。”

英国国内的愤怒情绪日益高涨
通过在中国、特别是上海的英国臣民的努力，以及由于英国官方圈子内引发的关注，索恩伯恩案在英国正受到广泛的宣传报道。
自从上周收到南京政府发布的唯一一份官方声明的电报报道以来，愤怒情绪不断升级。此处普遍相信，在获得英国政府外交承认的中国当局的知情下，索恩伯恩先生不可能在上海附近仅几英里范围内完全从地球上消失。

媒体将此事与治外法权相联系
英国报纸正刊登关于索恩伯恩案的全面详细报道，包括该案在整个中国引发的情绪以及对英国和中国官员的批评。
许多英国编辑认为，索恩伯恩案与中国废除治外法权的要求之间存在着非常明确的联系。

澳新军团协会发送电文
上海澳新军团协会（Anzac Society）是此地最新的英国人组织，昨日将其抗议加入已由其他各种组织（包括圣乔治协会、圣安德鲁协会、圣帕特里克协会和圣大卫协会）发往伦敦的抗议行列中。澳新军团协会的抗议形式是向英国首相发出的一封电报。电文如下：
“上海澳新军团协会，由参加过大战的澳新军团成员以及居住在中国的澳大利亚人、新西兰人组成，记录对约翰·索恩伯恩失踪一事的强烈愤慨。尽管英国当局获得了确凿的逮捕证据，中国政府仍否认知晓其下落。澳新军团协会恳请立即采取行动以维护英国的威望，因为所有在华英国人的未来安全均系于此。”

发现新证据
根据今早公布的一份报告，发现了有关年轻索恩伯恩被捕的新证据。该报告称，一位居住在昆山附近的天主教神父站出来讲述了这名青年被捕的故事。
“据这位神父说，这名年轻人在6月1日晚上10点左右来到他的住所。他敲门并被允许进入。他的衣服似乎完全湿透了。他说自己掉进了水里。报告称，第二天早上，这名青年离开了住所，但没走多远就被士兵拦住。经过一番挣扎后他挣脱逃跑，但再次被抓，颈部被一名士兵手中的刺刀刺伤。神父最后看到他时，他正被匆忙带往昆山火车站方向。”

英国妇女提出抗议
据悉，所有关心索恩伯恩案的英国妇女可在上午办公时间（上午9时至中午12时）前往外滩13号英国妇女协会总部，在准备好的签名名单上签名。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Tuesday, August 23, 1927

800 British Residents Sign
Protest On Thorburn Case

1,000 Signatures Expected Before Closing Time
Today; Blocked Text Of Cable Released

More than 800 British men and women residents of Shanghai at noon today had signed the Thorburn Appeal List, open to British residents for signature at 5 Peking Road. Indications at noon, despite threatening weather, were that fully 1,000 British residents will have signed the list before 4:30 p.m., which is closing time.

As soon as the list has been closed, it was stated today by Mr. A. P. Maer, sponsor of the plan, the following cablegram will be dispatched to the leading newspaper of London:

Text Of Telegram

An appeal signed by . . . . . British subjects in Shanghai earnestly requests the assistance of the London press in giving the greatest publicity to the case of young Thorburn held without trial by the Chinese authorities for more than six weeks and every indication (printed mutilated or dead (stop)) immediate strong action by the government absolutely essential and to secure this your valued help is urged (stop) . . . . . mendacious reply issued 18th by the Chinese Government regarding their investigation (stop).

A representative of The Shanghai Evening Post and Mercury this morning was permitted to scan the list of signatures. A considerable number of names of outstanding British residents was noted.

Missing Since June 1

The list was opened to British residents as the result of the strange disappearance from Shanghai on June 1 of Mr. John Thorburn, 19, who has been missing for 81 days.

British authorities, from information obtained from various Chinese sources, have reason to believe that the young man was arrested by the . . . . . near Quinsan, following the fatal shooting of two Chinese . . . . . was taken to Soochow and either was put to death, after being tortured, or is badly injured and is being held a prisoner.

British Rights Denied

Representations were made to the Nanking Government by the British Minister to China, Sir Miles Lampson, through his . . . . .

该计划发起人 A. P. Maer 先生今天表示，一旦名单截止，以下电报将发送至伦敦的主要报纸：

一份由……名在上海的英国臣民签署的呼吁书，恳请伦敦新闻界协助，对年轻索恩伯恩被中国当局未经审判拘押超过六周且种种迹象表明（印刷错误：肢解或已死亡（句号））一案给予最大程度的公开报道。政府立即采取强硬行动绝对必要，为确保此举，亟需您宝贵的帮助（句号）……中国政府于18日发布的关于其调查的虚假回复（句号）。

THE CHINA PRESS, TUESDAY, JULY 21, 1931

Thorburn Petition
Has Many Signers

British And Foreign
People Show
Interest

A. P. Weir, who is conducting a campaign to secure signatures to a petition asking for an inquiry into the circumstances surrounding the death of Mr. Thorburn, stated yesterday that over 1,000 people had signed the petition and that it was expected that the number would be considerably increased before it was forwarded to London.

The petition will be sent to all leading London newspapers, and through them, Mr. Weir hopes the petition will come under the notice of members of Parliament. He said yesterday that he thought this method would be more effective than directly approaching the Prime Minister or the House of Commons.

While many foreigners sought to sign the petition yesterday, none but British subjects were allowed. Approximately 500 signed between 9 a.m. and 4 p.m.

Local Chinese authorities would not be expected to sign, Mr. Weir said.

SMASHES WINDOWS IN

ROME, July 17.—The discovery
of a powerful bomb in St. Peter's,
the most sacred Catholic church,
has caused a tremendous sensation
inasmuch as according to experts
its explosion in any case would
have seriously damaged the famous
cupola of the basilica, which was
designed by Michel Angelo, even if
a still greater catastrophe had been
averted.
The bomb was found after the
basilica had been closed to the
public. It was wrapped in paper
in a confessional directly beneath
the cupola and close to the monument of Pope Benedict XV. It exploded spontaneously at two o'clock
this morning at an isolated spot
in the Vatican gardens whither it
had been removed after its discovery by Papal guards.
The force of the explosion, which
was heard all over Rome, awakened
the Pope from his sleep and smashed
a number of windows in the
Vatican's picture gallery, but
thanks to the precautions taken
did no further damage. Clues as
to the perpetrators of this barbarous attempt to destroy one of
the world's most famous and sacred
buildings have not yet been found,
though the city is full of contradictory rumours, circles close to
the Italian Government, which
immediately ordered a strict investigation, claiming that it must
have been the work of anti-Fascists who wanted to accuse
the Vatican and the Quirinal. Trans-

Official Statement From

Says He Was Not Arrested

INVESTIGATION AT SOOCHOW AND QUINSAN
BY GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS PRODUCES
NOTHING BUT REPEATED DENIALS

REMARKABLE CONTRADICTIONS FROM
WITNESSES IN SECOND ENQUIRY

Stationmaster, Chinese Porters, Constable And
Residents Who Previously Admitted Seeing
Bound Foreigner, Now Deny Statements

In an official statement from the Foreign Office of the
Nanking Government to the British Consul-General in
Shanghai, the results of the Chinese investigation into the
disappearance of John Thorburn, 19-year-old British resident of Shanghai, were communicated yesterday morning. It
is denied that Thorburn, or any other foreigner, was arrested
by the Gendarmerie, or that any foreigner was concerned in the shooting incident in the vicinity of Quinsan
on June 1. Allegations that any foreigner had been
imprisoned, wounded or beaten, either at Quinsan or
Soochow, are denied by the Chinese officials. All knowledge
of the whereabouts of John Thorburn are also firmly denied.
The statement from Nanking is, in effect, a general contradiction of the statements previously made to Mr. A. L. Scott, British Vice-Consul, by witnesses examined by him both at Quinsan and Soochow. These witnesses had stated
that they had seen a foreigner answering Thorburn's description
under arrest at Quinsan and Soochow. At the latter place he was
led through the streets with his
hands tied behind his back and
was subsequently tied to a tree
and publicly beaten.
John Thorburn disappeared
somewhere along the Shanghai-Nanking railway line between
Quinsan and Soochow on June 1.
Since that date he has not been
found. Reports from various
sources indicated that he had been
arrested by Chinese military
police in the vicinity of Quinsan.
All efforts to trace him proved
fruitless and the Nanking Government, through the British Minister, Sir Miles Lampson, was asked to conduct an investigation
into this mysterious disappearance. The result of the investigation by Nanking Government

罗马，7月17日电。——在圣彼得大教堂（最神圣的天主教堂）内发现一枚强力炸弹，引起了巨大轰动。据专家称，尽管避免了更大的灾难，但该炸弹若在任何情况下爆炸，都将严重损坏由米开朗基罗设计的著名大教堂穹顶。
炸弹是在大教堂对公众关闭后发现的。它被包裹在纸中，放置在穹顶正下方、靠近教皇本笃十五世纪念碑的一个忏悔室内。今晨两点，炸弹在梵蒂冈花园的一个偏僻地点自发爆炸，该处是教皇卫队发现炸弹后将其移往之地。
爆炸声响彻罗马，其威力将教皇从睡梦中惊醒，并震碎了梵蒂冈绘画陈列馆的多扇窗户，但由于采取了预防措施，未造成进一步损害。目前尚未找到这起企图摧毁世界上最著名和最神圣建筑之一的野蛮行径的肇事者线索，尽管城中充斥着相互矛盾的谣言。与意大利政府关系密切的圈子声称，这一定是反法西斯分子所为，他们意图以此指控梵蒂冈和奎里纳尔宫（意大利总统府）。跨洋通讯社-国民社。

南京政府外交部昨日早晨向英国驻上海总领事发出官方声明，通报了中国方面对19岁上海英籍居民约翰·索恩伯恩（John Thorburn）失踪案的调查结果。声明否认索恩伯恩或任何其他外国人被宪兵逮捕，也否认有任何外国人卷入6月1日昆山附近的枪击事件。中国官员否认有关任何外国人在昆山或苏州被监禁、受伤或殴打的说法。同时也坚决否认知晓约翰·索恩伯恩的任何下落。南京方面的声明，实质上是对此前由英国副领事A. L. Scott先生在昆山和苏州讯问的证人所作陈述的全面反驳。这些证人曾称，他们在昆山和苏州看见一名符合索恩伯恩特征的外国人被捕。在苏州，该外国人双手被反绑游街，随后被绑在树上公开殴打。
6月1日，约翰·索恩伯恩在昆山和苏州之间的沪宁铁路沿线某处失踪。自那以后一直下落不明。来自各方面的报告表明，他在昆山附近被中国宪兵逮捕。所有寻找他的努力均告失败，英国公使迈尔斯·兰普森爵士（Sir Miles Lampson）遂要求南京政府对此神秘失踪案进行调查。南京政府官员的调查结果如下：

WERE ALL THESE PEOPLE LYING?

The following points, taken from statements to British Consular investigators by Chinese at Soochow and Quinsan, are of great importance in the Thorburn investigation and compel close attention. Before the Chinese investigation began, the Minister of Foreign Affairs was informed in writing of the substance of the evidence in the hands of the British authorities. The following points were particularly stressed:
1.—Sia Zui-soong, “ha tsang” of the 4th Company, 1st Battalion, 1st Regiment of the Military Police spoke of the shooting incident and the arrest of a foreigner, who was taken to Quinsan, where he was detained until the afternoon of June 2, when he was removed under escort.
2.—The wife of the proprietor of the Tsang Ah-sing dry goods store at Quinsan stated that at about 4 p.m. on June 1, a young foreigner, whom she identified from a photograph as Thorburn, went to her shop and made a small purchase. He was wearing a pair of dark blue trousers with red lines down the side of each leg. On the following day she saw the same foreigner with his hands tied behind his back in the custody of the Military Police. She said he was put on a train.
3.—A policeman named You Loh-li, attached to the 1st Sub-Station in Quinsan, said he had seen a foreigner wearing long trousers with two red stripes, being taken along the street by the Military Police with his hands tied behind his back. He was put on a train going west just after 1 o’clock on June 2.
4.—Another policeman in Quinsan gave corroborative evidence and stated that the foreigner had given his nationality as English.
5.—When questioned, the stationmaster at Quinsan said that a foreigner had been put on the train going westward just after 1 p.m. on June 2. He was in the custody of a party of Military Police. He also stated that the foreigner had an inscription on his handkerchief and that he actually wrote the words “Sea Scout Troop” on one of the posts of the station platform. The words were still there on June 10 and were seen on that date by Mr. Scott, British Vice-Consul. He was noticed examining them, but when he returned to the station shortly afterwards they had been carefully erased.
6.—The Li-li Photograph Shop in Quinsan when visited revealed further evidence. Here it was learned that a photograph of the foreigner had been taken, shortly after his arrest, but the owner of the shop had no copy of the photograph as the negative had been taken away by the Military Police.
7.—Two porters at the Soochow Railway Station, No.’s 93 and 105, stated they saw the foreigner on the afternoon of June 2 being sent under a Military Police escort to the Military Headquarters.

WERE ALL THESE PEOPLE LYING?

Amateur Bath-House Racketeer
Finally Lands In Gaol

Ingenuity, not modesty, was the chief characteristic of Yang, a bath-house thief now “doing time” in the Municipal guest-house on Ward Road, according to the evidence submitted by aggrieved witnesses appearing at Yang’s trial.
Apparently Saturday night is “bath night” the world over for those not particularly addicted to self-ablution. At any rate Saturday night was Yang’s big night of the week and he made it a practice of visiting a bath-house on Avenue Edward VII where the clientele was more dressy than at most other places. Subsequent events proved that Yang was more interested in the habiliments of his fellow-bathers than in his own cleansing.
For instance, a week ago he suddenly let out a first-class bath-house war-whoop and called for the Riot Squad, the Ambulance Corps, S.V.C. and Chapei Gendarmerie, declaring to an excited multitude that some one had stolen his pants.
He got no satisfaction from the proprietor. But when that worthy’s back was turned Yang grabbed a spare pair of the proprietor’s and skipped into the street with only a shirt on.
The following Saturday he tried the same trick at another bath-house, this time calling for everybody’s help except that of the Pootung Protection Corps. Then, as the excitement commenced to die down, he seized a nifty silk jacket and hit out for the highway with hue and cry after him. This time he was caught.
On trial Yang stated that the bath-house proprietor merely had a grudge against him for using too much soap. In fact, said Yang, he had once hit him over head with a wooden bucket for using too much.
This the proprietor denied, but went one better by telling the court that the jacket stolen had contained $800. Three years for Yang.

FOREIGN OFFICE REPORT
OF ENQUIRY

With regard to the disappearance without trace of the British resident of Shanghai, Thorburn, it is on record that repeated letters have been received from the British Consul-General at Nanking requesting investigation; also that the replies of the various Departments concerned have been communicated to the British Consul-General. Further, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of War each sent an official of their respective Ministries to conduct a joint and strict investigation. These two officials have now reported as follows:
In pursuance of our instructions, we at once left for Soochow where we first visited the headquarters of the First Regiment of Gendarmerie occupying the Lao Wu T’uan Barracks. We were informed by the Colonel of the said Regiment that the Regiment certainly had not arrested any foreigner. As regards the matter of the wounding by shooting of two gendarmes at Weiting near Kunshan (Quinsan), the bandits had made good their escape owing to the passing of a train (between the combatants). Not only was no foreigner arrested on that occasion, but no Chinese was captured. We, thereupon, inspected the regimental gaol, where we found only two Chinese prisoners. Both were gendarmes. There was no foreigner in the gaol. We then inspected the military gaol. There were four prisons and one prison hospital and three workshops. We examined them all, one after another, and found that they contained no foreigner.

SOOCHOW MAGISTRATE’S
DENIAL

We then went to the District Magistracy of Wuhsien (Soochow). We were informed that on receipt of instructions from the Ministry ordering an investigation, the Magistrate at once wrote to the Headquarters of the First Regiment of Gendarmerie and also ordered the Commissioner of Police to investigate and report. The Gendarmerie headquarters replied that no foreigner whatever had been arrested. The Commissioner of Police reported that he had made investigations and found that there was no truth in the allegation that a foreigner had been arrested.
We then proceeded to the Soochow Railway Station where we interviewed the stationmaster and the assistant stationmaster, and asked them whether on or about the 2nd of June they had seen on the station premises a party of gendarmes guarding a foreigner. They replied that they were very busily engaged every day in the performance of their duties and did not know whether gendarmes had or had not brought a foreign prisoner to the station. 以下各点摘自苏州和昆山的中国人士向英国领事调查员所作的陈述，在索恩伯恩（Thorburn）一案的调查中至关重要，必须予以密切关注。在中方调查开始之前，外交部已收到书面通知，获悉英国当局所掌握证据的要旨。特别强调了以下几点：

1. 宪兵第一团第一营第四连的“哈藏”（音译，ha tsang）夏祖松（Sia Zui-soong，音译）谈及枪击事件及逮捕一名外国人的情况，该外国人被带往昆山，拘押至6月2日下午，随后在押解下被转移。

2. 昆山曾阿兴（Tsang Ah-sing，音译）干货店店主之妻称，6月1日下午4时许，一名年轻外国人光顾其店铺并购买了少量商品。她通过照片辨认出此人即索恩伯恩。当时他穿着一条深蓝色长裤，裤腿两侧各有红色条纹。次日，她看见同一名外国人双手被反绑，由宪兵看管。她说他被送上了火车。

3. 隶属于昆山第一分驻所的一名名叫尤洛利（You Loh-li，音译）的警察称，他看见一名外国人穿着带有两条红色条纹的长裤，双手被反绑，由宪兵沿街押解。6月2日刚过下午1点，此人被送上一列西行的火车。

4. 昆山的另一名警察提供了佐证，并称该外国人自报国籍为英国。

5. 在接受询问时，昆山火车站站长表示，6月2日下午1点刚过，一名外国人被送上一列西行列车。该外国人由一队宪兵看管。他还指出，该外国人的手帕上有字样，并且他确实在站台的一根柱子上写下了“Sea Scout Troop”（海童军团）字样。这些字迹在6月10日依然可见，英国副领事斯科特（Scott）先生于当日亲眼目睹。有人注意到他在查看这些字迹，但当他不久后返回车站时，字迹已被仔细擦除。

6. 对昆山的丽丽照相馆（Li-li Photograph Shop，音译）进行走访后，发现了更多证据。据悉，在该外国人被捕后不久曾为其拍摄了一张照片，但店主没有保留照片副本，因为底片已被宪兵拿走。

7. 苏州火车站的两名搬运工，编号93号和105号，称他们在6月2日下午看见该外国人在宪兵押解下被送往军事总部。

这些人都在撒谎吗？

业余澡堂敲诈者
最终入狱

根据在杨某受审时出庭的受害证人提供的证词，这位如今正在华德路市立监狱（Municipal guest-house，此处指监狱或拘留所）服刑的澡堂窃贼杨某，其主要特征并非谦逊，而是狡诈。

显然，对于那些不太热衷于自我清洁的人来说，周六晚上在世界范围内都是“洗澡夜”。无论如何，周六晚上是杨某一周中的重头戏，他习惯于前往爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）的一家澡堂，那里的顾客比大多数其他地方更为讲究衣着。后续事件证明，杨某对他 fellow-bathers（共浴者）的衣着比对自己身体的清洁更感兴趣。

例如，一周前，他突然发出一声一流的澡堂战吼，呼叫防暴队、救护队、上海志愿队（S.V.C.）和闸北宪兵队，并向激动的人群宣称有人偷了他的裤子。

他从店主那里没有得到任何满意的结果。但当那位可敬的店主转过身去时，杨某抓起店主的一条备用裤子，只穿着一件衬衫溜到了街上。

接下来的那个周六，他在另一家澡堂故技重施，这次他呼吁所有人帮忙，唯独没有叫浦东保卫团（Pootung Protection Corps）。随后，当骚动开始平息时，他抓起一件漂亮的丝绸夹克，在一片喊打声中逃向大街。这次他被抓住了。

在受审时，杨某声称澡堂店主仅仅因为他用了太多肥皂而对他怀恨在心。事实上，杨某说，有一次因为他用得太多，店主曾用木桶砸他的头。

店主否认了这一说法，并向法庭进一步陈述，被盗的夹克内藏有800美元。杨某被判刑三年。

英国外交部
调查报告

关于上海英国居民索恩伯恩失踪且下落不明一事，记录显示，英国驻南京总领事曾多次致函要求调查；此外，各相关部门的回复也已转达给英国总领事。此外，外交部和军政部各自派遣了一名官员进行联合严密调查。这两名官员现报告如下：

遵照指令，我们立即前往苏州，首先访问了驻扎在老吴团兵营（Lao Wu T’uan Barracks，音译）的宪兵第一团总部。该团团长告知我们，该团确实未逮捕任何外国人。关于昆山（Quinsan）附近唯亭（Weiting，音译）两名宪兵被枪击受伤一事，匪徒因一列火车经过（交战双方之间）而成功逃脱。那次事件中不仅没有逮捕外国人，也没有抓获中国人。随后，我们检查了团部监狱，发现只有两名中国囚犯。两人均为宪兵。监狱中没有外国人。接着我们检查了军事监狱。那里有四个监区、一个监狱医院和三个车间。我们逐一进行了检查，发现其中没有外国人。

苏州知事
否认

随后我们前往吴县（苏州）县公署。我们获悉，在接到部委下令调查的指令后，知事立即致函宪兵第一团总部，并命令警察局长进行调查并报告。宪兵总部回复称，未逮捕任何外国人。警察局长报告称，他已进行调查，发现有关逮捕外国人的指控不实。

随后我们前往苏州火车站，会见了站长和副站长，询问他们在6月2日左右是否在车站范围内看见一队宪兵看守一名外国人。他们回答说，他们每天忙于履行职责，不知道宪兵是否曾将一名外国囚犯带到车站。最近，英国副领事斯科特先生曾访问车站并查

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, JULY 16, 1931

Thorburn Case Goes Before
Public Of Britain

St. Andrew's Society Of Shanghai Sends Telegram
To Mr. Ramsay MacDonald Deploring Ineffec-
tive Policy; Home Newspapers Informed

Intervention by the British Gov-
ernment for the release of John
Thorburn, 19-year-old British
subject alleged to be in the hands
of Chinese military authorities for
a period now exceeding six weeks,
is being waged by the Shanghai
branch of St. Andrew's Society,
which has interested itself in the
affair for humane and national
reasons.

A telegram to Mr. Ramsay
MacDonald, British Prime Minis-
ter, was dispatched from Shang-
hai by the Society yesterday, as
follows:

"John Thorburn, British sub-
ject, held six weeks without trial
near Nanking by Chinese
authorities. Tortured, mutilated
or dead. Known to have been
alive three weeks ago. Request
for Sino-British investigation
refused. St. Andrew's Society of
Shanghai deplores ineffective
policy of Foreign Office and calls
for strong, definite action.
"Signed, Committee of St.
Andrews Society, S'hai."

Arrangements have also been
made to issue this telegram
through Reuter's Agency to news-
papers at Home for the purpose
of calling attention to the plight
of young Thorburn whose fate,
like his exact whereabouts, con-
tinue to remain a mystery.
Thorburn disappeared from his
home, 315 Rue Bourgeat, French
Concession, on June 1.
Movements Traced
Evidence collected since his dis-
appearance by Consular officials,
plain-clothes policemen, and inde-
pendent investigators points to his
having headed in the direction of
Nanking, following the railway
route. He is believed to have got
into difficulties with some Chinese
soldiers as a result of a shooting
episode along the railway embank-
ment near Quinsan, and to have
been taken prisoner and removed
to Soochow military barracks.
It has been reported that he
was transferred elsewhere, and
has been held prisoner since.
Corroborated testimony has also
been collected by British Consular
officers investigating on the spot
that Thorburn was tied to a tree
and beaten in the presence of a
number of Soochow villagers,
while an uncorroborated report
was received to the effect that
one of his soldier guards stab-
bed him with a bayonet.
All but definite proof of Thor-
burn having been held in prison
at Soochow was collected by Mr.
A. Scott, British Vice-Consul at
Shanghai, who remained for over
a week in Soochow conducting an
exhaustive inquiry. But although
the British official returned satis-
fied that Thorburn was in the
hands of the military, he could
not trace his whereabouts.
Minister Intervenes
He gathered sufficient evidence,
however, to prompt the British
Minister to China, Sir Miles
Lampson, to send a representative
to Nanking with a request for an
official investigation.
This representative, Mr. Frank
Aveling, called upon the Minister
of Foreign Affairs at Nanking,
who deputed a representative from
the Ministry and another from the
Ministry of War to proceed to
Soochow and investigate the re-
ports furnished by the British
authorities. But Mr. Aveling's at-
tendance at the investigation was
refused.
At the present time the Nan-
king Government representatives
are still conducting their inquiry
at Soochow, while Mr. Aveling
and the British authorities await
their report. So far, the Chinese
have been more than two weeks
on their task, but not a word as
to their movements or discoveries,
if any, has been received by the
British authorities to date.

《字林西报》，1931年7月16日，星期四

索恩伯恩案引起
英国公众关注

上海圣安德鲁协会致电
拉姆齐·麦克唐纳先生，谴责政策无效；
国内报纸获知此事

上海圣安德鲁协会出于人道和国家原因关注此事，正积极争取英国政府干预，以释放据称已被中国军事当局扣押超过六周的19岁英国臣民约翰·索恩伯恩。

该协会昨日从上海向英国首相拉姆齐·麦克唐纳先生发出电报，内容如下：

“英国臣民约翰·索恩伯恩，被中国当局在南京附近未经审判扣押六周。遭受酷刑、致残或已死亡。三周前已知其尚在人世。中英联合调查请求被拒。上海圣安德鲁协会谴责外交部政策无效，呼吁采取有力、明确的行动。
“签署人：上海圣安德鲁协会委员会。”

还已安排通过路透社将该电报发给国内报纸，以引起人们对年轻索恩伯恩困境的关注，他的命运如同其确切下落一样，至今仍是个谜。索恩伯恩于6月1日从其在法租界布尔热路315号（Rue Bourgeat）的家中失踪。

行踪追踪

自其失踪以来，领事官员、便衣警察和独立调查员收集的证据表明，他沿着铁路线朝南京方向前进。据信，他因在昆山附近铁路路基发生的一起枪击事件而与一些中国士兵发生冲突，随后被俘并被转移至苏州军营。

据报道，他后来被转移到其他地方，并一直被囚禁至今。

在现场调查的英国领事官员还收集了佐证证词，表明索恩伯恩在许多苏州村民面前被绑在树上殴打，同时收到一份未经证实的报告，称他的一名士兵守卫用刺刀刺伤了他。

几乎可以确凿证明索恩伯恩曾被关押在苏州监狱的证据，是由英国驻上海副领事A. 斯科特先生收集的，他在苏州停留了一周多，进行了详尽的调查。但是，尽管这位英国官员确信索恩伯恩在军方手中，但他无法追踪到其下落。

公使介入

然而，他收集了足够的证据，促使英国驻华公使蓝普森爵士（Sir Miles Lampson）派代表前往南京，要求进行官方调查。

这位代表弗兰克·阿夫林（Frank Aveling）先生拜会了南京的外交部长，后者指派了一名外交部代表和一名军政部代表前往苏州，调查英国当局提供的报告。但阿夫林先生被拒绝参加调查。

目前，南京政府代表仍在苏州进行调查，而阿夫林先生和英国当局则在等待他们的报告。到目前为止，中方人员执行任务已超过两周，但英国当局至今未收到关于其行动或发现（如果有的话）的任何消息。

THE CHINA PRESS, WEDNESDAY, JULY 8, 1931

British Authorities
Laud Press Findings
In Thorburn Mystery

Copy Of Reporter's Story Forwarded To Nanking
As Material Evidence For Investigators;
Father Of Youth Appreciates Paper's Action

Shanghai yesterday acclaimed The China Press investigation of the Thorburn disappearance as a valuable step toward the solution of the mystery and as added impetus to official inquiries now being carried out. Among those who recognized the importance of disclosures made in yesterday China Press, as a result of the three day investigation, were Mr. M. Hay Thorburn, father of the 19-year-old Britisher last seen in Shanghai on June 1, and the British superintending consul, Mr. A. D. Blackburn.

Mr. Blackburn, yesterday sent a copy of The China Press carrying intimate disclosures on the disappearance of John Hay Thorburn, 19, believed to have been detained for five weeks by Chinese military authorities, to the British Legation at Nanking.

Disclosures Significant

Mr. Blackburn told a China Press representative that the news story included details of a significant nature. He said that previous information gained by consular investigators and others was largely given by second and third parties. Practically all the testimony introduced into the China Press account of the alleged capture and detention of a foreigner by Chinese soldiers was given by Soochow residents who claimed to actually have seen the young man in the custody of soldiers. More than 50 witnesses were interviewed during the paper's three-day investigation.

Mr. Blackburn said that besides the quantity of added information included in the Press report, certain details differed from those collected by the British office. The consul had learned that the First Battalion held the young man, while the Press gained information from soldiers and townspeople that he was detained at the second Battalion Camp. Eye witnesses also denied the report received by British authorities to the effect that the boy had been mutilated.

Press Probe Welcome

The consular official said that the Nanking government had sent representatives of the War and Foreign Affairs Ministries to conduct a month's investigation of the case. One week has passed. Reports of their findings will be made public at the end of the month.

Mr. Blackburn said that the action taken by the China Press was especially welcome inasmuch as it came at a time when the hands of the British authorities were practically tied. He said that the Chinese government at Nanking had not definitely forbidden a British investigation of the Thorburn disappearance, but that when it was asked to sanction the sending of Mr. Aveling to represent the British government in the inquiry, the Chinese responded that they could conduct their own investigation. Mr. Blackburn said there is no objection to an informal British investigation, but the above response is in effect a refusal to allow a foreign representative to sit with them in consideration of evidence on the Thorburn case. The British government can only await developments brought about by the Chinese investigation, he declared.

Father Appreciative

Mr. Thorburn expressed his appreciation of the step taken by the China Press toward determining the fate of his son. He said that he had not yet given up hope that his son would be returned to him, and that the account in the China Press substantiated belief of his that his son was still alive.

1931年7月9日

《字林西报》，1931年7月8日，星期三

英国当局
赞扬新闻界在索伯恩失踪谜案中的调查结果

记者报道副本已作为调查材料证据送交南京；
青年之父感谢报社之举

上海昨日对《字林西报》关于索伯恩（Thorburn）失踪案的调查表示赞赏，认为这是解开谜团的重要一步，并为目前正在进行的官方调查增添了动力。在认可昨日《字林西报》基于三天调查所披露信息之重要性的人士中，包括6月1日在上海最后被目击的19岁英国青年之父 M. Hay Thorburn 先生，以及英国驻沪总领事 A. D. Blackburn 先生。

Blackburn 先生昨日将一份载有约翰·海·索伯恩（John Hay Thorburn，19岁）失踪案内幕披露内容的《字林西报》副本送往南京英国公使馆。据信索伯恩已被中国军方扣押五周。

披露内容意义重大

Blackburn 先生告诉《字林西报》代表，该新闻报道包含了具有重大意义的细节。他表示，此前领事馆调查人员及其他方面获得的信息大多来自第二手和第三手渠道。而《字林西报》关于一名外国人被中国士兵 alleged（涉嫌）抓捕和拘留的报道中，几乎所有证词均由声称亲眼目睹该青年处于士兵看守下的苏州居民提供。在该报为期三天的调查中，采访了超过50名证人。

Blackburn 先生表示，除了《字林西报》报道中包含的大量新增信息外，某些细节与英国办事处收集的信息有所不同。领事馆获悉是第一营扣押了该青年，而《字林西报》从士兵和市民处获得的信息显示，他被关押在第二营营地。目击者还否认了英国当局收到的关于该少年遭受残害的报告。

欢迎新闻界调查

这位领事官员表示，南京政府已派遣军政部 and 外交部代表对该案进行为期一个月的调查。一周已经过去。他们的调查结果报告将于月底公布。

Blackburn 先生表示，《字林西报》采取的行動特别受欢迎，因为此时英国当局实际上束手无策。他说，南京中国政府并未明确禁止英国方面对索伯恩失踪案进行调查，但当英方请求批准派遣 Aveling 先生代表英国政府参与调查时，中方回应称他们可以自行进行调查。Blackburn 先生表示，中方并不反对非正式的英国调查，但上述回应实际上拒绝了外国代表与其共同审议索伯恩案的证据。他宣称，英国政府只能等待中方调查带来的进展。

父亲表示感谢

Thorburn 先生对《字林西报》为确定其子命运所采取的步骤表示感谢。他说，他尚未放弃儿子会回到他身边的希望，且《字林西报》的报道证实了他认为儿子仍然活着的信念。

“我非常感激《字林西报》发起一项……
