THE SHANGHAI TIMES, WEDNESDAY, JULY 8, 1931

Thorburn Now Missing 37 Days;
Official “Search” Fruitless

The whereabouts of John Thorburn, 19-year-old Briton who disappeared on June 1 after setting out in the direction of Quinsan, are still definitely unknown to British Consular authorities and everyone else desirous of locating him, it was learned during inquiries yesterday.

It is significant, however, that although the committee of inquiry sent to Soochow by the Nanking Government at the request of the British Minister to China have been investigating for more than a week, they have not, so far, communicated to the British authorities any information whatsoever. According to their plans, they will continue to investigate for another three weeks, then return to Nanking and render their report.

In the meantime Mr. Frank Aveling, personal representative of H. M. Minister, sent to Nanking to press for this inquiry, is still at Nanking, forbidden to join the Nanking investigators at Soo-

chow.

Whether Thorburn is being held at Soochow, Lion Hill or anywhere else is not the real issue. It has been reported that he is now at Nanking and this report is being looked into, local British authorities stated yesterday.

Wherever Thorburn may be now cannot alter the evidence that he, or someone so like him as to satisfy the most sceptical, was seen in custody of Chinese soldiers at Soochow on or about the time of his disappearance.

This has been borne out, not by one witness, but by scores of witnesses, including railway officials, plain villagers and even soldiers themselves. Responsible British officials collected this testimony.

At Nanking or Soochow, wounded or not, guilty of the Quinsan shooting or not, the British authorities are satisfied that Thorburn was in the hands of the military. Their only doubt at present is where he may be found at this time.

《上海泰晤士报》，1931年7月8日，星期三

索伯恩已失踪37天；
官方“搜寻”毫无结果

据昨日查询得知，19岁的英国人约翰·索伯恩（John Thorburn）于6月1日向昆山方向出发后失踪，其下落至今对英国领事当局及所有希望找到他的人来说仍完全未知。

然而，值得注意的是，尽管应英国驻华公使之请由南京政府派往苏州的调查委员会已调查了一周多，但截至目前，他们未向英国当局通报任何信息。根据其计划，他们将继续调查三周，然后返回南京并提交报告。

与此同时，英国公使的个人代表 Frank Aveling 先生被派往南京敦促此项调查，目前仍留在南京，被禁止前往苏州加入南京方面的调查人员。

无论索伯恩是被关押在苏州、狮子山还是其他地方，这都不是真正的问题。当地英国当局昨日表示，有报道称他目前在南京，该报告正在核查中。

无论索伯恩现在何处，都无法改变这一证据：在他失踪前后，在苏州有人看到他，或看到一个与他极其相似、足以令最怀疑者信服的人，处于中国士兵的看守之下。

证实这一点的并非一名证人，而是数十名证人，包括铁路官员、普通村民甚至士兵本人。这些证词由负责任的英国官员收集。

无论在南京还是苏州，无论是否受伤，无论是否与昆山枪击案有关，英国当局确信索伯恩曾在军方手中。他们目前的唯一疑点是他此时可能被发现在哪里。

（批注：1931年7月8日）

THE NORTH-CHINA SUNDAY NEWS, JULY 5, 1931

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL
& S. C. REG.
S. B. D. 2464.
Date 7-7-31

THE THORBURN
MYSTERY

Disappearance Five Weeks
Ago To-morrow

NO RESULTS FROM
INVESTIGATIONS

To-morrow morning, July 6, there will have elapsed five weeks since Mr. John Hay Thorburn disappeared so mysteriously, and also one week will have elapsed since the National Government commenced its inquiry into his disappearance. So far official Chinese investigations have produced no result, despite the fact that the consular authorities have no doubt that Mr. Thorburn is, or has been, in Soochow or its vicinity.

Special pressure was brought to bear on the Nanking authorities by Mr. Aveling, H.M. Minister's personal representative, recently, and on July 27 he was informed by Dr. C. T. Wang, Minister for Foreign Affairs, that a representative of his ministry had already left for Soochow and that a representative of the Ministry of War was also leaving, and that official inquiries were to commence early last week. No statement has been made regarding the progress of their inquiries.

Prior to this the military police authorities at Soochow had persistently denied that they had any foreigner in custody. Mr. Thorburn left Shanghai on June 1, and on that morning a young foreigner, corresponding to him and wearing garments corresponding to those Mr. Thorburn had taken from home, was seen by Chinese in Quinsan.

The Shooting Incident

That night, about 10 p.m., a shooting affair occurred along the railway line near Weiting, when a man originally described as a foreigner and believed to be a Russian is alleged to have shot and wounded two military police, who subsequently died in hospital in Shanghai. The next morning an alleged Russian was arrested as grave suspicion was attached to him, and taken to the headquarters of the military police in Soochow.

明日早晨，7月6日，距离约翰·海·索伯恩先生如此神秘地失踪已满五周，距离国民政府开始对其失踪案进行调查也已满一周。尽管领事当局毫无疑问索伯恩先生正在或曾经在苏州或其附近，但迄今为止，中方的官方调查尚未产生任何结果。

英国公使的个人代表 Aveling 先生最近对南京当局施加了特别压力，7月27日，外交部长王正廷博士告知他，其部委的一名代表已前往苏州，军政部的一名代表也将启程，官方调查已于上周初开始。关于调查进展，尚无声明发布。

在此之前，苏州宪兵当局一直否认扣押有任何外国人。索伯恩先生于6月1日离开上海，当天上午，一名外貌与他相符、穿着与索伯恩先生从家中带走衣物相符的年轻外国人，被中国人在昆山看到。

枪击事件

当晚约10点，唯亭附近的铁路沿线发生了一起枪击事件，一名最初被描述为外国人并被认为是一名俄罗斯人的男子， allegedly（涉嫌）开枪打伤了两名宪兵，这两名宪兵随后在上海的医院中死亡。次日早晨，一名 alleged（涉嫌）俄罗斯人被捕，因他有重大嫌疑，并被带往苏州宪兵总部。

在英国总领事馆发布并于两周前刊登在《华北星期日新闻》上的一份声明中，有以下段落：“这一发生在日期上的 str... lar authori- ties ... mediately a ... se inter- ... proceed to ... es. The ... eft little ... who had ... connec- ... have ... by ... ilim ... that ... to ... ly ... *日本的西方音乐 ... pell ... 中法远征队 ... 穿越亚洲。 ... 我如何差点杀死一只老虎。 ... 快乐花园——一篇 ... 短篇小说，作者 Cosmo ... Hamilton。 ... 智者与其他人。 ... 儿童页。 ... 生活剪影。 ... 威尔士亲王 ... 在市政厅 ... 关于沙文主义政治的 m ... ni ... me ... sh ... (W ... Pr ... re ... on ... Go ... at ... La ... th ... Se"

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL
C. & S. B. REGISTER
No. S. B. D. 2454
Date J. 7. 31.
N74

THE SHANGHAI TIMES THURSDAY, JULY 2, 1931

STRANGE HAPPENINGS
AT SOOCHOW
Aveling Held At Arm's
Length; Thorburn
Is Moved?

CHINESE CONDUCTING
INQUIRY ALONE

For some reason best known to themselves, the Soochow military authorities are understood to have transferred John Thorburn, 19-year-old Briton last seen alive by his parents on May 31, from the military prison at Soochow to other dingy quarters at Shih Tan Shan, or Stone Hill, about an hour and a half's walk from Soochow.

The transfer was accomplished nearly two weeks ago, according to information reaching the British consular authorities here. Although the report is not quite as reliable as others which have been received by the British authorities, it nonetheless has more than a probability of truth in it, as borne out by supporting evidence of a circumstantial nature.

The reason for the transfer, if transfer there actually has been, is undoubtedly the institution of an inquiry, supposedly of a vigorous nature, by the Nanking Government acting under pressure applied by the British Legation.

This inquiry has already begun but the information as to the manner of its commencement is alone suspicious in character as the Chinese military authorities have refused permission to Mr. Frank Aveling, British Legation representative on the spot under instructions from Sir Miles Lampson, to accompany the committee of inquiry during the course of their investigations.

On June 27 representatives from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Ministry of War at Nanking left for Soochow in connection with this inquiry, Mr. Aveling was informed. They had strict instructions to investigate thoroughly the reports in circulation about Thorburn being under detention by the military authorities at Soochow.

At the same time as this information was conveyed to Mr. Aveling he was politely told that his association with the Government's investigators was not desired, for the reason already stated.

"We are, in fact, just as anxious to clear up this affair as you are," Mr. Aveling was told. That, and no more.

《上海泰晤士报》，1931年7月2日，星期四

苏州的
奇怪事件
Aveling 被拒之门外；索伯恩
被转移？

中方单独
进行调查

出于只有苏州军方当局自己才知道的原因，据悉他们已将约翰·索伯恩（John Thorburn，19岁，5月31日被父母最后目击时仍活着的英国人）从苏州军事监狱转移至石潭山（Shih Tan Shan，即 Stone Hill）的其他简陋住所，距苏州约一个半小时步行路程。

根据此处英国领事当局获得的信息，这次转移是在近两周前完成的。虽然该报告不如英国当局收到的其他报告可靠，但由于有间接性质的佐证证据支持，其真实性可能性很大。

如果确实发生了转移，其原因无疑是南京政府在英国公使馆施压下启动了据称力度很大的调查。

这项调查已经开始，但关于其启动方式的信息本身就带有可疑性质，因为中国军方当局拒绝允许英国公使馆代表 Frank Aveling 先生在调查过程中陪同调查委员会。Aveling 先生是根据 Miles Lampson 爵士的指示在现场工作的。

据告知 Aveling 先生，6月27日，南京外交部和军政部的代表已就此项调查前往苏州。他们接到严格指令，要彻底调查关于索伯恩被苏州军方当局拘留的流传报告。

在向 Aveling 先生传达此信息的同时，他也礼貌地被告知，出于前述原因，不希望他与政府调查人员合作。

“事实上，我们和您一样急于澄清此事，” Aveling 先生被告知。仅此而已，再无多言。

（批注：归档
JRL
1931年7月3日。）

Date 2. 7. 31.

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, TUESDAY, JUNE 30, 1931

THORBURN MYSTERY
STILL UNSOLVED

British Authorities
Unable To Make
Statement

There have been no developments in what has come to be known locally as the "Thorburn mystery," according to Mr. A. D. Blackburn, Superintending Consul, of H.B.M. Consulate-General.

The inquiry started by Mr. Frank Aveling, personal representative of Sir Miles Lampson. H. M. Minister to China, is still in progress, according to Mr. Blackburn, who was unable, however, to disclose the nature of any progress made to date by Mr. Aveling.

The despatch to Soochow of Mr. Aveling, it will be recalled, followed closely upon the release to the press of Shanghai by the British Consulate of an official statement of the discoveries made by British Vice-Consul A. L. Scott, specially sent to Soochow to discover what had become of John Thorburn, 19-year-old Briton believed to have fallen into hands of the Soochow military authorities.

Mr. Scott's inquiries pointed strongly to Thorburn being held a prisoner at Soochow and on the strength of this information, which was wirelessed to H. M. Minister in Peiping, Mr. Aveling was sent to press the Nanking Government for an immediate official investigation, a joint Sino-British Commission of Inquiry being suggested.

Mr. Aveling has already discussed the matter with Dr. C. T. Wang, Minister for Foreign Affairs, pressing for an immediate and full investigation. That was in the early part of last week. Since then, no further information has been vouchsafed by the local British consular authorities.

索伯恩谜案
仍未破解

英国当局
无法发表
声明

据英国驻沪总领事馆总监事 A. D. Blackburn 先生称，当地所称的“索伯恩谜案”目前没有任何进展。

Blackburn 先生表示，由英国驻华公使蓝普森爵士（Sir Miles Lampson）的个人代表 Frank Aveling 先生发起的调查仍在进行中，但他无法透露 Aveling 先生迄今为止取得的任何进展的性质。

回想起来，Aveling 先生被派往苏州，紧随英国驻沪领事馆向上海新闻界发布的一份官方声明之后，该声明公布了英国副领事 A. L. Scott 的发现。Scott 是专门被派往苏州去查明被认为已落入苏州军事当局手中的19岁英国人 John Thorburn 下落的。

Scott 先生的调查强烈指向 Thorburn 被囚禁在苏州，基于这一通过无线电报发给北平英国公使的信息，Aveling 先生被派去向南京政府施压，要求立即进行官方调查，并建议成立中英联合调查委员会。

Aveling 先生已与外交部长王正廷博士讨论此事，敦促进行立即且全面的调查。那是上周初的事情。此后，本地英国领事当局未再提供进一步信息。

THORBURN INQUIRY
TO BE PRESSED
Mr. F. Aveling Calls Upon
Dr. C. T. Wang At
Nanking

In connection with the alleged detention of John Thorburn, 19-year-old British subject, by the Soochow military authorities, it is understood that Mr. F. Aveling, representing Sir Miles Lampson, H. M. Minister to China, has already seen Dr. C. T. Wang, Chinese Minister for Foreign Affairs, and is pressing for an immediate inquiry.

Thorburn has been missing from his home since June 1, and the local British consular authorities have collected sufficient evidence to warrant the assumption that the missing Briton is being held a prisoner in a Soochow military prison and is, moreover, in bad physical condition at the present time.

SHOOTING OF MILITARY POLICE BY FOREIGNERS.

The Sin Wan Pao publishes the following letter
from the Woosung-Shanghai Garrison Commissioner's

The report published by your paper on the
killing of members of the Military Police near Tsing

1096

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, FRIDAY, JUNE 19, 1931

DISAPPEARANCE OF
JOHN THORBURN

Possibility Of Official
Statement By Brit-
ish Consul

An official statement upon the Thorburn mystery is likely to be forthcoming from the British Consular authorities within the next 24 hours, "The Shanghai Times" was informed yesterday, providing certain necessary formalities at present in motion are completed to the satisfaction of the authorities concerned.

The British Consular authorities, who have been making the fullest possible investigation into this affair in the face of many obstacles placed in their path, it is believed, by officials, outside the Settlement have reached the conclusion that the situation demands the full light of publicity and permission of the British Minister at Peiping is being sought for that purpose.

John Thorburn, 19-year-old Briton, left his home on June 1 with an obscure intention and wandered along the Shanghai-Nanking railway line in the direction of Quinsan. There, it is believed, he got himself into some sort of trouble with a party of Chinese soldiers whom he met, and there is strong evidence that he was subsequently arrested and taken to Soochow.

Definite denial of his arrest or detention has been given repeatedly by Chinese military officials at Soochow, notwithstanding much evidence to the contrary collected by British Consular officials and others who have carried out investigations on the spot.

Rumours of foul play have been in circulation and the British Consular authorities here are believed to be in possession of certain information which may eventually lead to the exchange of official notes with the Nanking Government.

（批：File 21.6.31.）

《字林西报》，1931年6月19日，星期五

约翰·索伯恩
失踪

英国领事可能
发表官方
声明

《字林西报》昨日获悉，只要目前正在进行中的某些必要手续令有关当局满意并完成，英国领事当局很可能在未来24小时内就索伯恩谜案发表官方声明。

据信，英国领事当局尽管面临租界外官员设置的诸多障碍，仍对此事进行了尽可能充分的调查，并已得出结论认为局势需要完全公开，为此正寻求英国驻北平公使的许可。

19岁的英国人 John Thorburn 于6月1日怀着不明的意图离家，沿着沪宁铁路向昆山方向游荡。据信，他在那里与遇到的一群中国士兵发生了某种麻烦，且有有力证据表明他随后被捕并被带往苏州。

尽管英国领事官员及其他在现场进行调查的人员收集了大量相反证据，苏州的中国军事官员仍反复坚决否认对其实施逮捕或拘留。

有关不法行为的谣言一直在流传，据信在沪的英国领事当局掌握着某些信息，这些信息最终可能导致与南京政府交换官方照会。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. & S. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. 2464
Date 19 - 6 - 31

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, WEDNESDAY, JUNE 17, 1931

HOPE FOR THORBURN
VANISHING

Conspiracy Of Silence
At Soochow Proves
Effective

Little hope is held out by the British consular authorities of tracing the whereabouts of John Thorburn, 19-year-old Briton, who mysteriously disappeared from his home on the night of May 31-June 1. Practically every possible avenue of inquiry has been thoroughly investigated, and although the evidence that Torburn fell into Chinese military hands continues to pile up, categorical denials that he did so, likewise continue to be received from Chinese sources.

For more than a week, Mr. A. L. Scott, British Vice-Consul, has been conducting an investigation at Soochow, but little or no light on the mystery has resulted. If anything, the mystery has deepened.

The past 24 hours brought to light one somewhat significant piece of information, however. It was the rumour that the First Regiment stationed at Soochow had been transferred to Kiangsi. It was a party of soldiers from this regiment, it is alleged, who were concerned in the shooting affair near Quinsan on or about June 2, which other rumours connected with the missing man Thorburn.

Notwithstanding the official denials issued by the Soochow military and judicial authorities that any foreigner had been concerned or arrested in connection with that incident, there is very strong evidence that a foreigner resembling young Thorburn was arrested by the Soochow military authorities and is being detained somewhere in Soochow. There is the alternative theory, unconfirmed rumours of which have already been in circulation in Shanghai, that young Thorburn was shot, but whether during the affair with the soldiers or in consequence of his part in that affair, may never be known.

（批：Reg. Please file. 18/6/31）

寻找索伯恩的
希望渺茫

苏州的沉默共谋
证明有效

英国领事当局对追踪19岁英国人 John Thorburn 的下落几乎不抱希望，他于5月31日至6月1日晚间从家中神秘失踪。实际上每一条可能的调查途径都已得到彻底排查，尽管证明 Thorburn 落入中国军方手中的证据不断累积，但来自中国方面的断然否认也持续不断。

一个多星期以来，英国副领事 A. L. Scott 先生一直在苏州进行调查，但对该谜案几乎没有或完全没有带来任何线索。如果说有什么变化的话，那就是谜团更加深了。

然而，过去24小时揭示了一条 somewhat 重要的信息。有谣言称，驻扎在苏州的第一团已被调往江西。据称，正是该团的一些士兵参与了6月2日左右在昆山附近的枪击事件，其他谣言将该事件与失踪男子 Thorburn 联系起来。

尽管苏州军事和司法当局正式否认有任何外国人卷入或因该事件被捕，但有非常有力的证据表明，一名酷似年轻 Thorburn 的外国人被苏州军事当局逮捕，并正被拘禁在苏州某处。另一种理论是，年轻 Thorburn 已被枪杀，上海已流传未经证实的相关谣言，但他是在与士兵的事件中被杀，还是作为该事件一部分的后果而被杀，可能永远无法知晓。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, THURSDAY, JUNE 18, 1931

THE THORBURN
MYSTERY

Fate of Missing Briton
Still Unknown

BELIEVED TAKEN TO
SOOCHOW

Still no news has reached Shang-
hai of the whereabouts of Mr. John
Thorburn, the young nineteen-year
old Englishman who disappeared
from home on June 1, was seen
walking along the Shanghai Nan-
king Railway in the neighbourhood
of Quinsan station and, apparently,
has completely vanished.

Inquiries set on foot by the Bri-
tish authorities have been, so far,
fruitless. Mr. A. L. Scott, who has
been investigating the affair at
Soochow, has returned to Shang-
hai. It is understood that
the local Chinese officials have
received no report either of
Mr. Thorburn or of any incident con-
necting him with the affray in
which two Chinese soldiers were
wounded, one of them mortally. In
fact, the statements of the Chinese
officials as recorded in the "North-
China Daily News" on Monday have
not been substantially varied.

The fact remains that Mr. Thor-
burn has not been located. It is
moreover ascertained, from reports
reaching this office, that a foreigner,
answering to his description, was
seen in custody and so far as can
be judged, was taken to Soochow.
The denials of the local authorities
are therefore taken to be based on
information incompletely seized of
the facts.

Obviously the matter cannot rest
there. Mr. Thorburn's disappearance
is seriously exercising the minds of
his parents. The British authorities
have made most careful investiga-
tions and it is probable that they
will before long have to take the
matter up formally with the Chin-
ese Government. It is expected
that a full statement of the facts
as they have been elicited will be
framed and representations made
through the proper channels for
steps to be taken in order to clear
up the mystery.

《字林西报》，1931年6月18日，星期四

索伯恩
谜案

失踪英国人的
下落仍然
未知

据信被带往
苏州

关于19岁英国青年 John Thorburn 先生的下落，上海仍未收到任何消息。他于6月1日从家中失踪，有人看见他在昆山站附近的沪宁铁路沿线行走，显然已完全消失。

英国当局发起的调查迄今毫无结果。一直在苏州调查此案的 A. L. Scott 先生已返回上海。据悉，当地中国官员未收到任何关于 Thorburn 先生或任何将其与两名中国士兵受伤（其中一人致命）的斗殴事件联系起来的报告。事实上，中国官员在周一《字林西报》上记录的陈述并无实质性变化。

事实仍然是，Thorburn 先生尚未被找到。此外，从到达本办公室的报告 ascertain 得知，一名符合其描述的外国人曾被看到处于羁押状态，据判断，他被带往了苏州。因此，地方当局的否认被认为是基于对事实掌握不全的信息。

显然，此事不能就此罢休。Thorburn 先生的失踪使其父母深感焦虑。英国当局已进行了非常仔细的调查，他们很可能不久后不得不就此事项与中国政府进行正式交涉。预计将根据已查明的事实起草一份完整声明，并通过适当渠道提出交涉，以便采取行动解开谜团。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, THURSDAY, JUNE 18, 1931

Mr. Thorburn's Fate
Whatever may be the conditions
in the interior of China, it is very
difficult to believe that a young
foreigner can disappear into the
blue within a few miles of Shang-
hai, without there being any trace
of his whereabouts. It is still more
difficult to believe in the face of
the known facts about Mr. Thor-
burn's adventure. It is establish-
ed that he was possessed of some
idea of travelling on foot into
China. It is admitted that he was
seen walking on the railway line
between Shanghai and Quinsan.
There is a sufficient amount of
cumulative evidence, circumstantial
and otherwise to justify the theory
that he was taken into custody by
some Chinese who escorted him to
Soochow. The time factor and,
other personal details, gave
grounds for the strongest presump-
tion that he was in some way or
another involved in the incident
which led to the arrival at Shang-
hai of two wounded Chinese
soldiers, one of whom subsequently
died. Yet in spite of the assiduous
inquiries of the British authorities,
the information from official Chi-
nese sources at Soochow fails en-
tirely to support these deductions.
That would not arouse comment if
the Soochow officials could produce
evidence of Mr. Thorburn's where-
abouts. They apparently cannot.
It would seem that the re-
ports which they have received
from their subordinates are defec-
tive. The matter is hardly likely to
be allowed to rest there. It is to
be hoped therefore that more in-
sistent inquiries will be made
through such channels as will pro-
duce reliable and reputable in-
formation on the subject.

《字林西报》，1931年6月18日，星期四

索伯恩先生的命运
无论中国内地局势如何，很难相信一名年轻的外国人会在距离上海仅几英里的地方凭空消失，且不留任何行踪线索。鉴于已知的关于索伯恩先生冒险经历的事实，这一点更令人难以置信。现已证实，他确实有过徒步进入中国内地的想法。据承认，有人看见他在上海与昆山（Quinsan）之间的铁路线上行走。有足够多的累积证据，包括间接证据及其他证据，足以支持这样一种理论：他被一些中国人扣留，并被护送至苏州（Soochow）。时间因素以及其他个人细节，为最强有力的推定提供了依据，即他以某种方式卷入了导致两名中国士兵抵达上海的事件，其中一人随后死亡。然而，尽管英国当局进行了不懈的调查，来自苏州官方渠道的信息却完全无法支持这些推断。如果苏州官员能拿出索伯恩先生下落的证据，这本来不会引起评论。但他们显然拿不出来。看来，他们从下属那里收到的报告是有缺陷的。此事不太可能就此搁置。因此，希望透过能够产生可靠且信誉良好的相关信息的渠道，进行更为坚持的调查。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. & S. D. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. 2484
Date 15. 6. 31

Extract from the Morning Translation of
June 15, 1931.

-----

Shooting of two Military Policeman by Foreigner

The Sin Wan Pao published the following letter
from the First Regiment Military Police on June 14 : -

"Re the shooting of two military police by des-
peradoes on the night of June 1 while patrolling near
Tsing Hee ( ). On the night in question a thick
fog set in and nothing could be seen at close range.
When the military police patrol of this Regiment reach-
ed a place about 3 li to the west of the Tsing Hee
Railway Station, some desperadoes suddenly opened
fire on them and consequently two policemen were
wounded . While the remaining police were in pur-
suit of the desperadoes, an express train passed
and separated the police and the desperadoes, who,
availing themselves of the opportunity, made good
their escape. The police made a thorough search but
made no arrests. These are the true facts of the case.
The information published by various newspapers is
mostly untrue; moreover, the report of the arrest of
a foreigner is entirely groundless and it has in-
curred suspicion on the part of foreigners. For
fear that the truth may still not be known to the
public, we hereby request that a correction be
published."

1931年6月15日晨间翻译摘录

-----

外国人枪击两名宪兵

《新闻报》于6月14日刊登了来自第一团宪兵队的如下信件：-

“关于6月1日晚在清溪（Tsing Hee，原文不清）附近巡逻时两名宪兵遭歹徒枪击一事。当晚大雾弥漫，近在咫尺也看不见东西。当本团宪兵巡逻队到达清溪火车站以西约三里处时，几名歹徒突然向他们开火，导致两名警察受伤。其余警察在追捕歹徒时，一列快车驶过，将警察与歹徒隔开，歹徒趁机逃脱。警方进行了彻底搜查，但未逮捕任何人。以上是本案的真实情况。各报纸刊登的消息大多不实；此外，关于逮捕一名外国人的报道毫无根据，并已引起外国人的怀疑。唯恐公众仍不知晓真相，特此请求刊登更正。”

BRITISH SUBJECT ALLEGED MISSING.

The Pao Tao, a mosquito paper, publishes
the following article:-
The British Consulate at Nanking received
a letter from the British Consulate in Shanghai the day
before yesterday stating that a British subject, resident
of Shanghai named "Ka S Un" (?), age 18, surreptitiously
left his home at the end of May, taking with him a pistol.
This man is very quiet tempered. In a letter left by him
he wrote that he desired to enroll with the Chinese army
to suppress the Communists. It is not known whether he has reached Nanking or has joined the Chinese
army. He is not in possession of a passport nor a pistol
licence. The British Consulate at Nanking have transmitted
the original letter to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
who in turn requested the Nanking Garrison Commissioner
to make investigations.

据称失踪的英国臣民。

小报《报导》刊登了以下文章：-
南京英国领事馆前天收到上海英国领事馆的一封信，称一名居住在上海、名为“Ka S Un”（音译）的英国臣民，年龄18岁，于5月底携带手枪偷偷离家。此人性情非常安静。在他留下的一封信中，他写道希望加入中国军队以剿共。目前尚不清楚他是否已到达南京或已加入中国军队。他既没有护照，也没有持枪许可证。南京英国领事馆已将原信转交外交部，外交部随即要求南京卫戍司令进行调查。

ate 17. 6. 31

THE CHINA PRESS, TUESDAY, JUNE 16, 1931

New Evidence In
Hands Of British
In Thorburn Case

Suspicion Persists That
Youth Was Taken By
Soochow Police

Despite the fact that the Soo-
chow magistrate and gendarmerie
officer are still strongly denying that
they have Mr. John Thorburn, 18-
year-old Briton who has been miss-
ing from Shanghai since June 1, in
their custody, British consular offi-
cials here have now more reason
than ever to believe their state-
ments untruthful, it was declared
yesterday.

The Superintending consul, Mr.
A. D. Blackburn, informed a repre-
sentative of The China Press yes-
terday that local British authorities
do not actually know the exact
whereabouts of the missing youth
but they are positive he is in Soo-
chow, in which city Mr. A. L. Scott,
vice-consul in the Chinese Affairs
office, is continuing his investiga-
tions.

Thorburn Seen In Soochow
Whether young Thorburn is alive
or dead is not known. British in-
vestigations have been carried out
ever since the youth's mysterious
disappearance, from his father's
house, 315 Rue Bourgeat, on June
1, was reported. As a city-wide
search was made for him here
without success, the hunt was spread
further afield.

The first important clue obtained
was the statement of the station
master of the Shanghai-Nanking
Railway's Quinsan station. This
official claimed to have seen a for-
eigner, answering exactly Thor-
burn's description, in the custody
of Chinese gendarmerie in Quinsan.
Now, the number of people who
have seen Thorburn in the gendar-
merie's hands have swelled con-
siderably for Mr. Scott has located
a few persons who actually saw
Thorburn, still in the hands of
Chinese military, in Soochow.

Cleared Of Shooting
Mr. Blackburn personally thinks
the lad is in Soochow and that the
Chinese authorities, for some rea-
son of their own, are deliberately
hiding his whereabouts.
At first it was believed that
Thorburn was connected in some

New Evidence In
Hands Of British
In Thorburn Case

(Continued from Page 1, Col. 3)
manner with the strange shooting
affray on the railroad track in
which two Chinese gendarmes
received fatal wounds and have
since died from them. This inci-
dent happened on the night of
June 2, a day after Thorburn dis-
appeared from his home in Shang-
hai.

Thorburn Cleared Of Charge
However, the commanding offi-
cers of the two gendarmerie divi-
sions in the Soochow district in-
formed Mr. Scott that no foreigner
was involved in the case, their men
being wounded by bandits. British
authorities here, knowing that
Thorburn was armed with a .45
caliber Shanghai Volunteer Corps
revolver, were at first afraid the
youth had been arrested in connec-
tion with the shooting and dealt
with by the Chinese themselves.
The statements of the Chinese
officers cleared Thorburn of a parti-
cularly serious situation and now
allows the youth's consular authorities
to have a clearer field to work upon
for his recovery irrespective whether
he is dead or alive.

Fond On Outdoor Life
Young Thorburn was a quiet lad,
very keen on all outdoor sports
and life in general. An enthusias-
tic hockey player during the win-
ter months, he is in the habit of
devoting most of his time in sum-
mer to tennis or on the river. He
was a Sea Scout and a live member

of the Drysdale Amateur Dramatic
Club. In 1928, then a boy of 17,
Thorburn started training, seriously
to train for the International
Walking Competition with the Eng-
lish team. After two weeks of
gruelling work he was forced to
abandon his idea of entering for
the race as his legs gave out on
him. Thorburn was a lad with a
great amount of "go" in him and
very popular in the younger set
here.

The missing youth was supposed
to have joined a boating party up
at Hephil the day before he disap-
peared. Instead of doing so, how-
ever, he spent the day in Shanghai
playing tennis at the Race Course
in the afternoon and returning to
his father's house to sleep that
night. He left the following day
after leaving a note to his father
merely saying he was going up coun-
try

《大美晚报》，1931年6月16日，星期二

英国方面掌握
索伯恩案新证据

怀疑 persist 青年
被苏州警方带走

尽管苏州地方法官和宪兵军官仍然强烈否认他们拘留了自6月1日起在上海失踪的18岁英国人约翰·索伯恩（John Thorburn）先生，但据昨日宣称，驻沪英国领事官员现在比以往更有理由相信他们的陈述是不真实的。

总领事 A. D. Blackburn 先生昨日告知《大美晚报》记者，当地英国当局实际上并不知晓这名失踪青年的确切下落，但他们确信他在苏州，负责中国事务办公室的副领事 A. L. Scott 先生正在该城市继续进行调查。

在苏州见到索伯恩
年轻的索伯恩是生是死尚不得而知。自从6月1日报称这名青年从其父亲位于布尔热路（Rue Bourgeat）315号的家中神秘失踪以来，英国方面一直进行调查。由于在此进行的全城搜索未果，搜寻范围进一步扩大。

获得的第一条重要线索来自京沪铁路昆山站站长的陈述。这位官员声称，在昆山看到一名符合索伯恩特征的外国人正由中国宪兵看守。现在，目睹索伯恩在宪兵手中的人数已大大增加，因为 Scott 先生已经找到几位实际上在苏州看到索伯恩仍在中国军方手中的人。

排除枪击嫌疑
Blackburn 先生个人认为这名少年在苏州，而中国当局出于某种原因故意隐瞒他的下落。
起初人们认为索伯恩以某种方式

英国方面掌握
索伯恩案新证据

（续第1版第3栏）
与铁路上发生的奇怪枪战有关，在那次事件中，两名中国宪兵受重伤并随后因此死亡。这一事件发生在6月2日晚，即索伯恩从上海家中失踪的第二天。

索伯恩被免除指控
然而，苏州地区两个宪兵分队的指挥官告知 Scott 先生，该案中没有外国人参与，其手下是被匪徒打伤的。驻沪英国当局知道索伯恩配备有一支 .45 口径的上海万国商团左轮手枪，起初担心这名青年因涉及枪击案而被捕，并由中方自行处理。中国军官的声明使索伯恩摆脱了这一特别严重的局面，现在使得该青年的领事当局能够在不受干扰的情况下，无论其生死，更清晰地开展寻回工作。

热爱户外生活
年轻的索伯恩是一个安静的少年，热衷于各种户外运动和一般的生活。冬季月份里他是一名热情的曲棍球运动员，夏季则习惯将大部分时间花在打网球或在河上活动。他是一名海童军，也是德莱斯代尔业余戏剧俱乐部（Drysdale Amateur Dramatic Club）的活跃成员。1928年，当时17岁的索伯恩开始认真训练，准备随英国队参加国际竞走比赛。经过两周的艰苦训练，他被迫放弃了参赛的念头，因为他的双腿支撑不住了。索伯恩是一个充满“干劲”的少年，在当地年轻人群体中非常受欢迎。

据称这名失踪青年在失踪前一天曾计划参加前往赫菲尔（Hephil，音译）的划船聚会。然而，他并没有去，而是在上海度过了一天，下午在跑马厅打网球，当晚回到父亲家睡觉。第二天他留下一张纸条给父亲，仅说他要去乡下，随后便离开了。

（批：登记处。请归档 1931年6月16日。）

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, TUESDAY, JUNE 16, 1931

NO LIGHT ON THOR-
BURN MYSTERY
Vice-Consul Scott Fails
To Return From
Soochow

Officially, there have been no
new developments in what has come
to be known as the "Thorburn
Mystery," which concerns the dis-
appearance on the night of May
31—June 1 of 18-year-old John
Thorburn, of 316, Rue Bourgeat,
who left his home for an uncertain
destination and has not been heard
of since.

Some light on the mystery was
expected yesterday with the return
to Shanghai from Soochow of Mr.
A. L. Scott, British Vice-Consul,
who went to Soochow early last
week in an effort to discover any-
thing which might lead to the
solution of the mystery. The miss-
ing youth is a British subject.

Inquiries made yesterday found
Mr. Scott still at Soochow and his
postponed return might possibly be
attributed to his having discovered
something new in connection with
the case, as he was expected to
return last Saturday.

One of the most important
developments in the case has been
the denial by Chinese military
authorities that the Quinsan shoot-
ing incident of nearly two weeks
ago, in which three Chinese gen-
darmes lost their lives, in any way
concerned foreigners. It was fear-
ed that Thorburn had, in some way
become embroiled in an argument
with Chinese soldiers and had made
use of a pistol he is alleged to have
taken away with him on May 31.

However, the Chinese declare not
only that no foreigner was mixed
up in that affair but also that they
have no foreigner in custody at the
present time, this notwithstanding
considerable evidence to the con-
trary collected at Soochow, Quin-
san and other points in that
vicinity.

（批：12/7 16/4）
page_data.zh:
1075

《上海泰晤士报》，1931年6月16日，星期二

索伯恩谜团
暂无头绪
副领事 Scott
未能从苏州返回

官方方面，在被称作“索伯恩谜团”的事件中没有任何新进展，该事件涉及居住在布尔热路316号的18岁青年约翰·索伯恩于5月31日至6月1日晚间失踪，他离家前往一个不确定的目的地，此后杳无音信。

人们原本期望昨天随着英国副领事 A. L. Scott 先生从苏州返回上海，谜团能有所澄清。Scott 先生上周初前往苏州，试图发现任何可能有助于解开谜团的线索。这名失踪青年是英国臣民。

昨日的查询发现 Scott 先生仍在苏州，他推迟返回可能归因于他发现了与案件有关的新情况，因为他原定上周六返回。

此案最重要的进展之一是中国军方否认近两周前发生在昆山的枪击事件（三名中国宪兵丧生）与外国人有任何关联。此前曾担心索伯恩以某种方式卷入与中国士兵的争执，并使用了据称他于5月31日带走的手枪。

然而，中方不仅声明没有外国人卷入该事件，还声明目前并未拘留任何外国人，尽管在苏州、昆山及周边其他地点收集了大量相反的证据。

（批：12/7 16/4）

1076
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Monday, June 15, 1931

Mystery Deepens
In Thorburn Case

Young Britisher Lost
In Uplands May
Be Dead

Is young John Thorburn, British subject, dead or alive and is he, if alive, being detained by the Soochow authorities?

These questions today are puzzling the local British authorities as the investigation into the whereabouts of the young man, ordered by Sir Miles Lampson, British Minister to China, continues at Soochow and Quinsan.

Of the following the British consulate general here is almost certain:

Left Home May 31

Thorburn, who is 19 years of age, left his home here on May 31, leaving a note in which he informed his father that he was "going up-country."

Thorburn was armed, carrying a loaded pistol and was wearing attire of the machine gun company, Shanghai Volunteer Corps, of which he is a member, but which would be better suited for dress parade.

Seen In Custody

On June 2, according to definite information received by the British consulate general from disinterested witnesses, the young man was seen in the custody of the gendarmerie near Quinsan.

The British authorities here, according to Mr. A. D. Blackburn, superintending consul, have reason to believe that Thorburn was seized by the gendarmerie in connection with the shooting of two soldiers on the railway line near Quinsan on the night of June 1.

Taken To Soochow

The consulate general also has reason to believe that the youth was taken to Soochow, where the headquarters of the gendarmerie are located, and that he either is dead or is badly injured and is being held by the gendarmerie.

After the strange disappearance of the youth had been reported to the consulate general and reported in turn to the British Minister, Mr. A. L. Scott, vice-consul of the Chinese Affairs Department was sent to Soochow and Quinsan to conduct an investigation. At Quinsan Mr. Scott, who still is at Soochow, ascertained from a responsible person that the young man had been seen in the custody of the gendarmerie.

Chinese Denials

Since that time the Chinese authorities at both Quinsan and Soochow stoutly have denied that Thorburn had been or is in custody, or that any foreigner had been connected with the fatal shooting of the two soldiers.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1931年6月15日，星期一

索恩伯恩案谜团加深

在“上乡”失踪的英国青年可能已死亡

年仅19岁的英国臣民约翰·索恩伯恩（John Thorburn）是生是死？如果还活着，他是否正被苏州当局拘留？

随着英国驻华公使蓝普森爵士（Sir Miles Lampson）下令对这名青年下落进行的调查在苏州和昆山继续进行，这些问题今天令当地英国当局感到困惑。

对于以下情况，驻沪英国总领事馆几乎可以确定：

5月31日离家

现年19岁的索恩伯恩于5月31日离开其在上海的住所，留下一张便条，告知其父他正“前往内地（up-country）”。

索恩伯恩携带武器，随身带着一把装有子弹的手枪，身穿上海义勇军（Shanghai Volunteer Corps）机枪连的制服；他是该连成员，但这套制服更适合用于礼仪阅兵。

被目击处于拘押中

根据驻沪英国总领事馆从无关利害关系的证人处收到的确切消息，6月2日，有人看见这名青年在昆山附近被宪兵拘押。

据监理领事A. D. 布莱克本（A. D. Blackburn）先生称，这里的英国当局有理由相信，索恩伯恩是因为6月1日晚在昆山附近铁路上两名士兵遭枪击一案而被宪兵逮捕的。

被带往苏州

总领事馆也有理由相信，这名青年已被带往苏州，那里是宪兵司令部所在地；他要么已经死亡，要么身受重伤，正被宪兵扣留。

在这名青年离奇失踪的消息上报至总领事馆并转报英国公使后，华务处副领事A. L. 斯科特（A. L. Scott）先生被派往苏州和昆山进行调查。在昆山，目前仍在苏州的斯科特先生从一位负责人处获悉，曾有人看见这名青年处于宪兵的拘押之下。

中方否认

此后，昆山和苏州的中国当局坚决否认索恩伯恩曾经或正在被拘押，也否认有任何外国人参与了两名士兵被 fatal shooting（致命枪击）的案件。

C. & S. B. REGISTRY

15.6.31

June 15, 1931. Morning Translation

MISCELLANEOUS

some desperadoes suddenly opened fire on them and consequently two policemen were wounded. While the remaining police were in pursuit of the desperadoes, an express train passed and separated the police and the desperadoes, who, availing themselves of the opportunity, made good their escape. The police made a thorough search but made no arrests. These are the true facts of the case. The information published by various newspapers is mostly untrue; moreover the report of the arrest of a foreigner is entirely groundless and it has incurred suspicion on the part of foreigners. For fear that the truth may still not be known to the public, we hereby request that a correction be published".

An English Youth Missing.
The China Times publishes the following report:-
A local English youth named Thorburn, age 18, residing at No. 315 Rue Bourgeat, has been missing since June 1 and so far his whereabouts are not known. On the day previous to his being reported missing, Thorburn planned to proceed to Kenli, but later he abandoned the idea and went to the Race Course to play tennis. In the evening he returned home and went to bed. According to public opinion, he proceeded to Quinsan by train on the night of June 1, thence planned to walk to Kenli. He has not been seen since June 2, and on the night of June 2 the case of the shooting of two military policemen by a foreigner at Tsaiting Railway Station took place. According to press reports, the guilty man was a Russian, but it was suspected that it might be Thorburn. Officials of the local British Consulate-General stated that the Station Master at Quinsan had seen a foreign youth arrested and detained by the military police and that his attire quite resembled that of Thorburn. In consequence the British Vice-Consul Mr. Scott went to Soochow, but enquiries made at the Military Police Headquarters revealed that no foreigner was concerned in the affair which took place on the night of June 2 and that no foreigner had been arrested and detained. Therefore the real facts of the case are not known for the time being and enquiries are being continued.

1931年6月15日。晨间译件

杂项

几名歹徒突然向他们开火，导致两名警察受伤。其余警察在追击歹徒时，一列快车驶过，将警察与歹徒隔开，歹徒趁机逃脱。警方进行了彻底搜查，但未抓获任何人。以上是本案的真实情况。各报纸刊登的消息大多不实；此外，关于逮捕一名外国人的报道完全毫无根据，并已引起外国人的怀疑。唯恐公众仍不知晓真相，特此请求刊登更正。”

一名英国青年失踪。
《字林西报》刊登如下报道：
一名居住于蒲石路315号、名为索恩伯恩的本地英国青年，现年18岁，自6月1日起失踪，至今下落不明。在报告失踪的前一天，索恩伯恩原计划前往肯利（Kenli），但后来放弃了这个念头，去跑马厅打网球。晚上他回家就寝。据舆论称，他于6月1日晚乘火车前往昆山，随后计划步行前往肯利。自6月2日以来无人见过他，而6月2日晚发生了在蔡亭（Tsaiting）火车站一名外国人枪击两名军警的案件。据新闻报道，凶手是一名俄国人，但有人怀疑可能是索恩伯恩。当地英国总领事馆官员表示，昆山站长曾看见一名外国青年被军警逮捕并拘留，其衣着与索恩伯恩非常相似。因此，英国副领事斯科特先生前往苏州，但在军警司令部的查询显示，6月2日晚发生的事件中没有外国人牵涉其中，也没有外国人被逮捕和拘留。因此，案件的真实事实目前尚不清楚，调查仍在继续。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, MONDAY, JUNE 15, 1931

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE C. & C. R. REGISTRY B. D. 2464 15 - 6 - 31）

MYSTERY STILL DEEPER
No Further News of Mr. John Thorburn
QUINSAN INQUIRIES
How the Soldiers Were Shot
SPECIAL TO THE N.C.D.N.

“No foreigner was involved at all in the shooting affair which occurred near Weiting Station on the night of June 1 when two gendarmes were fatally wounded,” said Col. Tsing Tsung-ying, Commissioner of Public Safety, at Quinsan, when interviewed yesterday by a representative of the “North-China Daily News” who paid a special visit to that place to make inquiries into the disappearance of Mr. John Thorburn, a 19-year old British subject, who has been reported missing for nearly two weeks.

Asked whether he had received any reports of foreigners being found dead or wandering about in the vicinity of Quinsan, or whether any foreigner had been arrested, Col. Tsing emphatically stated that he had received no reports to this effect and that no foreigner had been arrested. Had any such discoveries been made, he certainly would have been informed and he would have telegraphed at once to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs because he had received orders from the Waichiaopu and the Kiangsu Provincial Government to submit, without delay a report if any missing foreigner were found because he understood that the Waichiaopu had received an inquiry from the British authorities concerning the whereabouts of Mr. Thorburn.

A Futile Search
One of the purposes of the ‘North-China Daily News” representative in pursuing the inquiry was to find a certain English message. It is reported to have been written on the platform of the Quinsan Station. No such message was found, though every nook and corner of the station and points within a large radius of the station were carefully searched.

Accordingly, the investigator went to the headquarters of the First Battalion of the First Regiment of the Railway Zone Gendarmerie, to which the dead soldier belonged, and interviewed the officer in charge. This officer stated that he had read a report of the shooting affair which appeared in the Chinese press (a translation of which subsequently appeared in this journal) but it was incorrect in many respects. In the first place, only three soldiers were involved in the affair. In the second place, no foreigner was involved and no foreigner was arrested, though the report stated that a Russian had fired the shots and that he had been taken into custody.

Chinese in Long Gowns
“I personally interviewed the wounded soldiers before they were brought to Shanghai, where they later died on June 7 and 12 respectively, and took their statements. Both these men, together with the third soldier who was in their company, stated that the shooting was done by a Chinese who wore a long gown: there were eight or nine in all. The soldier who is still alive is absolutely sure of this fact that he is equally certain that it was not a foreigner who fired the shots,” the officer told the “North-China Daily News.”

“The three gendarmes started out from Quinsan to patrol the railway zone and reached a spot about three or four li to the east of Weiting Station when the shooting occurred on the night of June 1. As soon as they noticed the eight or nine men wearing long gowns, they felt sure that they were tufei, (bandits) so they called upon them to halt and submit to search. Instead of doing so, one of the gang drew a pistol and opened fire, bringing down two of the gendarmes.

Swallowed Up in Darkness
The man started to chase them but it so happened that the Nanking night express was passing at full speed and the gangsters had crossed the line before the train arrived. When the train had passed, the soldier searched for the gang but found that all of them had disappeared in a most mysterious manner in the darkness. Accordingly, no arrests were made.”

This statement was confirmed by Col. Tsing, the Commissioner of Public Safety, and the gendarme who gave chase.

（手写批注：15/6）

谜团更加深重
约翰·索恩伯恩先生再无音讯
昆山调查
士兵如何遭枪击
《字林西报》专讯

“6月1日晚在唯亭站附近发生的导致两名宪兵受致命伤的枪击事件中，完全没有外国人卷入，”昆山公安局长程宗英（Tsing Tsung-ying，音译）上校昨日在接受《字林西报》特派记者采访时说道。该记者专程前往该地，调查已失踪近两周的19岁英国臣民约翰·索恩伯恩先生的下落。

当被问及是否收到有关在昆山附近发现外国人尸体或外国人游荡的报告，或者是否有外国人被捕时，程上校 emphatically（坚决）表示，他未收到此类报告，也没有外国人被捕。如果有此类发现，他肯定会被告知，并且会立即致电外交部，因为他已接到外交部和江苏省政府的命令，如果发现任何失踪的外国人，须立即提交报告，因为他了解到外交部已收到英国当局关于索恩伯恩先生下落的查询。

徒劳的搜寻
《字林西报》记者进行调查的目的之一是寻找据称写在昆山站台上的某条英文信息。尽管对车站的每个角落以及车站周围很大半径范围内的地点进行了仔细搜索，但并未发现此类信息。

随后，调查人员前往死者所属的铁路区宪兵第一团第一营司令部，并采访了负责军官。该军官表示，他已阅读中文报刊上刊登的关于枪击事件的报道（该报道的译文随后刊登在本报），但报道在许多方面是不正确的。首先，卷入事件的只有三名士兵。其次，没有外国人卷入，也没有外国人被捕，尽管报道称是一名俄国人开枪并被拘留。

身穿长衫的中国人

“我在受伤士兵被送往上海之前亲自采访了她们并记录了他们的供词，他们后来分别于6月7日和12日在上海去世。这两名士兵以及与他们同行的第三名士兵均陈述，开枪者是一名身穿长衫的中国人：总共约有八九人。那名幸存的士兵绝对确信这一事实，他也同样确信开枪的不是外国人，”该军官告诉《字林西报》。

“这三名宪兵从昆山出发巡逻铁路区，在6月1日晚到达唯亭站以东约三四里处时发生了枪击事件。当他们注意到那八九名身穿长衫的人时，确信他们是土匪（tufei），于是喝令他们停下接受搜查。但他们非但没有照做，团伙中的一人反而拔出手枪开火，击中了两名宪兵。

消失在黑暗中

那人开始追赶他们，但碰巧南京夜班车全速通过，歹徒们在火车到达前已穿过铁轨。火车通过后，这名士兵搜寻该团伙，发现所有人都神秘地消失在黑暗中。因此，未能实施逮捕。”

这一说法得到了公安局长程上校和参与追击的宪兵的证实。

（手写批注：15/6）

THE CHINA PRESS, SUNDAY, JUNE 14, 1931

Rail Man Says Thorburn
Seen In Hands Of Police

British Consular Officials Continue To Look Into
Possibility That Lost Youth Is In Custody
Of Soochow Gendarmerie

Until a late hour last night the actual whereabouts of Mr. John Thorburn, 19 year old Briton who mysteriously disappeared from June 1 from his father's house, 315 Rue Bourgeat, and has since not been seen, could not be discovered. British consular authorities here, however, continue to work on the theory that the youth is in the custody of Chinese military in Soochow, though the latter have disclaimed the rumor that they have a foreigner in their hands.

Mr. A. L. Scott, British vice-consul in charge of Chinese affairs, is still in Soochow investigating the truth of the report about the foreigner in custody. His investigations, according to Mr. A. D. Blackburn, assistant consul-General of the local British Consul-General in Shanghai, are becoming more and more in the direction that the rumor is true and that the foreigner in the hands of the Chinese officials is actually Thorburn.

Young Thorburn, it will be recalled, was supposed to have joined a boating party at Henli on the day previous to his disappearance, but instead of so doing, he stayed in Shanghai playing tennis on the Race Course during the afternoon and returning to his home to sleep that night. It is the general belief that Thorburn caught a late train for Quinsan, intending to walk the short distance from that station to Henli, on the following night. He was not seen at all during June 2 by friends in Shanghai.

Thorburn's disappearance was at first believed to have been connected with the strange shooting affray which occurred at a point near the Quinsan Station on the night of June 2. Four Chinese soldiers were doing patrolling duty on the railroad line when a man, whom they believed to have been a foreigner, suddenly appeared before them. When this man was ordered to halt he, it is claimed, pulled out a revolver and opened fire mortally wounding two of the soldiers, Shen Iah-seng and Leo Kuo-tsai, both of whom have since died, before making a getaway. The wounded men were brought to Shanghai and conveyed to St. Luke's Hospital where they passed away.

Arrested Foreigner Seen

According to the British Consular authorities here, the station master at Quinsan has acknowledged having seen a foreign youth, dressed as a Sea Scout, in the custody of Chinese military.

The station master's description of the foreigner corresponds with young Thorburn. The missing youth was a keen Sea Scout and it is quite likely that he was in uniform for he presumably was on his way to join a boating party.

Department Not Cleared

Mr. Blackburn informed a representative of The China Press yesterday afternoon that the British Consulate here had received word from Mr. Scott to the effect that the Chinese military officials in Soochow have informed him that there had been no foreigners involved with the shooting affray on the railroad lines on the night of June 2. This is a very important factor in the case as it clears young Thorburn of a particularly nasty predicament.

1067
《字林西报》，1931年6月14日，星期日

铁路职员称索伯恩
被警方控制

英国领事官员继续调查
失踪青年可能被苏州宪兵队羁押的可能性

直到昨晚深夜，仍无法查明19岁的英国青年约翰·索伯恩（John Thorburn）的实际下落。他于6月1日从位于蒲石路315号（Rue Bourgeat）的父亲家中神秘失踪，此后一直未见踪影。然而，驻沪英国领事当局继续依据该青年被中国军方羁押在苏州的说法开展工作，尽管中方已否认有关其扣押了一名外国人的谣言。

负责中国事务的英国副领事A. L. 斯科特先生（Mr. A. L. Scott）仍在苏州调查有关外国人被拘押报道的真实性。据上海英国总领事馆助理副总领事A. D. 布莱克本先生（Mr. A. D. Blackburn）称，他的调查越来越指向该谣言属实，且在中国官员手中的外国人实际上就是索伯恩。

回想起来，年轻的索伯恩原定于失踪前一天参加在亨力（Henli）举行的划船聚会，但他并未前往，而是下午在上海跑马厅打网球，当晚回家睡觉。普遍的看法是，索伯恩在次日晚上搭乘了前往昆山的晚班火车，打算从该车站步行短距离前往亨力。6月2日全天，他在上海的朋友均未见到他。

起初，人们认为索伯恩的失踪与6月2日晚发生在昆山车站附近的一起奇怪枪击事件有关。四名中国士兵正在铁路线上执行巡逻任务时，一名他们认为是外国人的男子突然出现在他们面前。据称，当这名男子被命令停下时，他拔出手枪开火，致使两名士兵沈雅生（Shen Iah-seng）和郭才（Leo Kuo-tsai）受重伤，两人随后均死亡，之后该男子逃逸。伤者被送往上海，转入圣路加医院（St. Luke's Hospital），并在那里去世。

目击被捕的外国人

据驻沪英国领事当局称，昆山站长承认曾看到一名身穿海上童子军制服的外国青年被中国军方羁押。

站长对该外国人的描述与年轻的索伯恩相符。这位失踪的青年是一名热衷的海上童子军成员，他很可能是穿着制服，因为他推测正前往参加划船聚会。

部门未获澄清

布莱克本先生昨天下午告知《字林西报》记者，驻沪英国领事馆收到斯科特先生的消息，称苏州的中国军方官员已向他通报，6月2日晚铁路线上的枪击事件中没有外国人卷入。这是本案的一个非常重要的因素，因为它洗清了年轻索伯恩的一项特别恶劣的嫌疑。

1066
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury. Saturday, June 13, 1931

Thorburn Mystery
Inquiry Launched

Disappearance Of Local
Youth Linked With
Shooting Affray

Official inquiry into the mysterious disappearance on June 1 of Mr. John Thorburn, 19 year old British employee of Dodge & Seymour, Ltd., and the strange shooting affair on the night of June 2 between Quinsan and Welting on the Shanghai-Nanking Railway has been in progress for several days British consular authorities have revealed today.

Mr. A. L. Scott, British vice-consul has visited Soochow twice during the past few days in an effort to clear up the mystery of Mr Thorburn's disappearance, which has been linked with the shooting Military and civil authorities, however, deny having arrested a foreigner in connection with the Quinsan affair.

Two Soldiers Killed

The shooting, which resulted in the death of two Chinese soldiers stationed at Quinsan took place after dusk, according to testimony introduced at the inquest here this morning over Shen Lin-seng, one of the dead soldiers. He and three others were patrolling the road between Quinsan when a foreigner appeared, who, when ordered to halt, is said to have opened fire. Shen and a comrade named Lee Kuo-tsai were mortally wounded The former died last week while Shen passed away yesterday at the St. Luke's Hospital here.

Reports received from Soochow after the shooting stated that a foreigner had been arrested and the British consular officials immediately took steps to investigate. The foreigner, the reports stated, was either Russian or British.

Bullet Stamped "O38"

At the inquest over Shen Lin-seng today, a verdict of death due to bullet wounds was returned by Procurator Quo, acting as coroner. The only clue that might lead to the identity of the man believed responsible for the shooting was a bullet taken from the body of the dead man, bearing the stamp "O38".

《上海泰晤士报及信使报》，1931年6月13日，星期六

索伯恩谜案
展开调查

本地青年失踪
与枪击事件有关联

英国领事当局今日透露，针对道奇与西摩有限公司（Dodge & Seymour, Ltd.）19岁英国雇员约翰·索伯恩先生于6月1日神秘失踪一事，以及6月2日晚在京沪铁路昆山与唯亭（Welting）之间发生的奇怪枪击事件的官方调查，已进行数日。

英国副领事A. L. 斯科特先生在过去几天里两次访问苏州，试图厘清索伯恩先生失踪之谜，该失踪案已与枪击事件联系起来。然而，军方和民政当局否认因昆山事件逮捕过任何外国人。

两名士兵身亡

据今天上午在此间对死者之一沈林生（Shen Lin-seng）举行的验尸听证会上提出的证词，导致驻扎在昆山的两名中国士兵死亡的枪击事件发生在黄昏之后。当时他和另外三人正在昆山之间的道路上巡逻，一名外国人出现，据称在被命令停下时开了火。沈林生和一名名叫李国才（Lee Kuo-tsai）的同伴受重伤。前者于上周去世，沈林生于昨天在本地的圣路加医院去世。

枪击发生后从苏州收到的报告称，一名外国人已被逮捕，英国领事官员立即采取措施进行调查。报告称，该外国人要么是俄国人，要么是英国人。

子弹印有“O38”字样

在今天对沈林生的验尸听证会上，担任验尸官的检察官郭氏裁定死因为枪伤。可能导致认定涉嫌对枪击负责者身份的唯一线索，是从死者体内取出的一颗子弹，上面印有“O38”字样。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, JUNE 13, 1931.

THORBURN MYSTERY
GROWS DEEPER

Soochow Witnesses Say
They Saw Foreigner
Arrested

SILENCE MAINTAINED
BY MILITARY

A conspiracy of silence appears
to have been adopted by Chinese
military officials at Soochow over
the disappearance of John Thor-
burn (20), British youth residing
with his father Mr. W. J. Hay
Thorburn, of 815 Rue Bourgeat,
who left his home on June 1 under
somewhat unusual circumstances
and has not returned since.

“The Shanghai Times” inquiries
started several days ago following
receipt of information to the effect
that a youth answering to the de-
scription of Thorburn had been
seen in custody of Chinese soldiers
at Soochow, far from being dis-
proved by recent investigations
point more strongly, in fact, to
the correctness of the original re-
port.

In support of this, Mr. A. L.
Jones, British Vice-Consul, has
been in Soochow since Tuesday,
June 9, investigating similar re-
ports and is still at Soochow it
was learned yesterday.

Thorburn, investigation shows,
left his home at Rue Bourgeat on
June 1 without giving any in-
formation as to his intended move-
ments. Nothing was heard of or
from him for several days, al-
though the police had been notified
of his prolonged absence.

Some indication of where to look
for him was received from a report
to the effect that a young foreign-
er had been seen walking along
the railway track between Shang-
hai and Nanking, in the direction
of the latter place.

This report, emanating from
reliable sources, endeavoured, by
direct and circumstantial
evidence, to link up the missing
youth with a peculiar shooting in-
cident which occurred near Quin-
san when four Chinese gendarm-
es were fired upon by a foreigner
when an attempt was made by
them to search and detain him.
One of the gendarmes died shortly
afterwards. The others who were
wounded were transferred to St.
Luke’s hospital, Shanghai. One of
them died of his wound a day or
two after arrival. The other died
on Thursday evening.

Nanking Also Silent

Whether or not there is any con-
nection between Thorburn’s dis-
appearance and the shooting in-
cident is immaterial beside the
question of Thorburn’s where-
abouts at the present time. Also,
that Thorburn is alleged to have
taken a pistol, an S.V.C. weapon,
away with him when he left home
on June 1, is also a secondary
point for consideration pending
discovery of the youth himself.

The father of the missing youth
is understood to have paid a per-
sonal visit to Nanking to consult
the military authorities to see if

《上海泰晤士报》，1931年6月13日，星期六。

索伯恩谜案
愈发深奥

苏州证人称
目睹外国人
被捕

军方
保持沉默

中国军方官员在苏州似乎对居住在蒲石路815号的W. J. Hay Thorburn之子、20岁的英国青年约翰·索伯恩（John Thorburn）的失踪采取了一种沉默共谋的态度。索伯恩于6月1日在有些不同寻常的情况下离家，此后未归。

《上海泰晤士报》的调查始于数日前，当时收到消息称，在苏州看到一名符合索伯恩特征的青年被中国士兵羁押。最近的调查非但没有驳斥这一说法，事实上反而更有力地指向最初报道的正确性。

为此，英国副领事A. L. 琼斯先生（Mr. A. L. Jones）自6月9日星期二以来一直在苏州调查类似报告，据悉昨日他仍在苏州。

调查显示，索伯恩于6月1日离开蒲石路的住所，未提供任何关于其预期行动的信息。尽管警方已获悉其长期缺席，但数日内没有任何关于他的消息或来自他的音讯。

一份报告提供了一些寻找他的线索，该报告称有人看到一名年轻外国人沿着上海至南京的铁路线朝南京方向行走。

这份来自可靠渠道的报告试图通过直接和间接证据，将这名失踪青年与昆山附近发生的一起奇特枪击事件联系起来。当时，四名中国宪兵试图搜查并扣留一名外国人时，遭到该外国人射击。其中一名宪兵不久后死亡。其他受伤者被转移至上海圣路加医院。其中一人在抵达后一两天内因伤死亡。另一人于周四晚上死亡。

南京方面也保持沉默

索伯恩的失踪与枪击事件之间是否存在联系，在目前索伯恩下落的问题面前并不重要。此外，据称索伯恩在6月1日离家时带走了一把S.V.C.手枪，这也是一个次要考虑点，有待发现该青年本人后再行考量。

据悉，失踪青年的父亲已亲自前往南京，咨询军方当局，看看

Likewise, Soochow military

Independent inquiry has reveal-

Foreigner Seen
In the first place, there is in-
disputable evidence that a foreign-

streets of Soochow last week in
the custody of Chinese gendarmes.
Careful questioning at Soochow
has also revealed that the foreign-
er seen marching off in the direc-
tion of military headquarters was
wearing a pair of trousers of an
unusual type which answer the de-
scription of a pair belonging to
young Thorburn which are missing
from the wardrobe.
Furthermore, in support of the
evidence of the arrest of a foreign-
er by Chinese gendarmes at about
the time in question, there is the
statement by someone travelling
by train from Quinsan to Soochow
that a foreigner was removed from
the train by Chinese gendarmes at
Soochow.

Shooting of Railway Police by Foreigner

The Shun Pao publishes the following correspondence from Soochow : -

In connection with the recent killing of one and wounding of two of a group of military police while patrolling the railway line between Quinsan and Tsing Neo and the subsequent arrest and detention of a foreigner in the Military Police Headquarters at Soochow, Mr. "Sa Ko To" ( Scott ) the British Vice-Consul in Shanghai, yesterday (June 9) went to Soochow and enquired of the Hsien Government whether the arrested person was a British subject or not, as an Englishman named "Wei Lin Tai Ba" ( ), age 19, was missing from Shanghai. He was informed by Magistrate Wong that he was awaiting instructions from the Military Police Headquarters. Magistrate Wong promised to notify Mr. "Sa Ko To" as soon as instructions were received. The British Vice-Consul returned to Shanghai the same night.

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, THURSDAY, JUNE 4, 1931

ALLEGED CRIME
BY FOREIGNER

Shooting Affair on the
Nanking Railway

HELD BY MILITARY
AUTHORITIES

A foreigner, stated to be of
Russian nationality, was arrested by
Chinese soldiers on the Shanghai-
Nanking Railway, between Quinsan
and Weiting stations, on Tuesday
morning on a charge of being con-
cerned in the murder of two Chinese
gendarmes in the vicinity of Weiting
Station on the previous night. The
foreigner, who was found in pos-
session of two pistols, is being
detained by the Quinsan military
authorities pending investigations.

According to a statement made by
the military authorities to the Chin-
ese press, the two gendarmes who
are alleged to have been murdered
by the foreigner were detailed
with 14 others, to Quinsan on patrol
duty between that station and Wei-
ting. Four left the train at Weiting
to patrol the railway zone. At about
10 p.m., when these four men reach-
ed a spot about a mile from Wei-
ting, they noticed a tall man walking
along the track. They shouted to
him and called upon him to stop and
submit to search. The man is said
to have obeyed and raised his arms
but, when two of the gendarmes ap-
proached him, they noticed that he
was a foreigner. As they attempted
to search him, the man, who is said
to have held a pistol in his hand,
suddenly opened fire on them badly
injuring them. The other two
soldiers, who had remained stand-
ing some distance away, ran up to
investigate but the foreigner escaped
in the darkness.

Foreigner Arrested

A search was made but, as the
foreigner could not be found, the
wounded men were taken to the
Weiting Station and brought to
Shanghai but they died after being
admitted to hospital here.

On Tuesday morning, says the
report, soldiers stationed on the
railway arrested a suspicious-look-
ing foreigner between Weiting and
Quinsan and found him in possession
of two pistols. He was questioned
as to the shooting on the previous
night but denied all knowledge of
it. He was taken to Quinsan where
he is still being detained pending
investigations.

《字林西报》，1931年6月4日，星期四

涉嫌犯罪
外籍人士

京沪铁路枪击案

由军方羁押

据称一名俄国籍外籍人士，于周二上午在京沪铁路昆山站与唯亭站之间被中国士兵逮捕，罪名是涉嫌在前一晚于唯亭站附近谋杀两名中国宪兵。该外籍人士被发现持有两支手枪，目前正由昆山军方当局拘留，以待调查。

据军方当局向中文报刊发表的声明称，据称被该外籍人士谋杀的两名宪兵，曾与其他14人一同被派往昆山，执行该站与唯亭之间的巡逻任务。其中四人在唯亭下车，巡逻铁路区域。晚上10点左右，当这四名人员到达距唯亭约一英里处时，他们注意到有一名高个子男子沿铁轨行走。他们向其喊话，要求其停下并接受搜查。据说该男子服从并举起双手，但当两名宪兵靠近他时，发现他是一名外籍人士。当他们试图搜查他时，据说手中持有一支手枪的男子突然向他们开火，致其重伤。另外两名士兵原本站在稍远处，见状跑上前去查看，但该外籍人士已在黑暗中逃脱。

外籍人士被捕

当局进行了搜寻，但因未能找到该外籍人士，受伤人员被送往唯亭站，随后转至上海，但在入院后死亡。

报道称，周二上午，驻守铁路的士兵在唯亭与昆山之间逮捕了一名形迹可疑的外籍人士，并发现其持有两支手枪。他就前晚的枪击事件接受了讯问，但否认知情。他被带往昆山，目前仍被拘留，以待调查。

’ Le Journal de Shanghai. 
dated July 30, I93I. 


Our contemporary The North Chin a Daily News 
published yesterday once again details in connection 
with the case of Thorburn. The young Englishman was seen 
in Soochow on June IO by a witness at about dusk. He was 
in a pitiful state, wounded, covered with blood, and his 
hands tied at the back, pushed by soldiers who appeared 
to be conducting him to a place @rom which there is no return. 

(Here follows an extract on the subject from the "North China 
Daily News" ). 
Despite the negative result of an enquiry conduceted 
scam « Py Nanking Government nobody doubts any longer that 
young Thorburn had been arrested by the- soldiers of 
Soochow garrison, was tortured by them and very possibly 
executed under circumstances which we are ignorant of 
but which it would be interesting to know. ! 

We think that the officials of Waichiaopu are pewsons 
of too much intelligence to believe that the report of 
the enquiry commission appointed by the Ministry of Fortign 
affairs and the War Ministry, is correct. It is probable 
that upon learning of the extution of Thorburn by the 
soldiers, the enquiry commission decided to toray a thick 
veil om,the whole of this affair in order to hide from the 
world the real situation in China, which official representatives 
of Nanking Government abroad describe as a country where 
law is respected, where good order prevails, and where 
extraterritoriality is to all appearances an anomaly.. 

Leaders of the Anglo-Saxon nations have since many 
months now been conducting negotiations on the subject of 
extraterritoriality. In obedience to certain reasons 
of opportunism which we shall refrain from discussing, or 
in support of certain influences, which we shall not comment 
upon or pass judgment on, they were phowing a spirit of 
acccommodating conciliation to a great extent, Never before 
were there so many missionaries and foreigners arrested, 
carried away or massacred in Chine as within the past 
two three years, nevertheless the ren&noiation to special 
foreign rights in interior provinces, that is to say, 
logically, where the situation is practically the same 
to-dey as when these rights were granted, continued to 
be discussed. It would seem as if one was fascinated 
by Nanking, where the Government had assembled numerous 
intelligent and educated officials and established a 
modern administration. What dea@g it matter that a few 
hours uway from Nanking the situationwés quite different, 
the capital alone mattered together wi- th the distinguished 
men who were preparing a future there. The discussions 
were inclined to treat thenfuture as“reality. 

When news was received that in Hounan, Kiangsi, Hupeh 
and Nganhoei, bandits and communists had been arresting 
or killing missionaries, it was sufficient to deplore these 
sad incidents. : 

The case of Thorburn, by its reflections abroad, has 
beought about the effect of a thunderbolt. The veil which 
conce™aed the truth has’ been thorn apart. It is only 40 
kiplometres from Shanghai that the military authorities 


a 


violated international conventions and ignored the 
authority of the Nanking Government. Furthermore, 
this same Government, which, we are certain, is the 
first to deplore the excesses of the Soochow garrison 
soldiers, did not, however dare to deal vigorously 
with the guilty military and attempted to pass the affair 
by in silence, thinking that the foreign opinion would 
xet tired and would end tp by finding other interests. 
Bad reckoning; the truth has emerged in spite of everything. 

The result of all this is that the Anglo-Saxon 
countries are now talking of showing themselves less 
inolined to be conciliatory in the matter of extraterritoriality.; 
And really speaking, when one considers that the military 
are in a position to oppose the Gévernment, and to prevent 
the functioning ef a judicial body by intimidating witnesses, 
the question naturally arises what will be the fate of 
foreigners when the abolition of extraterritpgiality 
will have delivered them to the mercy of uncultured, 
brutal and unscrupulous soldiers.
